{np}A duke, is it? If his purse matches his title, there's coin to be had...{pp}A little rescue work might be just the thing.
How about it, Lanselot? What say you?
{np}Look. I'm sorry for not trusting you. It's true that if we're to rescue the duke, we're going to need help.
{np}Then there's nothing to be gained jabbering on here, neh? To Almorica Castle!

{np}Wait!
The castle is well defended.{pp}A fight there would mean our deaths―and yours, Lord Knight. And I...{pp}I've seen enough of fighting. Enough of death.

{np}What about you, {hero}?
Would you have our aid?

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} I would.
2. There is no need.
{np}Without your help, the duke is as good as dead.

{np}Then it's settled.
We will prepare at once.

{np}No. This is our fight.
I must decline your offer.

{np}What if I told you we make for Almorica too―not to aid you, but to fight for our own purpose.{pp}The arrow of the nobleman and the arrow of the hunter may find the same hare, though one shoots for sport and the other for his supper.{pp}What say we work together, while such cooperation is to our mutual benefit?
{np}Why not let 'em join us? I've a feeling they'll come whether we want it or not.
{np}Why do you not heed me, Brother?

{np}I know how you must feel, but what of my feelings? I don't want to lose you.{pp}Our father is dead―a hard truth, but a truth all the same.{pp}In all the world, you are the only one bound to me by blood, Brother. I couldn't bear to let you die.{pp}Forgive me. I know my words will not sway you. Only promise me...{pp}Promise you'll never leave your sister.

{np}What's keeping you?
Everyone's ready.
{np}You can't coddle him forever. He's no little boy anymore.
{np}Do not speak to me of my brother. He does not share your lust for blood.
{np}I have no love of war. But I'd sooner die on my feet than on my knees.
{np}You would die on the backs of others.
{np}You were the one who brought them in here, Catiua!
{np}Because when I find a tool well-suited for a job, I use it.{pp}At least one of us has the sense to recognize an opportunity. You should thank me!

{np}Feh. Is that how you see people? As tools?
I'd have expected more of a sibyl.
{np}I only want to see an end of death.
{np}{FF 9A 03}Lanselot and his allies have joined you as GUESTS.
{np}You're the rebels what been hiding out in Golyat. Here to save your duke, is it?{pp}There's two thousand goth on that one's head, boys! Half the purse to him what brings him down!
{np}A narrow stream scarce one pace across. Easily jumped, this. Watch.
{np}But look before, neh? You can only jump to ground of the same height or lower.
{np}Within your party, all units of the same class share a level.{pp}Even your newest recruit can step onto the battlefield and hold his own.

{np}When the battle's won, go to the Party Screen and press the {icon 4} button.{pp}This will toggle between the Unit List and Class List. The Class List is a handy way to see what level each class has reached.
{np}One of the winged, like me, moves with no heed of height or terrain.
{np}Even so, rushing in alone without someone to watch your back is asking for an early grave.
{np}You'll need a "classmark" in order to change a unit's class.{pp}Some classmarks can be found for sale in shops, but not all are to be had so easily.

{np}Probably goes without saying, but if you change a unit to a class you've been neglecting, more likely than not it will be level one.{pp}What's more, if you take on someone of a class you've never encountered, you'll have to work him up one level at a time.{pp}Best use caution. He'll make for easy pickings against a seasoned foe.

{np}When a unit's turn comes round, you can command it to {pal 16}Move{palreset}, {pal 16}Act{palreset}, or use {pal 16}Skills{palreset}.{pp}What's more, you can issue these commands in any order you see fit. Think on your choices well.
{np}The command to move can be canceled at any time.{pp}If you find a unit out of range for a planned attack, try moving it to a different location.
{np}Support skills are just that: skills that provide some passive benefit to the user.{pp}When I move, you'll notice yellow points of light near me on the ground.

{np}This is a support skill called {pal 16}Rampart Aura{palreset}.{pp}Any foes entering the range of the aura will be unable to move further until their next turn.{pp}Some support skills hinder the enemy's movement, while others might grant enhanced strength.{pp}Consider well your class and the lie of the battlefield when choosing which to use.

{np}Always keep a close watch on the action to see who will move next.{pp}Avoid unnecessary actions and keep speed on your side.{pp}The distance a unit moves and the actions it takes determine how long it must wait to move again.
{np}Press the {icon 4} button to display a list of all units in battle.{pp}You can {pal 16}Sort Units{palreset} by order of Attack Turn to quickly tell which unit will move next.
{np}Use common consumables such as mend leaf and magic leaf with the {pal 16}Inventory{palreset} command.{pp}Anyone can use these ordinary items; they're removed directly from your party's inventory.

{np}Use of more powerful consumables requires {pal 16}Field Alchemy{palreset}, a support skill.{pp}Different items require one of four Field Alchemy skill ranks.{pp}The Item List on the Party Screen indicates which items require which rank. Study well, lest you enter battle unprepared.
{np}All units begin battle with no MP, that being the font of all magical power.
{np}Units accumulate MP gradually over time.{pp}Powerful magic requires greater amounts of MP, so think ahead before casting a spell.
{np}Skills are divided into four broad categories: command, support, action, and special.

{np}A conjurer of magics such as myself must do more than learn a spell to wield it in battle.{pp}You must assign a unit the appropriate {pal 16}Command Skill{palreset} before he can use the spells he's learned.{pp}Assign skills to your units from the Party Screen. Be sure that you don't forget.

{np}One whisper of Ronwey's execution, and out you come, bold as you please.{pp}A rat can smell a trap, but not our rebels, eh?
High time we were rid of your lot.
{np}Wait...you're no Walisters! I know a man from Lodis when I see one!
{np}A trap. And we walked right into it.
{np}Trap or no, we fight or we die!{pp}I've never let a Galgastani get the better of me, and I don't mean to start today!

{np}Focus, Vyce!
Our first duty is to save the duke!

{np}Don't lecture me on duty!
Your only duty is to stay alive!

{np}You should not speak to {hero} so!
He was only trying to help!

{np}Are you all right, {hero}?
You shouldn't let Vyce get to you.

{np}I'm fine, Sister.
Back to the battle!
{np}Looks like our luck...has turned...

{np}{FF 9A 04}Experience points are not awarded to individual units. Instead, each class which participated in the battle receives a portion of the total. Only classes represented by the units who survive battle receive experience points.{pp}Skill points are handled in a similar fashion, with each surviving unit receiving an equal share of the total. Refer to the PLAY GUIDE in the Warren Report for more details.

{np}The way inside is clear.
Stay on guard.

{np}Leave the heavy lifting to us, {hero}.
Cover our flank―that's all we ask.

{np}{FF 9A 04}Experience points are not awarded to individual units. Instead, each class which participated in the battle receives a portion of the total. Only classes represented by the units who survive battle receive experience points.{pp}Skill points are handled in a similar fashion, with each surviving unit receiving an equal share of the total.
Refer to the Play Guide in the Warren Report for more details.

{np}Hmph. A fine time for this, with Master Nybeth away...{pp}Listen well. We face the rogues who slew Bapal and his men. Underestimate them and share Bapal's fate!{pp}Give these rebel swine a taste of Galgastani steel! Almorica shall never fall!

{np}Interlopers! Why do you meddle in our affairs?{pp}Our struggle with the Walister goes back generations―it's no concern of yours.{pp}Or do you seek to claim Valeria, as Lodis does?
I will have your answer!
{np}We are men without a country. We have lent them our swords because it suits us to do so.
{np}And we're looking for mercenary work, as it happens. Not hiring, by any chance?

{np}And worry you'll leave for a bigger purse?
We don't need outsiders to do our killing.
{np}He makes a good point. Let's rescue this duke, collect our reward, and be done with it.
{np}A craven who would choose lucre over loyalty deserves only one reward!
{np}My life...for Galgastan.

{np}The taste of freedom is sweet.
You have my thanks.{pp}Sweeter still that Walister youths came to my aid. {hero}, was it?{pp}Doubtless you and your friends are a gift from the Great Father himself.{pp}The Walister boon is great, and our future bright!
{np}We are not alone in our loyalty. Upon word of Your Grace's release, many Walister have left their haunts and hideaways for Almorica.

{np}And there is still time before the Galgastani come to remedy my freedom, though not long, I fear. We must regroup.{pp}{FF 92}Now I must ask if the tale our guests have told us is, indeed, the truth.

{np}Upon my sword, it is.
We are outcasts from our land.

{np}I do not doubt your sword. It is the whiskers of your companion that give me pause.{pp}I hear a diviner matching his description was ever at the side of King Tristan when your New Xenobia came into being two years past.{pp}And that you, Sir Lanselot, were captain of the Holy Knights.{pp}Is the Saint King so brazen as to cast out the very men who placed him upon the throne?
{np}I, too, have heard tell of this diviner, but I am not he.
{np}Lodis plagues us with the Dark Knights Loslorien. How do we know you are not some new menace visited upon Valeria?{pp}If New Xenobia does not seek to usurp, I would have your proof.
{np}Your Grace, these Holy Knights risked their own lives to win your freedom.
{np}A man can claim knighthood only when he serves a worthy lord. It is for such a man that we seek.

{np}I have your word then, and its proof shall be in your deeds.{pp}You sought a reward―you shall have it, and employment besides.{pp}I would have you train our Walister loyals as guards and soldiers here in Almorica.
{np}As you wish.
{np}Now, {hero}. Your father was an abuna in Golyat, was he not?{pp}I met him myself, once. A wise man, Abuna Prancet.{pp}What happened in Golyat was...a tragedy.
{np}Please, Your Grace, you must avenge our father―no―all the people of Golyat.
{np}Yet the enemy before us is Galgastan. They must come first.{pp}And for that, I will need knights. Knights...such as yourselves. Will you join my table at Almorica?
{np}Us? Knights!?

{np}As young heroes of Walister, you will serve as a shining example to your clansmen.{pp}I would have you become knights in my direct service. You will be the spear that strikes swift and true.{pp}Well, what say you?
{np}O-Of course. I mean, as you wish, Your Grace!{pp}I know {hero}'s with me on this.
{np}Excellent.{pp}Now, if you are to be a knightly order, you will require a name.
{np}How about...the Order of {order}?

{np}The Order of {order}? Yes...
A fine name.
You'll go far, I'm certain.{pp}I have much for you to do. Your first task takes you to the town of Krysaro, to the southwest.{pp}The captain of my knights, Sir Leonar, has gone there in pursuit of the former overseer of this castle, a necromancer named Nybeth.{pp}Truth be told, he's having a harder time of it than was expected.{pp}You'll be going to Krysaro to aid him. Understood?{pp}Before you leave, you'll want to fill your ranks with soldiers from Almorica and purchase such gear as you'll require.{pp}I expect you have little in way of coin, so I'm giving you 30,000 goth from the treasury.{pp}And...allow me to appoint a few of my own knights to serve under you. Leave as soon as you're ready.
{np}You can count on us, Your Grace. We won't let you down.
{np}Then may victory and glory await you, young heroes of Walister.

{np}You've led us to gainful employ after all.
My thanks.
{np}No, it is I who should thank you.
{np}So you're off to aid one of the duke's men. I regret we cannot join you.{pp}Above all else, stay alive.{pp}Win or lose, while there's life, there's hope.
{np}I'll try to remember that.
{np}Best not forget. The dead get no second chances.
{np}If death were our aim, there are swifter ways to go about it than soldiery.
{np}True enough. Still, do not needlessly seek out danger. Enough will find you as it is.
{np}Of course.
{np}You are the heroes of Golyat, are you not? I must thank you for saving His Grace the duke.{pp}Indeed, accept my thanks on behalf of us all.
{np}And you are...?
{np}Ravness Loxaerion, a knight in service of the duke.{pp}I would ride to Leonar's aid myself, but His Grace has other need of me. I fear the task falls to you.
{np}No need of fear, friend. We took back this castle, didn't we?
{np}In a manner of speaking, I suppose.
{np}And what "manner" would that be?
{np}She and her fellow knights drew off the garrison defending the castle, else we would not have succeeded.
{np}If it were not for the sacrifice of others, we would be no heroes of Golyat now.
{np}Make no mistake, I have high hopes for you.{pp}We must unite the people behind us if we are to put an end to this endless war.{pp}Word of your heroics emboldens them.
{np}Then you hold us up as heroes to serve some stratagem, is that it?
{np}If you do not like it, give truth to the lie. Write your own fate on the battlefield.
{np}May fate smile on us both, Dame Ravness.

{np}His Grace provided you with war funds, yes? Remember, they do no good sitting in your coffers.{pp}Arms, spells, provisions...even a single magicked ring can mean the difference between victory and defeat.
{np}She thinks highly of herself. I pray we are not near when she falls from such height!

{np}Walister rebels? Here? Then Almorica has fallen for true.{pp}Reinforcements for their kinsmen we have pinned down in Krysaro, I reckon. We can't let them pass.{pp}Make peace with the Light, Walister swine!
Today you die!
{np}You looked a lonely lot. Thought I might join you.
{np}I am Canopus. Step forward and meet your fate, dogs!

{np}{FF 9A 04}You can now use the Chariot Tarot!
During battle, the game keeps track of the last 50 turns. The Chariot Tarot allows you to return to any of these previous turns and replay the battle from that point.{pp}This alternate version of events is stored separately from the original, so you're free to choose the more favorable course. Access the Chariot Tarot by pressing the {icon 9} button, or press the {icon 12} button to access the System Menu and select the Chariot Tarot command.
{np}This is a Walister fight. We need no help from you!
{np}Stubborn as ever, eh? How did one so young grow so thick of skull?
{np}Thick? I'll give you thick!
{np}Ow! Not the wings!
{np}Vyce, control yourself!
{np}Today we fight for Walister honor, but where does it lead?
{np}What's the matter? Lose your nerve?{pp}Or has the nagging of your pacifist sister unmanned you? Always hiding behind her skirts.
{np}Thick of skull and a bully besides.
{np}That's enough squawking out of you, bird-man!
{np}Better a bird than a brute!
{np}You're not men, you're children!

{np}Let me tell you a thing or two about battle, {hero}. Clear the wax from your ears and listen.{pp}Whether you face a fearsome giant or a timid dormouse, the key is to divide and conquer.{pp}Focus your attacks on one enemy at a time, and you'll emerge the victor.

{np}{hero}, sibyls and mages cannot withstand the withering attacks of the front lines.{pp}Keep us in the back where we can support our warriors from afar.{pp}Be mindful of the enemy's position, and bring us no closer than need be.{pp}Use a bird's eye view if you are unsure of the distance.

{np}One more piece of advice, {hero}. I'm no parrot, so I'll say this only once.{pp}You're familiar with TP―Technical Points―yes?{pp}Action skills, special skills, and finishing moves all require TP to execute.{pp}TP accumulate over time and as units deal and receive damage.{pp}You'll need a weapon skill of rank two before you can use a finishing move, though.

{np}Gilbald...forgive me.
Look after Iuria...
{np}No place to die, this...
{np}Great Father! Ne'er have I seen such an undead throng! That necromancer uses men's souls for sport!{pp}Sleep, souls. Embrace the waiting Ever-World!

{np}Impossible!
My exorcism has failed!?{pp}Perhaps the corpses must be stilled before the soul can be put to rest...

{np}I've forgotten much in the fifteen years since I last faced the undead. Ah, but listen to me, making excuses.{pp}Patience, Leonar.
We need only wait for reinforcements.

{np}There, our liberators!
Great Father smile upon us this day.

{np}Perhaps they merely bare their teeth at you, old man. The sleep has already taken your friends.{pp}And no common sleep; they descend the sepulchral stairs toward death.{pp}When they wake, it will be as unliving horrors!
{np}We only need hold until Master Nybeth's return. Give them not an inch, and show them no quarter!
{np}Where is Master Nybeth? What's keeping him!?

{np}I've failed you...Leonar.
The rest is in...your hands.
{np}Master...Nybeth! Even in death would I have...served you.
{np}My thanks to you, {hero}. You've saved my life.

{np}And my apologies to you, Abuna. Such is our reward for striking blind.{pp}Already I have lost too many of the duke's men.
I know not how I shall face him.

{np}I am thankful that you, at least, still live.
The Great Father favors us.
{np}As he is surely displeased by the trespasses of this Nybeth: a sorcerer of the foulest sort.
{np}Yes, Nybeth! He lies hidden in a rotting fastness beyond the town.{pp}Odd. With his men left at Almorica, I'd have thought him bound for Coritanae...{pp}What could he be scheming?
{np}I want his head, whatever it may be plotting, but the fort is well defended.
{np}Agreed, even with the Great Father's aid, it would be a bold undertaking.

{np}Let us head back to Almorica and report.
Nybeth can't escape as long as we hold the town, so strike only when ready.
{np}It is for the best, considering the Galgastani threat. Why, they might attack at any moment.

{np}My skills would see better use in such a scenario indeed.
What are your plans, Abuna?
{np}I owe much to {hero}, it is heaven's will that I lend him my aid.

{np}I understand.
Others share that sentiment.

{np}Then it's settled.
We are yours to command.

{np}Our thanks to you, {hero}.
You've saved our lives.{pp}We came here in pursuit of Nybeth, but the man is as crafty as he is abhorrent. We were ambushed.{pp}I left some men in the field... Did you come across any other survivors?
{np}...As I feared. I have lost too many of the duke's men. I know not how I shall face him.
{np}If only we'd arrived sooner.{pp}Still, I'm grateful we were able to reach you. The duke is a reasonable man. Surely he knows you share his grief.

{np}You speak well, and I am grateful for your words.{pp}But this Nybeth...he is anathema to me and all with good in their hearts. How many have lost their lives to satisfy his dark hunger?{pp}I failed to take his head. A failure I mean to remedy.
{np}Leonar has told me of the battle. You have served me well.{pp}I hope you continue to do so. You are to accompany Leonar to Phidoch Castle―a Bakram holding.
{np}Phidoch Castle―where the Dark Knights are garrisoned. Why there?

{np}I want you to forge a treaty of non-interference before the real fighting with Galgastan begins.{pp}Not with the Bakram, mind you, but with the Dark Knights of Lodis.{pp}We cannot have them hounding our flank while we are occupied with Galgastan.
{np}But...Your Grace. It was the Bakram who brought on this war.{pp}Our parents died on Loslorien swords.{pp}Had they not aided the Bakram, how much suffering might we have been spared?

{np}None know this better than I, Catiua.{pp}But consider what would happen were we to face such a foe in open battle. They would crush us.{pp}The Bakram people, overfed swine that they are, are no threat. Ah, but the Dark Knights―there is a foe to be feared.{pp}Which is why we must swear our allegiance to Lodis and ensure they are no foe of ours.
{np}So Your Grace means to bend the knee to Lodis?

{np}Tread carefully, Vyce. I have told you we are of one mind on this.{pp}I know the devil's bargain we make with Lodis. But it is only until we can deal with Galgastan...and Balbatos.{pp}With the Dark Knights at bay, those opportunists in the Galgastani camp clamoring for war will fall silent.{pp}There's our chance. Once Balbatos is dead and buried, only then do we turn to strike the Bakram.{pp}What does our Holy Knight make of this?
The Xenobian throne has no designs on Valeria.
No Lodis, they.{pp}Surely, then, King Tristan would not object to a treaty of non-interference. A gesture of support for our burgeoning state.{pp}Ah, but I forget this has no bearing on you, Sir Lanselot. Forgive me.
{np}Well, the sooner you and Leonar have left for Phidoch, the better.{pp}A purse of 5,000 goth should help you see to your needs. I'll not have you depart unprepared.

{np}Walister forces...
Can't catch a break, can we?
{np}They have us in numbers. Best fall back to Rhime.
{np}I'd sooner fall into my grave! Are you a son of Galgastan or no!

{np}Talk brave as you like, it won't change our odds.
We should rejoin the file.
{np}Almorica falls, and you think the sky falls with it. There's no place here for cowards.

{np}Bring 'em on, I say!
For Galgastan!

{np}{FF 9A 04}You can now access the AI Menu.
Use the AI Menu to give control of your units to the computer. You can assign your units one of six behaviors, such as Melee, an aggressive combat role, or Vanguard, a front-line damage soak.
To control your units yourself, simply set the AI to Manual. To issue a command while units are moving under computer control, press the {icon 4} button.

{np}Warriors of Galgastan!
Lay down your arms, and you may yet keep your lives.
{np}I thought to offer you much the same deal, boy! A battle's won with blood, not numbers.

{np}Your cause is hopeless.
Why throw your lives away?
{np}Soon or late, all men meet their end. What good to live in fear of it?{pp}I know your kind―young, always thinking on tomorrow. You might try letting go. Drifting with the current.
{np}You think me unprepared for death? I'm not so young as that!
{np}Gods beneath us, why do I even bother?

{np}Stubborn wretch.
What's it take to kill you?

{np}Quite a tongue on you, boy.
Small wonder your kind find themselves reviled at every turn.

{np}{pal 16}Us{palreset} reviled!?
Look who's casting stones!
{np}Calm, Vyce.
{np}We do not fight to prove which side is least loved. We fight to restore peace!
{np}I spit on your peace! Almorica knew peace until you plunged it back into war!
{np}At least I'll know peace...in death.
{np}The sooner you accept the truth, the sooner this will be over. The alternative is also swift yet...painful.
{np}Kill me if you wish! You can never kill our spirit, nor our desire for justice!
{np}Defiant cur! Kill her.

{np}Hmm?
Who goes there?
{np}She's not Resistance... Another faction perhaps?

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} Whoever she is, we can't just leave her.
2. We have more important battles to fight.
{np}I won't stand here and watch her be hunted. Quickly, to her aid!
{np}I'd help her if we could, but we've more important battles to fight.
{np}You can't be serious. You'd let those Galgastani hunt her!?
{np}Of course he would, and he's right to do so.{pp}It's you I can't understand, Catiua.
{np}Either way, our quarrel is with the Galgastani. If we save her in the process, all the merrier.

{np}Aah, Cerya! Cerya, my sister...
Forget me...not.
{np}Cerya...? Where've I heard that name before?
{np}Aah, Cerya! Cerya, my sister... The Front is in...your hands.
{np}The Liberation Front? She's with them!?
{np}What!? I was not fated to die here... Not to you!

{np}Without your aid, I would never have escaped with my life. Thank you.{pp}I am Cistina, a warrior in the Liberation Front.{pp}I was scouting the Galgastani in preparation for a raid on their stores when they spotted me.
{np}Liberation Front? Partisan zealots, the lot of them. Nothing but trouble.
{np}I had always thought us two sides of the same coin.
{np}She is a Bakram traditionalist, a group loyal to the late King Dorgalua.
{np}I've heard of them. Not all Bakram support the current regime, after all.
{np}Oh, their goals are lofty enough, but their deeds border on butchery.{pp}They risk the lives of soldier and innocent alike with their subversion. Means unworthy of their end.
{np}You have us wrong! These are lies spread by Brantyn!{pp}We seek only a return to better times, when a man's race and beliefs could not discredit him.
{np}Better times? Don't make me laugh!{pp}Good enough for those with luck to be born Bakram, but we lived then as we do now―insects beneath the boots of our betters!

{np}I see...
Then tell me: why is it that you fight?

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} To secure a future for the Walister.
2. For peace.
{np}We must build a country of our own if our people are to have any future.
{np}Your words echo Brantyn's own. You speak of your country, your people, but you care only for yourselves.{pp}You refuse compromise, turn your back on cooperation. What selfish creatures.
{np}Are your motives so pure? I find the stench of Bakram dogs difficult to tell apart!

{np}Enough, Vyce.
Such talk leads us nowhere.{pp}You are free to go, Cistina. But you must quit this place at once.{pp}This is our land. Our fight. The Bakram are not welcome here.

{np}As you wish. But we will not stop until the world is made fair and just.{pp}One day you will open your eyes.{pp}You will see that only by putting aside vain desires can we usher in an era of true peace.
{np}Go now, and do not return.
{np}We seek only peace. A world free of war and strife. This is why we fight.
{np}Then we share common cause. Let us fight together.
{np}Us, fight alongside Bakram? Absurd.{pp}The peace we fight for is one in which the Walister can live as men.{pp}We want no part of any shared peace. I piss on your common cause!
{np}Without your aid, I would never have escaped with my life. Thank you.
{np}Think nothing of it. It is by chance we helped you, no more.{pp}Rather thank the Great Father. He favors you. Now, why is it the Galgastani clamor for your blood?
{np}I am Cistina, a warrior in the Liberation Front. I was scouting our common enemy.

{np}Liberation Front? Partisan zealots, the lot of them.
Nothing but trouble.
{np}Oh their goals are lofty enough, but their deeds border on butchery.{pp}They risk the lives of soldier and innocent alike with their subversion. Means unworthy of their end.
{np}It is plain nothing I say will sway you.{pp}I thank you again for saving me. Now I will take my leave.
{np}You have leave to go, Cistina. But you must quit this place at once.{pp}This is our land. Our fight. The Bakram are not welcome here.
{np}I shall try to remember that.

{np}Who goes there?
Speak your name!
{np}I am Leonar Reci Rimon, sworn sword of the Knights of Almorica.{pp}I come before you a humble servant of the great Duke Ronwey, esteemed leader of the Walister.
{np}I shall announce your arrival.

{np}The Dark Knights make their fastness here in Phidoch Castle.{pp}See her soaring white walls? No wonder they name her "The Swan."{pp}But beneath her outward beauty is a nearly impregnable fortress.{pp}Be glad we are not tasked to take her.
{np}We have looked for your arrival, Sir Leonar. You bring word from the duke?
{np}I do, my lord.
{np}No doubt you've had a hard journey. Come. Rest within our halls.
{np}...Good knights. We find your duke's proposal most intriguing.
{np}Have you an answer?
{np}Perhaps you had best ask my lord directly for that.
{np}Sir Lanselot is here, in this castle!?
{np}He is.{pp}Greetings, brave knights of the Walister. I am Lanselot Tartaros.
{np}Leonar Reci Rimon of Almorica, if it please you.{pp}You have considered our proposal?

{np}Ha! You waste no time, do you? I like that. I do have an answer for your duke.{pp}Tell His Grace that his struggle with the Galgastani is of no concern to His Eminence Abuna Brantyn.{pp}Nor is it any concern of ours. The Knights Loslorien remain and shall remain neutral on the matter.
{np}My thanks, sir, for your swift response. Our lord will be much pleased.
{np}Indeed. Yet I must ask: do you really believe you can defeat Galgastan without our aid?

{np}Defeat Galgastan? Surely not. But such was never our intention.{pp}All we want―all we have ever wanted―is to fashion a peace with them.{pp}The Galgastani are a proud people. Were it to come to light that we sought the aid of a foreign power...{pp}I am afraid it would endanger the position of those in the Galgastani ranks who seek an accord as we do.
{np}So your duke does not want to anger his neighbors by placing his problems in our hands.{pp}Bakram could stand to take a lesson from him!
{np}I...I did not mean to suggest...

{np}No matter.
We of Lodis place much upon a man's honor.{pp}I can understand why your duke would disdain the Bakram way―enjoying a life of leisure while others do their dirty work.
{np}As you say, sir.
{np}Forgive me, but your henchmen are so youthful I feared you wanted for seasoned men.
{np}Though they may be young in years, my knights' skill in battle is no lesser for it.
{np}Indeed.
{np}They freed His Excellency and routed the Galgastani at Almorica.{pp}Moreover, it was they who came to my aid in Krysaro. Without their intervention, I would not be here today.
{np}Ah, so these are the heroes of Golyat, then? Forgive an old knight his errant tongue.{pp}I say...have we met?

{np}No, not as such.
That is...

{np}That is...what?
Speak plainly.
{np}That night in Golyat, it snowed for the first time in years. I remember the sweep of flakes over the harbor, the bitter cold.{pp}You were there.
{np}Mind your place, Catiua! Have you forgotten why we are here?

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} Not now, Sister.
2. We were fools to treat with our enemy.
{np}He's right, Sister. This isn't the time. This conflict is larger than us now.
{np}Ahh, the torching. You would have been children...of course!
{np}Aye. We attacked that night on word that elements of the resistance lurked in town.
{np}False word, yes. I remember it well. As do you, clearly.{pp}We were in error, though I hardly expect forgiveness on that count. Still, I can but apologize, for all it will do.

{np}E-Enough of this.
The duke awaits our return.
{np}Oh? I had hoped to speak at greater length.
{np}Forgive them―forgive us, good sir. We'll be taking our leave.
{np}Was that entirely necessary?
{np}I recalled Hobyrim.
{np}Hrnn? My brother? Aye, he was a staunch ally in a fight. Why?
{np}Nothing. Only, the brother and sister just now put me in mind of him and you.
{np}We cannot join forces with a sworn foe...and you {pal 16}are{palreset} our foe.
{np}What quarrel is this, and what place has it here!?

{np}Are you mad?
Please, forgive him. His passion clouds his judgement.
{np}You recall Hobyrim?
{np}You set aside your own enmity for the greater Walister good. Such loyal service will not be forgotten.{pp}Would that time afforded you more rest―but I must ask you to leave for Balmamusa at once.
{np}Balmamusa? That lies in the territory the Galgastani allotted for Walister rule, no?

{np}Walister rule... Hmph. Camps where our people are forced to live in squalor.{pp}It was a mining town, once. Coal. Now our kinsmen are herded there like cattle.{pp}Some five thousand labor in Balmamusa, slaves in all but name.{pp}The conditions are horrific beyond words. Scores die by the day.
{np}Then it falls to us to free them.
{np}You could never free five hundred, leave alone five thousand. No, you are to incite them to revolt.
{np}An army five thousand strong, there for the taking.

{np}In truth, we cannot stay our course and hope for victory. We are far outmatched.{pp}However slight, we must tip the scales in our favor before Galgastan strikes.{pp}If all goes well, our bid will widen the rift between Balbatos and his enemies at home.{pp}He can scarce dispatch troops here before silencing the cries of dissent within his own ranks.{pp}We cannot let such chance escape us!
{np}There will be those in Balmamusa with no stomach for fighting, and others who would sooner leave things as they are.{pp}Your task will be to win them to our cause.
{np}They grow weary of fighting, else they would rally more readily.{pp}I can think of none better to wake their slumbering heroism than young heroes such as yourselves.
{np}I shall follow at the head of a separate file bearing arms for them.
{np}The Galgastani hold the lands west of Tynemouth. Dame Ravness will go with you in support.
{np}My sword is yours.
{np}Much rests on your young shoulders. I pray for your swift return.
{np}I'm counting on you, Leonar. Do not fail me.
{np}No need to worry. Our plans proceed apace.
{np}Sir Lanselot.

{np}Ah, {hero}.
Tracked me down, did you?
{np}Sir Gildas told me I'd find you here.

{np}So you have.
Please, come closer.
{np}You look troubled. This business in Balmamusa disturbs you?
{np}Sir Leonar says it will be a dangerous undertaking.

{np}Are you frightened?
That's not like you.
{np}I am not frightened.
{np}There's no shame in admitting fear. We are all afraid at one time or another.
{np}Even you?
{np}More times than I can count. At the first ring of steel, my hands tremble with it.{pp}But fear alone cannot kill you―it has no teeth.
{np}It's strange. I tell myself I would gladly die for our cause.{pp}But when faced with death, the fear is all too real.
{np}Risking your life is one thing. Losing it is another.{pp}The best way to aid your people is to stay alive. See the battle through to the end.{pp}And there's your sister to think of.

{np}What about you?
Would you die to save the ones you love?
{np}What's that?

{np}A music box.
It belonged to my wife.
{np}...Your wife?

{np}It's been four...five years now. Before the war with the Empire.{pp}They had already begun their advance, and we fled―vagrants in our own land.{pp}My wife fell ill, and before I knew it...she was gone.{pp}I considered following her into death. My thoughts often strayed down that path before battle.{pp}But her music box still sang of life, and I knew it was not my time.{pp}My burden had not yet reached its end.
{np}I’m sorry.
{np}One young as you should never be forced to fight. But that's not the world we live in.

{np}Walister? Here!?
And in such numbers...{pp}How does His Eminence not see it? Troubled times such as these demand a staunch front line.

{np}You there!
Hold the line, or I'll kill you myself!
{np}We cannot let these rebels cross Lake Bordu! Forward!

{np}Warriors of Galgastan!
Lay down your weapons and you may yet live!
{np}By the Light! Ravness, is that you? I thought you long dead by now.
{np}I know this voice. How is it that you do not find yourself dead, Grion? You have rare luck indeed.{pp}Let our swords meet. The cry of their steel is fitting lament for those you have butchered.

{np}More men...
We needed more...
{np}Broken through our line, have they? I always knew Grion weren't nothin' but talk.{pp}Just as well. Past time me pets had their first taste o' battle.{pp}Berda!

{np}Obda!
To me!
{np}And what are the rest o' you waitin' for? Get out here!

{np}Berda! Obda!
Show 'em how it's done!
{np}Berda? What have they done t'you!? Home now!{pp}No one hurts me precious Berda and gets away with it! I won't forget who it was done this!
{np}Obda? What have they done t'you!? Home now!{pp}No one hurts me precious Obda and gets away with it! I won't forget who it was done this!

{np}Am I...bleeding!? You children play a mite rough!{pp}Berda! Obda! Home now!
As for you...I won't forget who it was done this!

{np}Who...who's there? Rebels!?
We're under attack! To arms!
{np}We have some time before our support arrives.{pp}There’s no time to speak to everyone. We should gather a small group who can serve as our heralds.
{np}Are you daft? We didn't come all this way to listen to you spout nonsense.{pp}{pal 16}We{palreset} are not the enemy! Or are you so taken with your Galgastani masters you have forgotten?
{np}There's no call for such rancor, Vyce. We should hear them out.
{np}Suppose we do fight. What then? Conflict will only lead to more suffering.{pp}At least here the winds of war do not howl in our ears, and our stomachs do not grumble.
{np}Shelter, fodder―you enjoy all the luxuries of cattle. Doubtless you will so long as you remain.{pp}But do you not long to be free? To live as men?{pp}You are Walister! Where is your pride?

{np}Leave as you came. Let us live out our lives in peace.{pp}Today it's the Resistance, tomorrow who-knows-what, but you all sing the same tune.{pp}My son sounded much as you do―the war claimed him six months ago. Will your violence bring him back?
{np}We want no part of your fight.{pp}You’re doomed to fail, any road. Galgastan is too powerful.{pp}Heroes you may be, but the pride always comes before the fall!
{np}Forgive me, I was delayed. Might I have a quiet word?

{np}I overheard your conversation. These people do not convince easily.{pp}{FF 92}No matter. We feared it would come to this.{pp}{FF 92}Listen to me. There's something you must do.{pp}You must...you must kill them. All of them. Spare no one.
{np}What!?
{np}The duke foreknew this outcome. These are his orders.
{np}But why this? If you know even one reason, I would hear it!
{np}Because His Grace...demands it.

{np}If the people of Balmamusa rise up as we ask, well and good.{pp}But the words of these children will not be enough to move them to take up arms.{pp}When they refuse, you are to kill them under guise of Galgastani agents. Leave no survivors.
{np}You can't be serious! You order us to kill our own!

{np}Calm, Leonar. You've a good head on your shoulders. Consider our situation.{pp}If we are to defeat Galgastan, the Walister must unite as never before.{pp}If it appears the Galgastani destroyed Balmamusa, our people in the remaining camps will rally to our banner.
{np}But...Your Grace...

{np}Nor will opposition in the Galgastani ranks remain unmoved by such outrage.{pp}Balbatos will be beset by foes without and within.{pp}We will finally have both the opportunity and the moral imperative to rid the world of the creature.
{np}{hero} and the others will not do this quietly.
{np}You will see to that as well, when the time comes.
{np}You are with me then? It is the only way. The future of our people depends on it!

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} I understand.
2. Stop this lunacy!

{np}I see what must be done.
I will bloody my hands.
{np}Don't worry. We'll not let their sacrifice be in vain.
{np}{hero}, are you mad? You're going to go along with this!?
{np}The duke gave such an order, Leonar? And you would carry it out?
{np}Open your eyes. We cannot win if we are unwilling to dirty our hands.
{np}Ours is to follow orders. I swore an oath before the duke. Before the realm.

{np}Listen to you!
If I closed my eyes, I'd think I spoke with a Galgastani!
{np}The duke would sacrifice these people as a piece in some great game.{pp}Our lord has betrayed us all. To think I was willing to give my life for such a man. What a fool I was.
{np}Then you stand apart, Vyce? You will not join us?
{np}Damn right! These people have done nothing. Where the justice in killing them!?
{np}I did not think you one to abdicate duty, Ravness. To break faith with lord and realm.
{np}I break no faith. I renounce the duke... I renounce you all!
{np}I always thought to find you at my side the day the Walister won their freedom.{pp}But if men of our own blood would stand against us, why should I expect more of you?
{np}Am I not Walister?
{np}Walister descended from Galgastani stock.{pp}But the fault is mine. I should not have placed such faith in one of mingled blood!
{np}How dare you!
{np}Every victory comes at a price. Can't you see that?{pp}People are dullwits! The sacrifice must be great to wake them from their languor!

{np}And you, Catiua?
Will you follow in this madness?
{np}I...I will ever stand with {hero}!
{np}From this day, you and I are enemies!

{np}Kill them all!
No rebel leaves this place alive!
{np}Galgastani reinforcements―deal with them. Leave the townsfolk to me!
{np}Stop this madness! What virtue can there be in taking innocent lives!?

{np}You are yet young... Your heart is pristine, though I daresay your hands have seen their share of bloodshed.{pp}All that is required of you is to plunge those hands deeper. Bloody them not for survival, but for your cause.{pp}{FF 92}If you cannot do that, you do not belong in this battle!

{np}{hero}, are you all right?
Vyce, with us, quickly!

{np}Vyce? What are you waiting―
No...!
{np}Kill them, Vyce. All three of them!

{np}What good are kinsmen who won't lift arms for our cause? I'll tell you. They're as good as dead.{pp}If it's retribution you fear, fear not―they'll all be in their graves, thanking you for martyring them!
{np}I don't believe what I am hearing! If this is a jest, it is in terrible humor!
{np}Quiet, Catiua! You've made a fool of me long enough.{pp}You as well, {hero}! You...you {pal 16}vex{palreset} me. Always have!{pp}What ever gave you the right to command me!
{np}Leonar, I cannot believe such an order came from His Grace! And you would see this madness through!?
{np}I would see through any of His Grace's decrees, as his loyal servant―no, as a loyal servant to our people.

{np}You'd call such bloodshed "service"? Since when have we used our kinsmen's lives as leverage?{pp}Our lord has betrayed us all. To think I was willing to give my life for such a man. What a fool I was.

{np}Hear me, fierce warriors of Galgastan! We made this province to give shape to the peace we all want.{pp}Yet Ronwey in Almorica and his rabble have trampled upon that peace, and lifted their swords once again.{pp}We will not sit here and wait for death to visit us! We'll show them what it means to be Galgastani!{pp}Root out the Walister in town and butcher them like the swine they are! Leave not one alive! To battle!
{np}Vyce, to me! Leave this to the others. We take the town!
{np}Wait... Leonar! Vyce!
{np}Heel, Ravness. You yap like the mongrel you are!
{np}Leonar...do not think you can escape...judgement for your deeds.
{np}I hoped more from you, {hero}.{pp}A man who places ends before means treads a dangerous path.{pp}The shame is mine for daring to hope.{pp}On my honor, you are my foe, {hero}!

{np}Since ancient times, there has been a word for one who sells his soul to the devil.{pp}They call him "ogre," a demon who eats the flesh of men!{pp}I see now the many you will consume in your lust for power. You are an ogre in truth!
{np}This is the path you have chosen, {hero}...{pp}May the Light...pierce the clouds o'er you...
{np}I just can't believe you're of Galgastani descent.
{np}You feel yourself betrayed? You'd heed blood over word and action?{pp}Can the light of deed not pierce the shadow of one's birth?{pp}I believe it can. I will not believe otherwise!
{np}Now now, her blood's not mixed of her own doing, boy.{pp}I myself am not of the common race...though I can't say as I've met misfortune on that account.{pp}Just luck, perhaps.
{np}I...hadn't considered that.

{np}Time for considering later.
We've more pressing matters.
{np}Lower your blade, Ravness. What reason could any of us have to quarrel amongst ourselves?

{np}I would have your reasons, if you've any worth repeating! You'd give your blessing to this sacrilege?{pp}Or have you chosen to turn your back on the Light, on the very teachings of the Great Father? Is revenge your calling now, Abuna?{pp}The blood of your sworn enemy flows in my veins! Why not slay me, too?
{np}If the Great Father does not yet require my soul, then what? Am I to be a shepherd to these youths?
{np}I'll kill you by my own hands, {hero}! I swear it!
{np}Do not let them harm the villagers! We will defend them with our own lives, should it come to that! Go!
{np}Next will be your turn. I'll kill you by my own hands! I swear it!

{np}{FF 9C 0101}{FF 8D 0102}{FF 85 013d}There is blood on my hands,{FF 89 51}
{FF 8D 0102}{FF 85 013d}how long till it lies on my heart?{FF 98 0105}

{np}Tracked me down, have you? Moldova's gone, then.{pp}She harbored a rare appreciation for my research. Sad to see her pass, though I envy her newfound vicinity to Death!{pp}Yet it is not time to join her company. Perhaps we might come to an...understanding?{pp}I care not who rules this island. Take it, it's yours.{pp}My siege of Almorica was a purely business venture, you see. A deal struck with the Hierophant to satisfy my...curiosities.{pp}And what of it? Your precious castle is returned. What's done is done!{pp}I propose you let me go free. The alternative, of course, would be for us to do battle.{pp}But no...the time it would take to destroy you is that much less time for my research! Hardly efficient.{pp}If there's anything I detest in this world, it is inefficiency!

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} Surrender, and I will not harm you.
2. To the darkness with you!

{np}Lay down your arms, and you will come to no harm. But you cannot go free.{pp}If you would do penance for your crimes, come to Almorica. I promise your life will be spared.{pp}...Though, you will be our prisoner and treated no better than you deserve.

{np}I approve! You forsake the chaotic nature of youth for the twin lights of reason and order!{pp}Yet, I must decline. You may mean well, but there is no shortage of others who would see me hang.{pp}Even as I ask why we must fight, I accept the inevitability of the coming battle. Freedom's wage must be paid in full.{pp}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you! Darkness to me!
{np}Now, an experiment! Let us mix youth with danger and observe the reaction!
{np}You would take lives to sate some curiosity?{pp}You profane the Light as you profane the dead.

{np}You have me wrong.{pp}My intellectual curiosity and your blind loyalty are not so dissimilar.{pp}Both inspire us equally to action, and there is little difference in the number of resulting dead.{pp}But you see, while you leave only death in your path, I leave a species of life.{pp}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you! Darkness to me!
{np}Let's see whether your false piety can prevail!
{np}To steal not only lives, but the very dignity of repose...you fiend!{pp}In the name of the Great Father Philaha, I condemn you to hell!
{np}Oh dear, not one of those. I find men who go about claiming they speak for gods insufferable.{pp}The tenacity of your belief is admirable, but truly, deities and demons? Rubbish.
{np}Avaunt, mage, for the holy Light that gives me strength is a miracle in truth―{pp}As the necromantic heresy you practice is the work of demons!

{np}What you call magic is merely another aspect of physical law, and those who call themselves "deities" or "demons" merely flesh.{pp}While one man's spirit may be lofty, and another's heart devilish, bowing to one of them does not make you pious...{pp}It makes you weak!{pp}To honor gods and despise demons is to dilute the weight of your words and the import of your actions.{pp}A man of your years should have realized this fundamental truth by now.
{np}Enough of this cretin's blasphemy! I was wrong to pay him any heed at all.

{np}I am forced to choose between retreat and death. How...unexpected.{pp}But I am afraid your victory cannot be complete, for there is still vital research to be done, and none to do it but me!{pp}{hero}, was it? A name I shall make a point to remember.{pp}When the war is lost and won, I feel we will meet again. When we do, I will be only too happy to reveal the ripened fruits of my research.{pp}Until then.
{np}Don't go on blaming yourself. You did all you could.

{np}I did nothing.
I couldn't save them.
{np}{hero}, what if we left this place? Sailed far away and never looked back?
{np}We've been through this―father must be avenged!{pp}Besides, how could we leave things as they are?{pp}No, we stay and see this through. We owe it to those who died at Balmamusa.

{np}At it again, are you?
Give your quibbling a rest and look at this.
{np}As the duke grows more impatient, you grow more valuable! Up to 30,000 goth now.
{np}Salt in our wounds. We are criminals before all the world.
{np}Justice and war seldom keep company. In the heat of battle, all are criminal and all are innocent.{pp}Only later does the victor decide who is which.{pp}That's the way of the world.
{np}And since I lost―since I failed Balmamusa―I am made a criminal for it.
{np}All the more reason to be on the winning side. Come, enough navel-gazing. We need to go.
{np}Go? Where?
{np}The Walister army gathers southwest of the Burnham Massif in the Psonji Weald.
{np}Of course. Galgastan doesn't stand a chance of repelling the Resistance, not now.
{np}You touch it with a needle. Balbatos's days are numbered. I daresay Walister victory is in the air.
{np}In which case we shall remain outlaws.

{np}All the more reason to be on our way. Something must be done.{pp}Word reaches me that the Holy Knight Lanselot has taken up position behind the Walister―on Tynemouth Hill, to be exact.{pp}With the Walister massed elsewhere, Tynemouth will have but light defense.{pp}What better place to break through the line?
{np}Of course! Lanselot will aid us, I am certain.
{np}Then we move. There's naught more to be done in this wretched place.
{np}Here, have a look. The likeness is uncanny! Say, you're up to 30,000 goth now.
{np}There's nothing left for us here. We should leave. Sail somewhere far away.
{np}You know I can't do that, Sister. Not now.
{np}But what can we do, few as we are? We've nowhere to turn.
{np}The Resistance has crossed the Burnham Massif. They gather in the Psonji Weald.
{np}Yes, and soon they will be fighting the Galgastani. What of it?

{np}Balbatos is done. Galgastan has little hope of routing the Resistance. They are grown too strong.{pp}But that is no true victory. We only trade one tyrant for another.{pp}The duke's means may be more subtle, but they are no less cruel.
{np}But what are we to do about it? What can we do?

{np}I am told Lanselot and his men are among the force sent to besiege Coritanae.{pp}Since they are not Walister, they've been stationed on Tynemouth Hill, at the far end of the Psonji Weald.{pp}The Resistance holds that ground lightly. What better place to break their line?
{np}If anyone will help us, it's Lanselot. But even so...
{np}We will have no better chance, Sister! Come. The moment is upon us!

{np}At last I find you, {hero}.
You've given good chase, but the hunt ends here!
{np}You're not the first headhunter to mistake me for easy quarry.
{np}Oh, I'll have your head, but I am no headhunter. You'll pay in blood for what you did in Balmamusa!

{np}You were in Balmamusa!?
Please, you must hear me!

{np}We are past talk.
For Balmamusa! For my brother!

{np}Enough of this!
We did no murder in Balmamusa!{pp}We were there, I'll not deny it―but we did all we could to stop the slaughter!
{np}Lies! I only pray you sold your loyalty for a worthy sum!
{np}My brother injured his leg―he couldn't even walk―but they cut him down just the same.
{np}All the duke's doing. Galgastan had no hand in it, though the duke wished it to appear so.{pp}Believe what you will, I speak the truth!
{np}Have you no shame?
{np}She has no ear to listen. If words will not win us free, our steel must!
{np}If she'll not listen to reason, she leaves us no choice.
{np}Hold, Arycelle! You must hear me!{pp}All {hero} has told you is true. We were conspired against!
{np}Abuna Donnalto? How can this be!?{pp}Leonar said that you...you died in Balmamusa!

{np}Leonar told you this? I did not think him capable of such duplicity...{pp}Arycelle, as I am living proof, Leonar's words are false.{pp}A cozener playwright, he knows the truth, yet writes for us a damning fiction.
{np}What do you mean to say? That Leonar has misled me on purpose?{pp}Nay...this is no fiction! I know the horrors I saw in Balmamusa! I will never forget!
{np}No, Arycelle! You are captive to your own rage. It veils from you the truth!{pp}O, Great Father Philaha! Raise this child's heart from the dark recesses of hate!
{np}Did Leonar know his error when he spoke to me of Abuna Donnalto's death?
{np}No easy task, discerning the truth. Least of all when it's unpleasant.
{np}Do you suggest I am blind to the truth, outlander? Speak!

{np}I suggest only that you take a deep breath. I find it often calms a troubled mind.{pp}The wind and my people have been as one since the dawn of days.{pp}Restoring the balance of spirit and wind helps clear the head―and only a clear head can search the soul.{pp}Easier said, eh? Still, if you can do, might see something you missed.
{np}Am I now to be lectured by one who prostitutes his loyalty?
{np}Sky above, what is it that makes you Valerian women so stubborn?
{np}I know when I am bested...though the knowledge that my brother goes unavenged pains me more than any wound.
{np}It is done. Now kill me. Kill as you did in Balmamusa!
{np}I will not. You are not my foe.{pp}If you have lost the will to fight, leave. I will not give chase.
{np}If I leave here now, I will only return to claim your life.
{np}Then know I am bound for Tynemouth. If you would hunt me, hunt me there.
{np}You're going to regret this.
{np}Regret? There is already too much for me to regret.
{np}The Wheel spins true! "You'll find them in Asyton," they said, and here you are!{pp}Not every day you chance on a mark worth 30,000 goth!
{np}There are your headhunters, {hero}. I know them by the dull light in their eyes.
{np}Wa ha ha! A comely maid with a curdled tongue! I approve!{pp}Don't worry, little lass. You'll be spared. You alone.{pp}A man grows lonely so far from home, heh?
{np}Well, well, let's begin, shall we? Look sharp, boys! Let one go, it'll mean your purse!

{np}You there, warrior. You've the look of a man who settles for digging in the dust when he could be moving mountains.{pp}You'll find more glory in battle than chasing after a pittance of bounty, no?

{np}Glory in battle? Ha!
There's no glory to be had there, not any more.{pp}Balmamusa made a cripple of Galgastan. She only has the one leg left, and that already in the grave.
{np}Little profit to be had from laying siege to Coritanae, then?
{np}Aye, that's the truth of it. Still profit in claiming heads like yours, though.

{np}Feh. That was ill played.
Pull back! These ones'll keep for later.
{np}What, running away? After all your talk of glory? Bristle-bearded boor!
{np}Har! That mouth ne'er opens but a mealy nugget spills forth. I'd tarry longer just for that! But next time, fair lass. Next time.

{np}Feh. That was ill played.
Pull back! These ones'll keep for later.{pp}I trust you'll hold any other 'hunter off from plucking that gourd of yours, boy!
{np}Take the scouts alive! They'll talk...or they'll scream.
{np}Decurion, I know this woman. She led the ambush at Lodum.
{np}This...{pal 16}this{palreset} is the Thunder Maiden!?

{np}What of it? Near six hundred fell at my bidding, 'tis true. Would you deliver their vengeance?{pp}The blood of tenfold that number stains your hands! And then there is Balmamusa...{pp}I'll not be lectured by the likes of you!

{np}Is that Arycelle? 
The Galgastani have her outnumbered. We must help!
{np}Oh? It is she pursues us. What cause have we to help her?
{np}Sister, no doubt you are right. But I will live with no more regrets!
{np}My dear {hero}...
{np}Arycelle, I'm coming! Draw closer, if you can!
{np}Explain yourself, {hero}! I am your sworn enemy. I name you traitor!
{np}I am no traitor. But I was wrong to fight for the duke. I see that now.

{np}Still you spout treason!
Stay back! Any closer, and I'll kill you!

{np}Arycelle, your faith in Leonar is understandable―I would fain believe him myself.{pp}But he― Leonar has lost his way. He forgets that no aim, no matter how lofty, is ever served by sin.{pp}He was not like this before. I fear he has lost his way.

{np}It's true then? Leonar is responsible for Balmamusa?{pp}Abuna, I...I can't believe it.
I do not want to believe.
{np}Nor do I. But the blood of our people soaks his sword.{pp}Perhaps as high champion of the Knights of Almorica, he placed duty before honor.
{np}Why him? Why was he alone tasked with such a burden?
{np}I know no more than you. Indeed, it vexes me I did not espy it in his heart before it was too late.
{np}No. I loved him. It is I should have known. Perhaps...it was my love that blinded me.
{np}There's no doubting your resolve, but how long must this go on? We are not the enemy!
{np}No more words. I must have proof!
{np}Fair enough. But is not the enemy of an enemy a friend?{pp}The Galgastani are our common adversary. Can we not first deal with them?

{np}A truce then.
For now.
{np}For now. There's no getting round to the truth if we're dead!
{np}I will NOT die...not until I have the truth from Leonar.

{np}Brother, forgive me.
I did not intend to join you...before avenging you.

{np}No!
It wasn't supposed to be this way! No!!!

{np}My life spills on the ground...
Forgive me, brothers. Your deaths go...unavenged.

{np}Again I've failed.
Am I so powerless as this?
{np}I can go no further.

{np}I surrender, {hero}.
I'm too weary to go on.
{np}Then your life is mine. But I will not claim it here.
{np}So I am to be your hostage? Do not think such tactics will dissuade the duke.

{np}You have it wrong. We wish only to clear our names.{pp}Watch with your eyes, listen with your ears. Witness the truth of this war for yourself.{pp}If still you cannot trust me, your life will be yours once more.{pp}And my life yours as well.
{np}Your words have the ring of truth, but I am a Knight of Almorica.{pp}Honor demands evidence more substantial.
{np}Then I will speak on this no more. Come, we should be going.

{np}Resistance? Here? I thought they rallied in the Psonji Weald...{pp}Wait, I know that face.{pp}You're the Walister that did for Balmamusa! I saw the bill for your bounty.{pp}Bad enough you made it seem our work, but to slaughter your own... Faithless swine.{pp}So young, for acts so foul. No wonder the duke outmaneuvered you so easily.
{np}Believe what you will, we played no part in that pantomime.

{np}It's no good. Even our fellow Walister are convinced you were behind it.{pp}What hope have you of convincing this crowd of your innocence?{pp}And the fact remains: they are Galgastani, we are Walister. We are honor bound to fight!
{np}It's as the lady says. I care nothing for the bounty on your heads.{pp}One Walister is much like another―only good to me dead.{pp}Rally to me! For our brothers! For our homeland!

{np}You waste your breath. Arycelle is Walister, she did not believe us. Why should they?{pp}The Galgastani are our enemy. Convince them of our innocence, and they will remain so.{pp}In either event, it will come to battle. We are Walister!

{np}Brother, forgive me.
I did not want to join you...before avenging you.

{np}My struggle ends too soon...
Glory to Galgastan! Glory...
{np}There's no one here. Strange. Perhaps they've already joined the others in the Psonji Weald.
{np}What? Impossible!

{np}Good to see you again, {hero}.
And looking so well.{pp}I worried some second-rate headhunter had done for you.

{np}What are you doing here?
The Holy Knight Lanselot―where is he?
{np}Vyce! What business have you here? I thought you in the Psonji Weald!

{np}And I thought you dead, Arycelle. Guess we were both wrong.{pp}They say you ignored Leonar's orders and chased down {hero}...but this?{pp}So that's the way of it. Turned traitor, have you?{pp}Fool woman. You choose the losing side.
{np}I choose no side until I have judged for myself who the traitors among us truly are.
{np}What are you doing here, Vyce? Where's Lanselot?
{np}Ha ha! All these years, and still you surprise me. I did not think false whispers would lure you so easily.{pp}Your Xenobian's not here. No doubt he's in Rhime by now, deep in his cups.
{np}Sorry you won't be joining them, but you die here.{pp}Duke's orders. None with eyes at Balmamusa are to live.

{np}You too, Arycelle.
If the truth were to get out, it would mean no end of trouble.
{np}You were at Balmamusa, Vyce?
{np}Aye, that I was. With your beloved Leonar, no less. So wait―{pp}You knew nothing of what was planned? Not a word?
{np}No...no! Leonar must be mad! Only a lunatic would pay such price for victory.
{np}Pity you learned the truth, girl.{pp}There'll be no reconciling with Leonar now. You're not one to look the other way.

{np}Kill them all!
Spare no one!
{np}What are you doing here?
{np}Ha ha ha.
{np}Where's Lanselot?
{np}Ha! All these years and you still surprise me. I did not think false whispers would lure you so easily.{pp}Your Xenobian's not here. No doubt he's in Rhime by now, deep in his cups.
{np}I will avenge my brother on his killer. Even be that you, Leonar.

{np}Vyce! Call off your men!
There is no need for this!
{np}You disobeyed orders at your own peril... Traitors!
{np}Orders!? That was a call to slaughter innocents! What man could heed that?
{np}This man could! How are you unable to see it, {hero}?{pp}History will show that our countrymen's sacrifice built our future anew.
{np}Vyce...what's happened to you?

{np}A life spent hiding from soldiers... Brings back old times, eh?{pp}After the Dark Knights attacked Golyat, we three hid in a deserted house near the church waiting for the Bakram to withdraw.{pp}Our stomachs were empty, our hearts full of fear they would discover us.{pp}You swore you would never live like that again, Catiua.
{np}Your point eludes me.

{np}It's not too late, Catiua. Come with me. I can have you spared with a word.{pp}Where has following {hero} led you?{pp}Always running, always hiding. It wearies you, I see it in your eyes. Wouldn't you rather walk in the light?

{np}Shadow, light, I care not!
My only wish is to stand at {hero}'s side!

{np}Do you feel nothing, Vyce?{pp}How can you look upon the wreckage of Balmamusa and not weep with shame?{pp}We have known each other since we were children! How can you lift your sword against a friend!?

{np}Because I know that what I do is right, Catiua.{pp}I'm no murderer, but this is war! We are not playing at soldiers anymore!{pp}And I am not content to sit grousing about "injustice" when the means to end this suffering is within my grasp!
{np}As you "ended the suffering" of so many of your countrymen in Balmamusa?

{np}I see you'd place all the evils of war at my door!{pp}Tell me, what would you have done if {hero} had heeded Leonar―heeded the duke's orders in Balmamusa?{pp}What if he had chosen as I did? What then?{pp}No, stay your answer. I already know. Readily would you have joined in the slaughter! Am I wrong, Catiua!?
{np}Never... He would never...
{np}There are many in Almorica who are as I was, blind to the truth of Balmamusa!{pp}Will you go on deceiving them? How long can you carry on such deception?
{np}As long as need be, if we are careful.{pp}The people care nothing for truth. They need only a story they can convince themselves is true!
{np}You're wrong! Without truth we are lost!
{np}When {hero} told you the truth, were you quick to believe him?{pp}Did you not yet cling to Leonar's tale?{pp}Then as now, you believe only what you want to believe!
{np}Grah! This could have gone better... We withdraw for now!
{np}No going back to Asyton, {hero}! Your route is cut off. There's nowhere to run.
{np}You flee, Vyce? Coward!{pp}I'll chase you to the ends of the earth! You'll never escape what you did in Balmamusa!
{np}{hero}, you were right. I owe you an apology.{pp}My life...my life remains yours to do with as you will.
{np}We should withdraw before they receive reinforcement. Fall back to Krysaro.
{np}We too should withdraw before they receive reinforcement. Fall back to Krysaro.

{np}Ho ho, the Hero of Golyat shows himself.
It's as Vyce predicted.
{np}Had you figured for {hero}'s man. Out scouting all alone? You've courage, I'll give you that!
{np}You should take better care of your friends, lest they fall into the wrong hands!

{np}Who is that knight?
Do you know him, Sister?
{np}Their captive? No. And you've sent out no scouts, have you?
{np}Take him away. We've work to do here.
{np}The ground be your graves, whey-faced Walisters!
{np}To die at a traitor's hands...
{np}I am Sir Folcurt, of the Liberation Front, as it please you.

{np}The Liberation Front.
Cistina belonged to your company.
{np}So it was you, then, who saved Cistina in Rhime?{pp}My comrades have told me of your plight...though I did not expect to come upon you here.
{np}Had you arrived any later, you would not have.{pp}The duke's men are at our tail. We make haste for Rhime.
{np}For Rhime? I'd call that rash. Fatally so.{pp}You stand little chance of penetrating the duke's lines with your numbers.
{np}Yet we accomplish nothing by standing here, wringing our hands.

{np}A proposal, then. As it happens, some friends of mine were taken by pirates.{pp}If you were to aid me in wresting back our ship, I could take you to Rhime.{pp}A suitable arrangement for us both, I should think!
{np}A rather self-serving proposition.
{np}You lack options. I lack men.
{np}Water does seem the more easily tread path.

{np}The pirates are in Qadriga Fortress.
It's not far, and their numbers not many.
{np}Very well. We'll aid you.
{np}You have my thanks.

{np}You trust this man?
Have you forgotten who the Liberation Front are?
{np}You see another way? If we run afoul of the duke's lines, we will die, Sister.
{np}I care not for such coercion.
{np}Be more charitable. He's merely eager to aid his fellows.
{np}Would that I had your faith.
{np}You care for little that does not play out as you see it.
{np}Perhaps.
{np}I am Sir Folcurt, with the Liberation Front, as it please you.
{np}It pleases me not. The Front are nothing but scoundrels, would-be followers of the late King Dorgalua.
{np}I had heard that there were those who opposed Abuna Brantyn, even among the Bakram.
{np}You give a noble dressing to heinous misdeeds, Brother.{pp}The Front's wanton destruction harms only those they claim to help.
{np}You are mistaken, or else misled by our detractor's lies.{pp}We protect the people against Brantyn, Balbatos, and their ilk.
{np}Murderers seldom name themselves so.

{np}Ours is a difficult truth to believe. Take it or leave it, as you wish.{pp}On to other matters. You are the {hero} for whom the Walister Resistance searches, yes?{pp}My comrades have told me of your plight...though I did not expect to come upon you here.
{np}Should've stayed well away if you knew what's good for you.{pp}You'll need more men than that to break what storm and sea have made strong.

{np}Bayin, are you all right?
Steady on, I'm coming!
{np}Why are you returned, Folcurt? Ought to have left me for dead.

{np}Good idea, that.
Waste the old fool!
{np}But spare the women, lads. They'll fetch a tasty price!

{np}Forgive me, Cistina.
You must save...yourself...

{np}We'll meet again, Cistina.
Someday.

{np}You must stop her.
Stop...Cerya.
{np}Veldrei won't be best pleased...
{np}The ship is ours once more. We sail with the tide.{pp}We'll take you safe to Rhime, as agreed. Best get aboard.

{np}Hold, Folcurt.
They've taken Cistina.

{np}What!?
I thought her safely away.
{np}The others are safe. Her alone they took and scurried back to their den.
{np}Surely we must rescue her ere we return to Boed.

{np}Of course. And we shall.
But first we must take them to Rhime.

{np}Foolishness!
You'd as well kill Cistina yourself.

{np}They honored their promise.
I owe them no less.
{np}I thought Cistina dear to you. Perhaps I was mistaken.
{np}Before all else I am a knight, Bayin. I'll not break a sacred vow.
{np}Stubborn mule! If you'll not help, perhaps I can appeal to their better nature.
{np}You heard my tale. Our friend is taken captive by pirates.{pp}No concern of yours, to be sure, but we'll need help if we are to rescue her. What do you say?
{np}Surely there are many others you might call upon. Why do you not do so?
{np}By the time our pleas reached them, it would already be too late.

{np}We are pursued ourselves. Already we've delayed too long.{pp}And have we not kept our word? This fortress is fallen, and your ship is yours once more.{pp}Sir Folcurt has the right of it. It now falls to him to fulfill his part of the bargain.
{np}You'll be safe once at sea. The Walister cannot give chase.{pp}An attack on the pirates now will delay your arrival in Rhime by a scant few days.

{np}Enough, Bayin.
She's right, you know.
{np}Yours is the final word, {hero}. I would hear your thoughts.

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} We will help you.
2. We must decline.
{np}You have our swords. Though we may disagree on much, I find your devotion to your allies admirable.
{np}But, {hero}!
{np}Follow my lead, Sister. The others will understand.
{np}I am in your debt, {hero}. You have a kind heart.
{np}I know where the pirates make their den: Ndamsa Hold on Deknigos.
{np}To Ndamsa Hold, then.
{np}I am sorry, but we cannot lend you our swords. Time is too pressing, and the stakes too high.
{np}What!? Has the whole of Valeria sold its standards at market, then? Bah!
{np}Leave off, Bayin. Our problems are not theirs.{pp}Pay him no mind, {hero}. Off to Rhime, now, before your hunters arrive.

{np}You too, Folcurt? Bah!
If none will aid me, I'll go myself!

{np}Sorry. If that old man were any more set in his ways, I'd need a chisel just to wake him in the morning.{pp}If you're on to Rhime, there's someone I'd have you meet in the fortress at Boed. What say you?
{np}Boed? It's more ruin than fortress. Why go there?
{np}Run-down it may be, but Boed is an essential fastness. Our leader, Cerya, commands from there.
{np}And you would have us meet her, the leader of your Liberation Front? Why?
{np}You will know when we're there. And you will learn of many other things besides.{pp}Now, aboard. I'd like to reach the deep while we still have some light.
{np}We should make for Golyat first―stock up on supplies.{pp}Most of the duke's men muster in the Psonji Weald. The town's defenses should be light.
{np}Good. Oh, and one other thing. I'd like to pay a visit to Boed Fortress before delivering you to Rhime.
{np}Cerya? The same woman Bayin bade us stop with his dying breath?
{np}I've a favor to ask before we make for Rhime. It's Cistina. She's been taken captive.
{np}Taken captive? By whom?
{np}Those blasted pirates made off with her.{pp}No concern of yours, to be sure, but I'll need help if I am to rescue her. What do you say?
{np}You want us to steal into their den and free her, is that it?
{np}Precisely. With Folcurt gone, I've no one else to turn to.
{np}We are pursued ourselves. Already we've delayed too long.{pp}And have we not kept our word? It now falls to you to fulfill your part of the bargain.
{np}Days that may mean our lives.
{np}I thank you, {hero}. You are every bit the young man Cistina said you were.{pp}I know where the pirates make their den: Ndamsa Hold on Deknigos.
{np}To Ndamsa Hold, then!

{np}Has the whole of Valeria sold its standards at market, then? Bah!{pp}Have it your way. The ship is yours.
Off to Rhime with you. I'll save Cistina myself!
{np}Hold your head high. We fulfilled our end of the bargain.
{np}Still...

{np}Come, let's away. There's no telling when the duke's men might arrive.{pp}We should put in at Golyat before reaching Rhime, take on fresh supplies.{pp}The duke's forces still mass in the Psonji Weald―Golyat's defenses will be light.
{np}We should be going. I'll feel better if we're at sea before it grows dark.
{np}We should put in at Golyat first, lay in supplies. I expect the town's defenses will be light.

{np}Agreed.
And then a visit to Boed Fortress before we make for Rhime.
{np}Yes, of course... Perhaps you could stay her hand.
{np}What do you mean?
{np}You'll understand when you meet her. We have hardships of our own, you know.
{np}Now, aboard. I'd like to reach the deep while we still have some light.
{np}At last we've wrested our ship from those vile pirates. We sail at our leisure.{pp}Folcurt promised to see you safe to Rhime. I'll not break his vow.
{np}First to Golyat. We can take on supplies there.{pp}With the duke's men mustering in the Psonji Weald, the city's defenses should be light.
{np}Boed is an essential stronghold. Our leader, Cerya, commands from there.
{np}When you see her, you will understand. We've problems of our own.{pp}We should put to sea at once. If we we're not in the deep by nightfall, the pirates will be upon us again.

{np}Come, let's away.
There's no telling when the duke's men might arrive.
{np}We owed them nothing, you know that. Self-preservation is our foremost duty now.
{np}We stood by as they went to their deaths, Sister.

{np}Save your worry for us. We can mourn the dead when we're safe.{pp}We should put in at Golyat before reaching Rhime, take on fresh supplies.{pp}The duke's forces still mass in the Psonji Weald―Golyat's defenses will be light.

{np}Of course.
You're right.
{np}You're the ones who killed Darza, aren't you. He may not have been much of a man, but he was {pal 16}my{palreset} man.
{np}We've come for Cistina. Return her to us, and I guarantee your safety.
{np}A likely tale, but Darza took no fool for his wife.{pp}You'll not have her back so easy as that!{pp}This one's for the boss, boys! Bring me their scalps!
{np}Defy us and you'll soon rejoin him. Release Cistina at once!
{np}You'll not have her back so easy as that! Darza took no spring maid for his wife.{pp}This one's for the boss, boys! Bring me their scalps!
{np}Cistina... I would have given anything to see you...once more...

{np}You must...save the girl.
Save...Cistina...
{np}You're made of sterner stuff than you seem; poor Darza never had a chance.{pp}But I'm not bested yet. I'll have my revenge.{pp}For Darza, and for the child I carry!

{np}I can't go on.
Forgive me, Darza...
{np}Enough! The battle is over. End this!
{np}Wh...What?
{np}We did not come to fight you. Free Cistina, and our quarrel is past.{pp}End this now―for your child if not yourself!
{np}End it? As you ended Darza, boy?{pp}Peddle your pity elsewhere. I'm not sunk so low.

{np}I did no wrong in killing your husband. It was his life or our own.{pp}I tell you, you are not our enemy save you make yourself so.{pp}Please, sheath your blade. Withdraw your men. We will not pursue you.
{np}I'll not forget this...kindness. Nor what you have taken from me.

{np}Where are you, my love?
Your wife and child...come for you...
{np}That's twice you've saved me―a debt no words can repay.
{np}I feared I'd never see you again. Thank the Light you're alive.
{np}I rejoice to see you. You and Bayin both.
{np}I hate to interrupt, but I think it best we set sail.
{np}Yes. Yes, of course. Best if we reach the deep while we still have some light.
{np}Before we make for Rhime, perhaps you might accompany us to Boed Fortress.
{np}A splendid idea. If we're lucky, we might even reach Cerya in time to stop her.
{np}Boed, did you say? It's more ruin than fortress. Why go there?
{np}When you see her, you will understand. We've problems of our own.

{np}Best get aboard.
We sail.

{np}And you.
But what of the others?
{np}We...we're the only two left.
{np}Then our gambit failed. So many lives lost...for nothing.

{np}Thank the Light.
I thought I'd lost you, too.
{np}"Too"? What do you mean?
{np}Oh. Oh dear...
{np}Sir Folcurt is dead. Slain in an attempt to save you.
{np}Sister!
{np}He died...for me?

{np}Before my very eyes.
Forgive me...
{np}I'm sorry we couldn't save him, Cistina.
{np}Why apologize to her, Brother? She is rescued and unharmed.
{np}What's the matter with you!? Have you no heart?

{np}This is war, Brother.
The Wheel turns. People die.{pp}You would do well to learn that tears will not bring them back.{pp}It is for their sake we must press onward.
{np}And our humanity? Where does that fit in?
{np}Enough. Do not bicker on my account.

{np}Catiua is right.
This is not the time to wax sentimental.{pp}We sail at once. I must reach Boed, and there my sister, Cerya.
{np}Boed?
{np}At least we were able to save you, if no one else.

{np}No one else?
What do you mean!?
{np}Well...you see...
{np}Must we spell it out? Sir Folcurt and Bayin are dead, slain in an attempt to rescue you.
{np}Dead? Both of them?
{np}We stood by, powerless. I'm sorry, Cistina.

{np}Catiua is right.
This is not the time to wax sentimental.{pp}We sail at once. I must reach my sister, Cerya.{pp}I would ask a favor: will you join me at Boed Fortress before traveling on to Rhime?{pp}Boed is one of our most vital strongholds. My sister, Cerya, commands from there.
{np}Right then. Now, let's aboard. We sail.
{np}Sir Folcurt is dead. He died in an attempt to save the old mage.

{np}Folcurt...dead?
How? Why?
{np}Noble to the last, he gave his life trying to save mine. Forgive me.
{np}What's the matter with you!? Have you no shred of empathy?
{np}Must we spell it out? Sir Folcurt, Bayin...they're all dead.

{np}Folcurt...dead?
How? How can that be?
{np}I'm sorry, Cistina. We saw it with our own eyes. There was nothing we could do.

{np}{hero}? Here!?
How did you escape the siege?{pp}No matter. It is enough that the Wheel has brought us together, traitor.{pp}Your bounty is the answer to my prayers.

{np}Forgive me, Cistina.
I...I take my place in the Ever-World...

{np}Soon we...meet again, Cistina.
Soon...
{np}Hear me, boy. You must...stop Cerya. If you don't...no one will...

{np}Cerya, sweet sister...
I'm sorry...

{np}Thirty thousand goth...
So small a sum, to...save my daughter's life...
{np}Who's there!?
{np}Answer well, else it's my bow you'll quarrel with!
{np}Hold, he's a friend.

{np}It's I, Cistina.
Unbend your bow!

{np}Cistina? It is you!
I'd feared the worst.{pp}Chief's been worried, too. Well, come on up.
{np}You heard the man.

{np}Steady on.
He's with us.

{np}It's me, Folcurt!
Unbend your bow!

{np}Folcurt? It is you!
I had feared the worst.
{np}Come on, let's get inside.

{np}Easy.
He's one of us.

{np}Unbend your bow.
Don't you recognize old Bayin?

{np}Master Bayin? It is you!
I had feared the worst.
{np}Come, I'm eager to be within.
{np}Stay where you are!
{np}You're the ones the Walister are after. The Order of {order}, was it?

{np}You have us exact.
My name is {hero}.
{np}And we are warriors of the Liberation Front.{pp}Our mistress is keen to meet you. I would take you to her.
{np}Well, {hero}?
{np}They do not seem to intend harm. Let's see what they want.
{np}You bring wanted men here, to our refuge!?{pp}Might as well tell every crier and herald from here to Almorica where we hide!{pp}So tell me, why {pal 16}have{palreset} you returned?
{np}Be not so quick to anger, Sister. At least hear my tale.
{np}Here, I am not your sister. I am your commander.
{np}I was taken captive by pirates. These people rescued me. I owe them no less than my life.

{np}Pirates?
Did they harm you?
{np}I am well enough, Sister―my pardons―Commander.{pp}As for why I've returned, I've come to stop this madness you call a plan.

{np}A tale long since grown stale in the telling. Squabble all you please, it changes nothing.{pp}You left with those who shared your doubts, did you not?{pp}I do not oblige anyone to take part against his will, else I would not have let you go.
{np}Take part in what? What plans?
{np}It's no concern of yours. I would thank you to remain silent.
{np}They mean to assassinate Duke Ronwey.
{np}Silence!
