{np}Assassinating a single man, even the duke, will not end this struggle.{pp}With no one to tend the Walister rudder, the Bakram will sense opportunity. It will be all-out war.

{np}That is our purpose. Balbatos and the Galgastani now teeter on the brink.{pp}If the Walister are allowed to deliver the finishing blow, they will control half of Valeria.{pp}The Bakram and Walister armies would then be evenly matched―they would break themselves one against the other.{pp}But Brantyn and Ronwey are no fools. They would forge a truce, and all would be as it is now!{pp}However, if the duke is dead, a very different story unfolds. The Bakram would at last invade.{pp}And when Brantyn declares himself hegemon over all Valeria, then...{pal 16}then{palreset} we assassinate him as well.{pp}This isle will be ours!
{np}A great many ifs and whens.
{np}No more than we require.

{np}You've heard our plan. Why not join us? Fight at our side?{pp}You can run, let the duke hunt you, or...you can become the hunter.{pp}Help us cast down the duke, cast down the Dark Knights, and restore peace to this land.
{np}War's horrors are visited not on us, but on the smallfolk caught in the maelstrom.{pp}I want no part in a kingdom built on the bones of the innocent!
{np}You'd best have good reason for this interruption!
{np}A messenger!
{np}Catch your breath soldier, and we'll hear your news.

{np}No, Sister! You must stop this!

{np}What means are left us now that Coritanae has fallen?{pp}We must move swiftly, before the duke rallies the Galgastani remnants to his flag.{pp}If there were another way, its time has passed, Cistina.
{np}No, Sister, you are wrong. You are wrong!

{np}I'm afraid I am needed elsewhere.{pp}While she remains blind to the reckoning of the day, my sister will ever chase her dreams.{pp}Lofty visions are all well and good, but without feet firmly upon the ground, you will drift.{pp}If my sister refuses to soil her hands, the moment will slip through her fingers.{pp}...Much as it has for you.

{np}War's horrors are visited not on us, but upon the smallfolk.

{np}You truly expect the people to forgive you for this?

{np}What means are left us now that Coritanae has fallen?{pp}We must move swiftly, before the duke rallies the Galgastani remnants to his flag.{pp}If there were another way, its time has passed, Folcurt.

{np}I'm afraid I am needed elsewhere.{pp}While he remains blind to the reckoning of the day, Bayin will ever chase his dreams.{pp}Lofty visions are all well and good, but without feet firmly upon the ground, you will drift.{pp}If he refuses to soil his hands, the moment will slip through his fingers.{pp}...Much as it has for you.

{np}I lost much less at Balmamusa than did her people. What's your business with us?

{np}What sort of exchange?
{np}You will aid us, and in return, I will clear your names in the tragedy of Balmamusa.
{np}How?
{np}We set a plan to motion―a plan that should interest you.
{np}Nothing that might lead to more slaughter of innocents is to our interest.
{np}Do you think us barbarians? We are revolutionaries, yes, but we do not love war!
{np}We mean to assassinate the very man who has placed a price upon your head: Duke Ronwey.
{np}Yes. When the duke is dead, you will profit―if you join us.
{np}You truly think the people will forgive you this?

{np}What means are left us now that Coritanae has fallen?{pp}We must move swiftly, before the duke rallies the Galgastani remnants to his flag.{pp}If there were another way, its time has passed, Catiua.
{np}You are barbarians in truth. Barbarians flying a false flag of peace.{pp}You rival the duke and Balbatos in love of bloodshed!

{np}I'm afraid I am needed elsewhere.{pp}While she remains blind to the reckoning of the day, Catiua will ever chase her dreams.{pp}Lofty visions are all well and good, but without feet firmly upon the ground, you will drift.{pp}If she refuses to soil her hands, the moment will slip through her fingers.{pp}...Much as it has for you.

{np}My sister is wrong. There must be a better way.{pp}If we choose ends over means, we are no better than the demon Brantyn and the duke.{pp}Is that what you have been fighting for, Sister? A country with roots steeped in blood? I cannot believe it.

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} Come with us, Cistina.
2. You chase a dream...
{np}Join us. We're your people now.
{np}In truth, I've felt a kinship with you from the time we met.
{np}Then fight with us!
{np}I shall. And I will cling to my dream, even if that should lead me into opposition with my own sister.
{np}We must consider our needs before our ideals, Cistina.
{np}Was it not ideals that turned you against the duke's massacre?
{np}Perhaps, but I've since awakened to the need for practicality.

{np}Are you so weary of flight from headhunters that you've let slip your convictions?{pp}...Understood. I shall consider this a painful lesson and part ways.{pp}Farewell, for I do not imagine we will meet again.
{np}And to you, Cistina.
{np}I've never seen her so hellbound.
{np}What will you do?
{np}No point in rotting away here. I suppose I shall gather a band and venture forth again, in time.
{np}Why not join us?
{np}Aye? I'm Bakram, if you haven't forgotten.

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} We have no quarrel with you.

{np}Our fight is not with you, sir.
{np}There are others who will not see it so, though I thank you for your offer.
{np}I see. May the Wheel turn for you, then.
{np}And for you, {hero}. I will listen for word of your exploits in days to come.
{np}I bear no enmity for the Bakram. Only for those who would drive our clansmen toward chaos.
{np}Perhaps together we can guide our people true.
{np}Her heart was once so...gentle.
{np}What will you do now?
{np}I think it is perhaps the Great Father's will that I fight no longer. I will away, far away.
{np}You could come with us.
{np}Aye? I'm Bakram, if you've not forgotten.
{np}Our fight is not with you, mage.
{np}Behold! A new day breaks to rouse us from our long, troubled sleep!{pp}A time of nightmare, oppression, and darkness ends with the death of this man!
{np}The blade's too clean a death! Let him feel the Walister's pain!
{np}Why does his blood still pump warm while my son lies in the earth! Die, Galgastani demon!
{np}To hell with you, ogre! Your death is new life for Galgastan!
{np}Hear that, Balbatos? Even your clansmen bear you no love.
{np}Be done with it.

{np}Quiet, quiet. Brave Walister clansmen. I hear your cries all too clearly...{pp}For they are my own!{pp}Galgastani friends!{pp}Know that all suffering, yours and ours, flowed forth from this man.{pp}With his blood, let us wash away all bile and rancor. Let his life pay the debt upon our hearts.{pp}Walister and Galgastani stand as one. War is ended!
{np}Child of the Great Father, Son of Philaha. Have you any last words?

{np}War is...ended? 
Ha! Fool.{pp}It was not I who started this war. All of you took up arms with me.
{np}Despicable! Even with your last breath, you seek to place the blame upon these people, your subjects?

{np}I pity you, Ronwey. We are more alike than you can know, sitting behind our castle walls.{pp}We talk much of how the world should be, yet never stoop to dirty our own hands. That's what knights are for, is it not?{pp}Yet as much as you tell yourself the people are yours, you are wrong.{pp}They do not dance upon our palms. It is we who dance upon theirs. Mark my end well, Ronwey, for it will be yours.
{np}That's enough of that. Do it!
{np}They kill me now because they tire of war. What cause will they proclaim when they kill you?
{np}Silence... No one's here. It's all right, Sister. You can come out.
{np}Xapan!
{np}A fortunate encounter! The Wheel turns for me!
{np}If not for us. I'd have happily grown old never having seen your pock-marked mug again.
{np}Ah now, no need to be so sour. If you only got to know me, you'd find me quite amiable.
{np}Amiable when luring us into a trap!
{np}No, no trap. Just luck!{pp}Now, to claim that head of yours before any saintly knights happen along with different ideas. Get 'em!
{np}I misstepped at Rhea Boum, but I'll make no such errors this round!
{np}Why not show some sense. Retire before it's your head rotting on some pike.
{np}Almost worth it, if my head could rot next to yours!{pp}Take my hand, lass, and I'll lead you to a better place.
{np}I'd sooner throw myself down before the host at Almorica! You...{pp}You'd show me more mercy to gouge my eyes than force me to look upon those bearded jowls!
{np}An alluring angel, plucking at the strings of my heart!
{np}You spoke of knights.{pp}So you knew not only that we made for Rhime, but our purpose withal.
{np}Aye. Perhaps it comes as no surprise that we're here on Almorica's coin.{pp}See, with their Galgastani problem done for, they're all eagerness to see you done for as well.
{np}An eagerness Lanselot does not share, apparently.{pp}Why else would they hire you lot?
{np}Aha! The lad is more than just a pretty face!{pp}Still, it changes nothing. I'll have your head, and I'll have it now!

{np}Now why couldn't you just lay down arms and come along nicely?{pp}Ach, I suppose you wouldn't be worth the bounty then, would ya? Heroes...bah!{pp}I can see why the duke wants you nailed to a post.{pp}If the Wheel had spun another way, hells, it might have been you paying my coin.
{np}We've no hope of prevailing against the duke's men, not yet. We must withdraw!

{np}What?
What was that?
{np}Take the town!
{np}No more! Is this what passes for honor in Lodis?
{np}You bear the arms of Xenobia... So this is the Holy Knight Lanselot!{pp}How I have longed for this moment!{pp}Show me the power that crushed Hyland!

{np}Only too gladly!
Let our steel sing!
{np}Come out, Xapan! Where are you hiding!?
{np}Here, {hero}!
{np}Catiua! Where―!?
{np}Up here!
{np}Greetings, {hero}! So close, so very close. Almost slipped away on me.{pp}Your sister will be joining my merry band. If you care to see her again, hasten to the walls of Almorica!
{np}No...Xapan! Don't do this! Coward!
{np}Did your mother not warn you against playing on the streets at night, boy?
{np}Gildas!?
{np}Dark Knight of Lodis! Your quarrel is with me!
{np}What's this? A Xenobian wants to fight? I'll gladly meet you, if you've even strength enough to draw!
{np}Pick up your feet, lass!
{np}Go, {hero}! Swiftly! Follow them!
{np}As imprudent as you are impudent. I'll dress you like a holiday goose, hedge knight!
{np}I said go!
{np}But first, a venomous strike to take the fight from you!
{np}Hnnngh!
{np}{FF 9C 0101}{FF 8D 0102}{FF 85 0101}Coritanae Keep{FF 99 01c9}
{np}I can't steal a moment's peace... What now?
{np}It's the Bakram, Your Grace. They've marched on Rhime!
{np}What? That's absurd!
{np}Our riders send word that the battle is already joined.
{np}What news of the city? Has it fallen?
{np}No, Your Grace. The Xenobian knights have managed to hold her walls.{pp}But they cannot long last against the Bakram siege. They've requested immediate reinforcement.

{np}Very well.
Summon Leonar!
{np}Begging Your Grace's pardon, Sir Leonar rode for Almorica at daybreak.
{np}Yes... Yes, of course.{pp}Bring quill and parchment. Leonar must know of this.{pp}Ready the fastest courser in Coritanae!
{np}At once, Your Grace!
{np}What is Lodis scheming, eh?
{np}With Balbatos gone, old alliances turn to ash.{pp}Confound them all!
{np}Here he is, sure as the wind. I half worried the Bakram had got the best of him.
{np}So this boy is the hero-butcher of Balmamusa, is he?
{np}Xapan, you coward! What have you done with my sister?
{np}You know what's to be done, then.
{np}Aye, well enough. I don't give a fig for no bounty, long as his head rolls.{pp}I had old friends at Balmamusa. They'll rest better with him beneath the earth.
{np}Pardon the parley, {hero}. Had a few matters needed tending.{pp}Your sister's safe and sound within the castle. But you'll not be leaving with her, exceptin' by force.
{np}By force, then.
{np}Ramidos, hear me. You have Balmamusa wrong!

{np}That you, Abuna?
Feh. Thought you kept better company.{pp}A man of the cloth abetting in such...carnage. But then the Church has never shied from a good blood-letting, has it?
{np}It was Leonar and the duke who slew the people of Balmamusa, not us or the Galgastani.{pp}I swear it in the name of the Great Father!

{np}You clergy are all alike. Invoke the name of god and expect the people to follow you like sheep.{pp}Balbatos and Brantyn can scarce void their bowels without speaking Philaha's name.{pp}Well I'm not having any of it! Your god is just another faerie tale!{pp}Tell me, what god would visit war on his people? And a holy war, that's the richest of them all!{pp}I may not believe in gods, but the devils who brandish their steel before me are real enough!

{np}I would rather have lived out my days in a cottage with my grandchildren. They weren't much younger than you, boy.{pp}But the war took my sons and their sons. I joined the Resistance to end this madness.

{np}So did we all. Nor have I forgotten the suffering we have endured.{pp}If I could better the lives of the Walister through battle alone, I would fight till my last breath.{pp}When the duke named me Hero of Golyat, I thought it might somehow further our cause.{pp}But the duke uses men as a cattleman uses his kine―quick to slaughter when his hunger needs sating.{pp}How can you not recognize him for the creature he is?
{np}You're quick to blame the duke, but what about yourself?{pp}What would you sacrifice to sate YOUR ambition?{pp}How many of your companions would you send to their deaths to save your sister?
{np}I would never wage war for my own profit!
{np}Surrender and give the lie to my words! Or do you value your own life above your companions?
{np}Ramidos, please, you must listen!
{np}Arycelle? Now this is a surprise. I thought you dead.{pp}But it's not like the Thunder Maiden to betray the Resistance over a pretty young face, hero or no.
{np}The massacre was the duke's plot. I had it from the lips of his own men!{pp}{hero} tried to stop them. He's innocent!
{np}If it is as you say― Leonar lied to us?
{np}I know. I didn't want to believe it, but I can no longer deny the truth.
{np}Have the years robbed me of my wits?
{np}That's three times you've bested me, boy!
{np}If Xapan thinks I'll abandon my sister, he's sorely mistaken.

{np}I...I didn't know.
I was too quick to judge.{pp}The spirits have...told me everything. Forgive me, {hero}.{pp}The Wheel finally...comes round. With luck, I'll find my sons waiting.
{np}Fat lot of good she was, the mealy old hag!
{np}I'm coming, Sister.
{np}Vyce? Here?

{np}You...you can't!
We were allies!
{np}Fool. I know the proper use for a hostage.
{np}Uagh!
{np}You're next, {hero}.
{np}What have you done with Catiua?
{np}Unhand my sister!
{np}Oh, I will. But first, you and I have a score to settle.
{np}There must be some other way. Hear me out―

{np}Talk, talk, talk.
Let our steel speak!
{np}Vyce, it doesn't have to end like this!

{np}Ever since we were boys, you could do no wrong.{pp}They lavished praise on you while I looked on, forgotten.{pp}Is it because of our fathers, do you think?{pp}The son of a respected abuna and the son of a loutish drunkard.{pp}It was a relief when he died. {np}This is...this is a fantasy! You're my friend.
{np}What became of that friendship?
{np}Did I hide my hatred so well? I was never your friend.{pp}How I envied you! Your father, the good abuna. Your sister, all beauty and grace.
{np}Catiua thinks of you as a second brother.
{np}If you could only hear yourself.{pp}You've always been the one she cares for. Not even your father was good enough for her.{pp}You're the only one she trusts―the only one she loves!
{np}No...it's not too late. Whatever you may say, I was a friend to you. And I would be so again.
{np}I want no betrayer for a friend!{pp}The duke and Leonar have placed their faith in me. They are friends enough.
{np}They only use you. When you've outlived that usefulness, they'll throw you to the wolves!
{np}You have it the wrong way round. I am using them.

{np}Enough of this!
Stay your blades!
{np}But he's good as dead!
{np}Easy, Vyce! Our circumstance has changed.
{np}But it was you who ordered his death!
{np}Stop talking and listen! You'll want to hear this too, {hero}.

{np}Rhime has fallen.
The Bakram will soon be here.
{np}But Sir Lanselot―
{np}Dead. Fled. I know not.{pp}But we no longer have the luxury of fighting amongst ourselves.{pp}{hero}, you must join the duke!{pp}What's done is done. Our true foe stands before us!

{np}Have you gone mad?
He's a traitor!
{np}Enough, Vyce. Did you hear nothing I said?

{np}I know why it is you fight, {hero}. You dream of a world free of war and hatred.{pp}A worthy dream, and reasonable. But reason alone cannot move men to act!{pp}Is that how you want this to end? Will you let your father go unavenged?{pp}Join us. If not for yourself, then for the Walister!

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} You're right, this is no time to fight.
2. You know I can't do that.
{np}The Bakram are our true enemy. We must work together if we are to stop them.
{np}Good. You see the truth of it. I expected no less of our young hero.
{np}You've both gone mad! I'll take no part in this.
{np}Vyce, wait!
{np}Let him go. We must away to the duke.
{np}Vyce... Damn him!
{np}I'll never rejoin you. You're no different from the Bakram.{pp}You are beaten. It is you who chase a dream!
{np}What now? Do you go on trying to bend the world to your will?
{np}I'm not so arrogant as that. But I will show our people there is another way!{pp}I believe they can rise above this...pettiness.

{np}While we walk the earth, there will ever be conflict.{pp}A man will kill another over a husk of bread if not restrained!{pp}It falls to us to rein in these base creatures and bring order to the world.{pp}They crave a master to lead them, to give them purpose.

{np}There is truth in your words, but still I mistrust them.{pp}I don't know what to believe...{pp}Why do I fight?
Why do any of us?
{np}Perhaps you will understand in time. These are demons you alone can face.{pp}Now go, {hero}. Take your sister and leave this place!
{np}What are you doing? You can't just let him leave!
{np}Go. See the world as it is and dispel your doubts.{pp}Search the isles―search all the world―you will not find what you seek.{pp}When your hope has died, come back. I'll be waiting.
{np}You'll wait a long time.
{np}Let him go. He must come to us willingly, or not at all.
{np}We may regret letting him live.
{np}Should it come to that, I'll put him down myself.

{np}No.
Let it be me.

{np}{FF 9C 0101}{FF 8D 0102}{FF 85 013d}Am I so naive?{FF 89 3d}
{FF 8D 0102}{FF 85 013d}Do I know so little of the world?{FF 98 0105}

{np}Galgastan... I heard.
Another culling.

{np}Just as the duke planned.

{np}Though my blood be not true, it does not lessen my love for the Walister.{pp}In the end...which is more important?{pp}I can never forgive the duke.{pp}It is for warriors to die on the battlefield.
{np}Ravness...
{np}You must...save the Walister. Light their way...
{np}Ravness? Can you hear me? Ravness!
{np}{hero}... Build a new home...for our people.
{np}I hear no alarum, Sister. I think we made it.
{np}By the look of things, the Galgastani can't have stationed many men here.{pp}The fewer we must kill to be done with this business, the better.
{np}You would have me fight such a battle with our numbers? Are you gone mad?
{np}I mislike your tone.
{np}Forgive me, Your Grace. We are more powerful now than ever, I grant you.{pp}But let us not forget, we failed to rouse the Galgastani against Balbatos. Our Resistance remains far outmatched.
{np}I do not need you to tell me what I know so well.
{np}Then I beg you to reconsider.

{np}Humor your duke.
Hear my plan before you reject it, hmm?{pp}First we dispatch a light force to secure Balmamusa, a small town southwest of Coritanae.{pp}Thence to advance to the Xeod Moors.
{np}You'd distract them by needling their flank? They will never fall for such a ruse.
{np}Your ears would serve me better than your tongue...{pp}I mean to have our young hero lead the band.

{np}We will feed sweet lies to their whisperers: that it is no small band, but half our army that marches.{pp}A morsel they will find impossible to resist.{pp}Nor will they know whether it is from Almorica or Balmamusa that we strike.
{np}And they will believe this tale?

{np}The presence of the Hero of Golyat will convince them. Balbatos would not think we place our hero at the head of so few.{pp}This will be enough to give Balbatos pause, but he is no fool. He will not commit the entirety of his forces to Balmamusa.{pp}No, he will divide his men between the Psonji Weald and the Xeod Moors.{pp}The martial advantage is his. Even with his forces split, he will not fear defeat.{pp}Yet only this way will we have a true chance at victory.
{np}Perhaps. But if Balbatos does not split his troops, what then?

{np}We must see that he does.
There's more.

{np}Once our heroes have a foothold in Balmamusa, they will turn their attentions to the port of Asyton.{pp}Asyton is but a short distance to the west of Coritanae. Balbatos will fear an assault.{pp}And with his troops mustering in Coritanae, Asyton will be ripe for the taking.
{np}Of course. Without Balmamusa or Asyton, they'll be cut off from the sea.
{np}Is that so great a blow?

{np}In Valeria, the sea is life. Without the bounty of her trade, we wither and die.{pp}Doubly so the Galgastani in their landlocked keep at Coritanae.{pp}Believe our rumors or no, they must respond. And that means splitting their troops.
{np}Should the gambit fail, we still weaken them by closing their ports.
{np}And what becomes of us?
{np}If you sense disadvantage, withdraw swiftly.
{np}So in the end, we still must fight a battle of Galgastan's choosing.

{np}You fret like an old maid, Leonar.
The plan is perfect.
{np}As you say, Your Grace.

{np}Forward!
Leave no Galgastani standing!

{np}The Xeod Moors are within our grasp.
Onward.

{np}{hero} of Golyat?
I see a rumor in the flesh!{pp}Then Balmamusa was no feint after all. Ha!
{np}You there. His Eminence must hear of this. Go! Now!
{np}We must halt their advance as long as we can. Remember, we fight not for ourselves. We fight for Galgastan!
{np}Only your blood can pay the price for those you've slain.
{np}Then we share a grim cause. But I bear you no malice; it is war makes us enemies.{pp}And as enemies, we must fight!

{np}The simple reasoning of youth!
I expected more than that.
{np}The hatred I bear for you is anything but young. I carry on the struggle of my father, and his father before him. I am the wrath of the Walister!

{np}The struggle of your father... That's cause enough to fight.{pp}Cause we share. The roots of the conflict between Galgastani and Walister do run deep.{pp}But you must look past your hatred to see your true foe. The sins of the father trap the son.
{np}And what of you? Do you not harbor some hurt that drives you to fight?

{np}I'll not deny I do.
My twin brother, Orba―you killed him.
{np}I...I did not know.
{np}Say nothing. There's nothing to say. It was the will of the Wheel he die at your hands.

{np}I said only your blood could atone, but I was wrong.{pp}We must set aside the wounds we carry if there is to be any true atonement.{pp}It is with this knowledge that I fight...but I do not expect you to understand. You are yet young, naive...common.
{np}Not so naive that I am blind to the wounds you carry.

{np}Forgive me. Fault is most difficult to see in oneself. Let me be your mirror, then.{pp}So long as there is vengeance in your heart, your victories will turn to ash.{pp}But you must know this only too well, Butcher of Golyat!

{np}If only I had heeded...my own advice.
It is I was naive...foolish.
{np}I do not fight for vengeance.

{np}The Butcher of Golyat!?
Here?{pp}If he means to lay siege to Coritanae from our backs, we dare not leave the keep undefended.
{np}You, bring word of this to Sir Xaebos. Impress upon him the need for reinforcements!

{np}Forget the others―it's the boy I want!
We'll mount his head on the walls of Coritanae!
{np}I thought myself prepared for death, but now I find...I'm frightened.
{np}Is this town the prize you've come for, rebel? Best think again.{pp}Galgastan gives no quarter to an ogre who slays his own!
{np}May the Light judge our enemies...and embrace our fallen.

{np}Very well. Give the order.
Tomorrow we attack with the dawn.
{np}At once, Your Grace.

{np}I beg you wait, my duke.
It's too soon!
{np}Oh? Balmamusa is fallen, is it not? The plan proceeds apace.
{np}But we still do not know whether Balbatos has divided his troops.
{np}Even as we breathe, {hero} takes Port Asyton.{pp}My plan unfolds as I have seen it. Why do you worry so?{pp}The gods of Valeria are with us, Leonar. You'll see.

{np}I do not question our success, but surely there is no harm in awaiting word from Port Asyton.{pp}It is not only our lives that hang in the balance, but the destiny of the Walister race. Prudence demands caution.

{np}So I am imprudent {pal 16}and{palreset} reckless?
You talk a perilous line, Leonar!
{np}Your orders, sire?

{np}You have them.
Go, and see that they are carried out!
{np}As you command.
{np}Please, Your Grace!
{np}That's quite enough from you! Begone from my sight!
{np}...As you wish.
{np}Look again. It is you who've fallen into our trap, fool of a Galgastani!

{np}Galgastani? No.
Your work in Balmamusa brings me here!
{np}You were in Balmamusa!?
{np}Such fine heroes we Walister make... You will die for what you did at Balmamusa―for what you did to my brother!

{np}We cannot fight amongst ourselves!
You play into the enemy's hands!

{np}I know your part in the massacre.
Do not deny it!
{np}My brother had hurt his leg... He couldn't even walk.
{np}You know what happened. Then know also that we had no choice.{pp}Had we fought the Galgastani openly, there could be only one outcome.{pp}There was no other way to bring our people together!

{np}Our people? This is a war fought in the name of power, not people.{pp}The nobility want it, and they will crush whomever they must to have it.{pp}Don't you see? You're no better than the Galgastani or the Bakram.{pp}If it's absolution you seek, look elsewhere!
{np}I never wanted power. Only a future for the Walister!

{np}You ignore the will of your people―slaughter them―and call it revolution!?{pp}Who do you think it was first fanned the flames between clans, then pointed at the bonfire as proof of conflict? The nobility!{pp}Better the rams rise to lead the flock than such shepherds with miters for crooks and crowns for caps.{pp}And you...you are little better than the yapping sheepdog that does his master's bidding.{pp}To hell with you. To hell!

{np}Arycelle? Is that you?
Don't you recognize me?

{np}Abuna Donnalto?
Why are you here?{pp}I thought you a man to keep better company than this.
{np}The Galgastani torched my abbey. I have been a member of the Resistance ever since.

{np}What of Karl?
What of my brothers and sisters?

{np}They have passed into the Light.
There was nothing I could do.
{np}And for this... For this you joined in the massacre at Balmamusa!?
{np}Sydney... He's truly dead?
{np}You should know―you killed him!

{np}I didn't know he was in Balmamusa. I didn't...
What have we done?
{np}Crippled as he was, he clung to the leg of a soldier, begging him to stop the slaughter.{pp}Your Resistance cut him down where he lay.
{np}Please, Arycelle, you must listen. We were there, in truth, but we took no part in the massacre.

{np}Excuses! You watched in silence when you could have stopped them!{pp}The Galgastani murder our children, and you seek to right this with more slaughter?{pp}I looked up to you once, Abuna. But I can never forgive what you've done!
{np}Hatred begets hatred. Vengeance demands vengeance... I've been a fool.
{np}Feh... Retreat! We retreat!
{np}As for you... You will die with or without my hand.
{np}We'll deal with your kind once the hierophant lies in the ground.
{np}Oh, hadn't you heard? Your duke lost at Psonji!
{np}Peddle your lies elsewhere. We're not buying!

{np}'Twas a victory of attrition decided by a handful, but a victory for Balbatos nonetheless.{pp}More than enough to sound a death knell for your Resistance. The people will turn to us to lead them now!

{np}I do not believe it. I cannot!
Did Balmamusa mean nothing...?
{np}Sister, let us take this ship for our return to Almorica.{pp}If that woman spoke true, the roads will be too perilous.
{np}{hero}... Let us quit this island altogether!
{np}Cut and run? You can't be serious!
{np}If what she said is true, then we are finished whether we admit it or no.{pp}They'll kill us if they catch us.
{np}But we must return to Almorica to see the truth of it ourselves. No?
{np}...Here is the truth of it.{pp}I would not lose you, {hero}!{pp}There is a mare that visits me nightly, a dream in which I am alone, brotherless.
{np}Only a dream, Sister. As I stand here now, I will never leave your side.
{np}And yet it frightens me as though I saw it in waking. I...I cannot live alone.
{np}You won't have to. Don't worry, the duke hasn't lost, I'm sure of it.{pp}All will be revealed at Almorica.{pp}And if we find the castle fallen, then we will leave this island. Together.
{np}Promise me we will. Promise me.

{np}Who are you!?
You got no business with us!
{np}Ahhh, come to steal my prize, is it? Can't be lettin' you do that.{pp}5,000 goth on this one's head, and I'm keen to collect!{pp}There's knifework to be done, lads. Gut 'em!
{np}You're a rare breed of bounty hunter.
{np}Bounty this, bounty that...I'm just a mercenary.{pp}And you, you're not from these isles: feathers the wrong color. The mainland, is it?

{np}Yes, as it happens.
A mercenary, like yourself.{pp}Not in over your head, by any chance?
{np}Old Xapan, in over his head? Ha! I'm tempered in a hundred battles.{pp}When I stare death in the eye, death blinks. It'll take more than a handful of pirates to do for me!
{np}Good. I like a challenge!
{np}Of all the luck.
{np}A pirate's death...for me.
{np}A tight scrape, that. Don't think I'd have made it on my own.

{np}The pirate―he mentioned a bounty.
Who are you?

{np}No criminal, if that's what you're thinking. I'm a Walister, same as you.{pp}Hired on with the Resistance, but my boss man died on the Psonji Weald 'fore I saw a single goth.{pp}Any road, I must've left an impression on the Galgastani. They went and put a bounty on my head.

{np}Then it's true.
The Resistance lost in Psonji.

{np}Plenty dead on all sides. I reckon both armies are headed home to lick their wounds.{pp}But don't worry, the duke's alive.{pp}Way I see it, he owes me some coin. I'm off to Almorica to collect.{pp}Say, you're not headed that way are you? If you need another sword, you can hire mine for a song.

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} Why not?
2. The risk is too great.
{np}We could use all the help we can get.

{np}It's a deal, then.
And don't forget your part of the bargain, eh?{pp}When we reach Almorica, be sure and tell the duke you hired me on. We'll throw it on top of what he owes me.
{np}A wanted man in our midst might draw unwanted attention.

{np}Now that's a pity.
I thought we'd get on like geese on bread.{pp}Be seein' you round then.
{np}I had hoped to avoid the attention of the Resistance and the battle that must follow. Alas...
{np}High Commander, we'll assay to hold them here. Withdraw to Psonji.
{np}A Galgastani commander turn his back upon the enemy? Never!
{np}No, m'lord Gatialo. You cannot throw away your life here. Galgastan needs you alive.{pp}Return to our holdings at Coritanae, there to reform our lines.
{np}You are but a band of arkhiatros. They'll crush you!
{np}We are prepared to die. We have always been so.{pp}Besides, you're in no condition to fight. You wouldn't reopen wounds so freshly closed and ruin our work, would you?
{np}Then I shall take especial care not to die.
{np}Let down your guard at your own peril, Walister! We are proud warriors of Galgastan, and we will fight to the last!
{np}Care, {hero}. That Gatialo is danger!

{np}Well, if it isn't old Gatialo!
Fancy seeing him here!
{np}You know him, Xapan?

{np}Aye, he's a commander in the Galgastani army, a real goadsticker of a man. As feared as he's respected.{pp}Worse, it was him what pushed for Balbatos's blood war.{pp}My band ran afoul of Gatialo's lines at Psonji, and they hewed us down like scythes to grass.{pp}His kind would kill Walister for sport. Best give that one a wide berth.

{np}So it ends, Commander...
Run. Live... Avenge us!
{np}The killing of soldiers is one thing, but to slay arkhiatros with such abandon... You reaffirm my convictions.{pp}The Walister are a plague upon this land, a blight to be burned away!

{np}Hngh... Base Walister r-runt...
You besmirch the glory of Galgastan!

{np}No...
A true hero of Galgastan has died today.
{np}Walister devils! I will visit this pain in my heart upon you sevenfold!
{np}I've marked well your faces, Walister. Next we meet, I shall mount them upon pikes that all may see!
{np}Now, to buy m'lord as much time as we can.
{np}My hands have healed many. Now...they rest.
{np}I am heartened by your return. As you live, so too does the Resistance.
{np}What do you intend to do after such a defeat?
{np}Defeat? Nonsense! Psonji was a stalemate!{pp}All that's lacking is the coup de grace. I will muster a new host and march on Coritanae.
{np}And where will you find the men for this...host?
{np}What do you propose instead? Hmm? If you're sitting on some great stratagem, I would hear it.

{np}Balbatos suffered losses as great as ours at Psonji. This is fact.{pp}But do not forget, {hero}'s feint required that Galgastan hold considerable forces in reserve.{pp}If he were to strike now, we would be hard-pressed to repel him.{pp}What's more, ever since Balmamusa, we've suffered an endless stream of deserters.{pp}We cannot fight a war without soldiers.
{np}If I held a dagger at Balbatos's throat, you'd complain of its dullness!

{np}Not complaints, Your Grace.
Simple facts.{pp}One thing to talk of bringing down Balbatos, but idle musings bring us no closer to victory!

{np}All talk, am I?
Impudent knave!

{np}Enough of this.
This is no time to quarrel amongst ourselves.
{np}We must turn to the Dark Knights Loslorien for reinforcements.
{np}What? You can't be serious! This is some species of madness!

{np}The decision is made.
It is the only way to bring down Balbatos.

{np}By begging for reinforcements, we all but admit defeat.{pp}Again you would vassal us to the Bakram.{pp}Were it to become known, our ranks would dwindle further. Even those under watch of our walls would take flight.{pp}You would drive them into the waiting arms of the New Walister Alliance.{pp}I will not lend my name to this...this suicide!
{np}Still I wait to hear how {pal 16}you{palreset} would deliver us!{pp}No, forget I asked. I've heard enough of your counsel.
{np}What does our young hero make of this? It's you I must persuade.
{np}Well...

{np}Will you not venture to Phidoch Castle?
Convey my missive to Tartaros?

{np}Your Grace!
You must rethink this!
{np}It is not your place to tell me what I must and must not do. Begone from my hall!
{np}The future of the Walister rests on your decision. Will you go?
{np}As my duke wishes.
{np}Hold up, there!
{np}Why the urgency? The duke paid you, no?
{np}Aye, and then some! Said there was more where that came from if I'd join you.
{np}I'm pleased for you. But you needn't come with us.
{np}Eh, why's that now?
{np}Our path leads to danger.

{np}This messenger's errand?
What danger in that?

{np}Remember our safety is at the mercy of the Dark Knights Loslorien. Galgastan is as eager to prevail as we.{pp}They may have sent their own messengers to persuade the knights from their perch and onto the battlefield.
{np}True, that. If the knights have joined against us, you'd be walking into the lion's den, as it were.
{np}Indeed. Yet we're bound to see how the lion lays.{pp}You have your coin. You only place yourself in needless peril by joining us.
{np}Ha! Hard to argue with that. But I'll join you all the same.{pp}Where there's peril, there's reward!
{np}A soldier with a merchant's heart, I see! As you like then. I'll not stand between a man and his profit.
{np}You're {hero}! The "Hero of Golyat," they call you?{pp}Hrm. Something tells me I won't be recruiting you.
{np}You must be part of the New Walister Alliance. We share a common cause.
{np}Cause? You abandoned our cause when you drew steel on your kinsmen, traitor.

{np}Listen up, boys! That one there's the Hero of Golyat!{pp}Slaughtered the people of Balmamusa like cattle, he did. All to slake his thirst for power!{pp}You going to let him and his bloodthirsty lord rule us into the grave?{pp}I didn't think so!
For the Alliance!

{np}You're Catiua, sister to {hero}, are you not?{pp}Oh, he has forsaken you, truly! Power is the prize in his eye now.{pp}But you, you know better. You know strength can push away as well as it pulls closer. Does the duke's army not bleed men by the day?{pp}If you have the best interests of the Walister at heart, you will leave {hero}'s side and service!

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} Who are you?
2. Who do you think you are?

{np}Your face is not known to me.
How do you know mine?
{np}Oh, it matters little what I know. What matters is what {pal 16}we{palreset} know.{pp}Your brother is a danger to his own people. And to you.
{np}Why should I listen to anything you have to say?
{np}Because I say only what you already know. In his heart, {hero} has abandoned you!
{np}Don't listen to him, Sister! I stand, as always, by your side!
{np}What is your business, and how do you know who I am? Your words sit very ill with me, I'll have you know.
{np}Ah, er, yes, well...
{np}Well what? If you've aught to say, say it!
{np}Y-You see, ma'am, we seek to build a society free of the repression v-visited upon us by the ruling elite!

{np}Well said.
Go on.
{np}S-See, your brother, {hero}, he's but a c-clinging cretin, wagging his tail for the duke!{pp}Thinks maybe the duke will throw him a bone...some land or a title, perhaps, eh? And you'd follow him?
{np}I follow one thing only: my heart.{pp}And my heart tells me to remain by {hero}'s side. Valeria be damned!
{np}I see...
{np}You...are not the woman I'd heard you to be. Go on, follow your heart 'fore it melts. It's made of ice.
{np}And fire, which you forget at your peril!
{np}Well...that could have gone better.
{np}Why such hurry, {hero}?

{np}Sir Lanselot is here, Sister.
Come.
{np}Must we greet him so short of breath?

{np}Sir Leonar? What are you doing here?
Where's Lanselot?
{np}I wished a private word with you, and Sir Lanselot was good enough to oblige me.
{np}Why such secrecy?
{np}It is a matter of grave importance.
{np}The Resistance teeters at the edge of the void.{pp}We lost a great many men in the battle at Psonji, and each day we lose more to desertion.{pp}Why do you think that is?
{np}I can't say.
{np}It is our leadership, or lack thereof.
{np}We were defeated at Psonji because we rushed into battle too soon.{pp}We moved before the enemy's forces were fully divided, and see where it has led us.
{np}Already we hasten toward a greater error.
{np}If we place ourselves at the mercy of the Dark Knights, we betray everything for which our kinsmen died.
{np}Think you not so?{pp}Until now I have been patient. Too patient, perhaps.{pp}Triumph over Galgastan is more distant than ever. Walister rots from within.
{np}Our Resistance needs a new leader.{pp}I believe you are he!
{np}You can't be serious!

{np}The duke has played his part.
It falls to us to draw the curtain.

{np}This is madness!
Do you have any idea what you're saying?

{np}Only too well, Catiua.
Your brother sees it, too.
{np}You would murder the duke, a man you swore to honor. I'll not believe it...

{np}Sister...Leonar is right.
If we continue down this road, the Resistance is finished.{pp}Those who gave their lives at Balmamusa will have died for nothing.{pp}We must win this war, whatever the cost. The duke is lost already.

{np}Night and day, soldiers desert the duke's army. The people love him not.{pp}But you? You have accomplished much, you have the people's trust...and the vigor of youth.{pp}Yes. The people will see the brightness of our future in you.{pp}We could ask for none better to lead!

{np}This is absurd!
My brother is no leader!

{np}Well, {hero}?
I say you are.

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} Yes. This is my calling.
2. I could never replace the duke.
{np}If this is what our people need of me, so be it.

{np}This jape has gone too far! Do you truly think the people will follow the man who slays their duke!?{pp}Always you trust to steel for deliverance, but where has it led us?{pp}We are beaten! Accept this, and let us quit this island.

{np}No. Not yet.
Our battle is far from over.{pp}Someone must bloody his hands. If there is none other with courage to do so, let it be me.

{np}Well said, {hero}. You are a man grown now, and the role well suits you.{pp}When you act, the people will follow―the failings of the duke are hardly a secret.{pp}But the people will not know where this new road leads. They lack the vision to see.{pp}They will turn to you to shepherd them. To be their courage― Ah, but there will be time for talk later.{pp}We must return to Almorica and strike before the duke realizes aught is amiss.
{np}I leave the chore of ruling to the rulers. I am no leader of men.
{np}Nonsense. You've led your company as well as any knight I've known.
{np}Please, torment my brother no further. He is ill prepared to lead the Resistance entire.
{np}Forgive me. It was never my intent to force your hand. It is enough that you are with me.{pp}Come, we must return to Almorica and strike before the duke realizes aught is amiss.
{np}A poor replacement for the duke I would make. Look at the blood on my hands.
{np}The blood of Galgastani. You fought only guards at Balmamusa.{pp}The sins of that day are mine to bear.
{np}I stood by as men and women were slaughtered. Is there no sin in that?
{np}These horrors touch you less than you think. Your heart is still pure.
{np}Then I will speak on it no more. It is enough that you are with me.{pp}Come, we must return to Almorica and strike before the duke realizes aught is amiss.
{np}Who would have thought we'd meet again like this?

{np}Vyce?
What are you doing here?
{np}I had hoped the good knight Lanselot might lend me his aid, but alas, he's nowhere to be found.
{np}You need only give the word, Vyce!
{np}Calm, Arycelle. A quarrel now would only leave our strength diminished.
{np}But they are the backbone of the Resistance. We must strike while we can.
{np}Gousin said much the same thing, and now he feeds the worms.
{np}Arycelle...how did you come to be here?{pp}Vyce, you don't mean to― You wouldn't!

{np}Not to worry, Catiua.
Our enemy is elsewhere.
{np}Yours, perhaps, but I do not forgive so easily! I will avenge you, Brother!
{np}Damn that woman! It should not have come to this.

{np}Call off your men, {hero}! A fight between us serves no purpose.{pp}The duke who pulls your strings―{pal 16}he{palreset} is the enemy!{pp}He cares nothing for liberating the Walister. He thinks only of the kingdom he might build for himself.{pp}It is he who plays each clan against the other. He who sacrifices the blood of his kinsmen!{pp}Anyone who ignores the will of his people and uses them as a means unto an end is my enemy!{pp}Who knows all the duke has wrought better than you, {hero}!
{np}Quite a speech. But it is your actions that concern me, not your words.{pp}What can you know? You, who ran from the truth!
{np}It was you who ran, not I!{pp}You talk of revolution, but revolution without principles is meaningless!{pp}What happened to the old {hero}? Has lust for power blinded you to the damage you do?

{np}Always so quick to judge, Vyce, so impatient for results.{pp}A mountain is climbed in steps, but you expect to vault to the top in a single leap!{pp}Can't you see that what I've done―what I do―is vital?

{np}What you've done is treason.
I'm sorry it's come to this.
{np}I would not have thought to find you in league with the New Walister Alliance, Vyce.
{np}In league, Catiua? The New Walister Alliance is my creation.
{np}Of course... No wonder Gousin knew so much of me.

{np}You remember our life in Golyat? Miserable as it was, you had your brother. I had nothing.{pp}But I don't hate my father for it. It wasn't his fault.{pp}When I saw what happened at Balmamusa, I finally understood. It is men like the duke who bear the blame.{pp}These so-called noblemen play the smallfolk against each other to avert our watch from the true enemy.{pp}Balbatos and Brantyn are no better―clergy and nobility are two sides of the same false coin.{pp}Both want only a docile flock to rule.
{np}Gone is the quiet boy I knew, too timid to speak his mind.
{np}I know you, Catiua, like your brother cannot. He'll never understand your true spirit.
{np}And you do?
{np}Deny it if you will, but you know it in your heart. I'm not like him.
{np}Frankly, I care nothing about who you are or what you do.
{np}I know. More's the pity.
{np}Still with this flock, bird-man?
{np}You're rather loose with your tongue for a man about to die.
{np}And looser still with my coin―how much to switch sides? I'll make you a sweeter offer than the duke ever did.
{np}No deal. Even you should know a mercenary's true currency is trust, not coin.
{np}Oh, but it's more than that, no?{pp}I know what it is that keeps men like you with {hero}.
{np}Aye? Then you should join us. The rewards of friendship are far richer than the spoils of war.
{np}Friendship is in rare supply these days.

{np}I walked away from a friend once. Seems an age ago now.{pp}And over what? Some trifle I scarce remember. Foolish to let such a small thing drive us apart.{pp}At the time, I never wanted to see him again, let alone fight at his side.{pp}But even without words, true friends have a way of understanding one another.
{np}You're rambling, old man. Your point?
{np}Whatever may come between you, in time, it will pass.
{np}You have all the wisdom of a dusty old tome, and the charm to match.
{np}And you rise to the bait like a spring trout. Ha!
{np}Your lust for power will be your undoing!

{np}Arycelle, the anger and vengeance in your heart are my doing. I'll not deny it.{pp}Nor will I beg your forgiveness. There is no forgiving what I have done.{pp}I ask only for time. And when it has passed, gladly will I give my life to you.
{np}Time? To do what?{pp}I can well imagine. You hope to atone for your sins.{pp}But no atonement will restore life to the dead. Nothing can change what you've done.
{np}No, nothing can wash away my sins. Still...
{np}Yes?
{np}You helped me see the anger and vengeance clouding my judgement.{pp}I know now that true victory is won in the heart, not on the battlefield.
{np}Your meaning escapes me.
{np}As it must, for now. But in time, you will understand.
{np}Forgive me, Brother. I have...failed you.

{np}Arycelle!
No!
{np}I didn't expect the Bakram attack to come so soon.{pp}And you, the duke's loyal, scarce equipped to march, let alone repel them!
{np}If the Bakram expect us to lie down for the trampling, they're in for a nasty turn!
{np}What, you have a plan?{pp}No matter, I'll see soon enough. But there's little time.{pp}If you've some miracle on hand to rally the Resistance, best work it quickly.
{np}I will. When next we meet, it will be as enemies full-fledged, Vyce. Stay whole till then.

{np}And you, {hero}.
Until next time.
{np}Your Grace, I bring terrible news! {hero} rises against us in revolt!

{np}What!?
Impossible!
{np}I am not certain of his numbers, but they are likely more than these walls can bear.{pp}We could send for our host on Tynemouth...but I fear it would arrive too late.
{np}Bah! The commons were right about him, it seems. He is a traitor to the core!
{np}Your Grace, it's not safe for you here. Please, go while there is still time.
{np}Go? Fool. Where would I go!{pp}No, the key is the boy. Kill him, and this ends!
{np}M'lord.
{np}The cur bites his master's hand, eh?
{np}Betrayer! Whose creature are you? Balbatos? Brantyn, maybe?{pp}Are you blind to the army at our gates? You place us all in jeopardy!
{np}I am no lord's creature! I seek only what the Resistance has always sought!{pp}Our ranks dwindle by the day! Can't you see it?{pp}The people no longer follow the duke!
{np}And so they follow you? Usurper! They say Heaven's justice is swift, but you deserve far swifter!

{np}Fool boy... I curse you...
With my dying breath, I curse you!
{np}We're going in, press the attack! Spare any who've lost the will to fight!

{np}Traitor to the Resistance! How quickly you forget your debt to the duke.{pp}Your kind are thorns in the heel of progress―how fortunate I bear the perfect remedy.{pp}My sword will teach you the right of things! Advance!
{np}You may have stopped me, but...our uprising will not die...so easily.

{np}Your Grace.
Sir Leonar has arrived!
{np}Leonar? Here? Perhaps there is yet hope.
{np}Your Grace, my humblest apologies for not coming sooner. Not hanging from the parapets yet, I see.
{np}No, good friend. But that rebellious upstart would be the first to see me so, no doubt.
{np}If he fails, the Bakram will have their chance soon enough. Rhime has fallen.
{np}Leonar!? But...why?

{np}Your Grace bears too great a burden.
Let me lighten your load.
{np}Listen well. I want no needless bloodshed. Make a path out of the castle, and drive out those who resist.
{np}Sir!
{np}Sir Leonar! What of the duke?
{np}All went according to plan, thanks to your effort.
{np}Then the duke is no more.

{np}Yes...
And all that remains is for you to join him!
{np}What!? What are you doing!?

{np}Something that would have been impossible were it not for you.{pp}You die, taking responsibility for both the revolt and the death of the duke, and the Resistance rallies to me.{pp}Truly, you have my undying gratitude, {hero}.
{np}You really think my death will accomplish so much?

{np}How could it not? Death is the ultimate absolution, and you have much to atone for.{pp}―Mostly {pal 16}my{palreset} sins, but no matter. You've played your role.{pp}Rest. Your days of sacrificing heart and soul to the Resistance are over.
{np}Venomed words―don't listen to him!{pp}It's as Vyce said. Leonar and the duke are the same: men, drunk on power!

{np}Respect, please!
I am twice the man he was.
{np}Rise, {hero}! This is not your place to die! I...I forbid it!

{np}I am sorry...
You will live on in my heart.

{np}Stand and fight, {hero}!
Have you forgotten your promise!
{np}You, Vyce? What are you doing here?{pp}Ah, I see. Old friends reunited. Very well. You can die together!
{np}Respect, please! I am twice the man he was.
{np}Now to restore the Resistance. Raise your sword, {hero}!
{np}I thought you different from all the rest, Leonar. But you love the nobility as much as they love themselves.
{np}If the nobility can provide a fairer rule, then they have my devotion.
{np}A fairer rule under the same despots? You dream if you think the nobles will serve as their own headsmen!

{np}You mistake me, Vyce. If a man wants power, he must claim it for himself. No noble will do that for him, true.{pp}Yet most commons wait for such a man, a savior to put things to rights. Whence this savior, then?{pp}Why not people like you―like me―the few who take up the sword to better their lot in life. They can be the next nobility, shepherds to the rest.{pp}And where the wrong in that? I know you desire change, but such is forged slowly, link by link, not made whole in the span of a night.
{np}You talk much of power, but what of honor?{pp}What possible claim to virtue could you make over {hero}'s disgraced corpse!

{np}I fear you lack sufficient dedication to understand. It is my dedication to a cause that trumps all such fleeting considerations.{pp}The man who wallows in sentiment accomplishes nothing. That is what it means to bloody your hands, boy!
{np}You forget whose blood it is!
{np}Vyce...thank you.
{np}Our paths crossed by chance. That's all.
{np}Be that as it may, I still thank you.
{np}Vyce, Arycelle...thank you.
{np}Fortunate for you that an even greater menace faces us both.{pp}I sheathe my hatred of you for the sake of the people, for now. Do not expect to find me so charitable next we meet.
{np}Leonar, put away your weapon! I do not wish to fight!

{np}Still clinging to some hope of reconciliation, you simpering waif? Know I will strike without hesitation!{pp}If you wish to live, if you wish to change this world on your own terms, then slay me!{pp}Fail, and only the worms will remember you.
{np}You leave me no choice!
{np}Gak... He's tough.
{np}Arycelle, withdraw!
{np}As you say.
{np}{hero}! I value my hide too much to throw it away here.{pp}It's up to you now. Live, so that Valeria will know what he's done.
{np}Brother...I come to join you.

{np}No, Arycelle!
She deserved a better death than this.

{np}It's over.
Well fought, {hero}.{pp}Go on, finish it.
Tell our people... Tell them this:{pp}It was my scheming brought us here.
{np}Did you intend this all along?

{np}Either death, yours or mine, serves to unite the Resistance.{pp}Though in truth, I had much rather it been yours. Ha.{pp}We harbor none of Vyce's nobles or their pets now, do we?{pp}The New Walister Alliance will...will join you. Welcome them.{pp}My eyes...grow dark.
My limbs numb.{pp}All rests on you now. You have the strength... You have the strength.
{np}The road to Coritanae is long. Why take her all that way?{pp}She's for the gallows at any rate. I say we have done with it here and now!
{np}Orders is orders. Commander Loxaerion is to have a proper hearing before her justice is meted out.
{np}And is it not some opposition nobleman who spares her?{pp}Why do you suppose they go to such lengths to keep her from harm?
{np}They say there's Galgastani blood in her. Might be that blood is bluer than most.
{np}Then her crime is twofold, for she is a kinslayer besides!{pp}I see no Galgastani before me―only a Walister knight!
{np}The Walister name me a Galgastani traitor, while the Galgastani claim I am a Walister knight.{pp}Enemy to all and friend to none.
{np}The Galgastani can't so much as escort a prisoner without a quarrel. No wonder the country splits in two.
{np}Silence her!
{np}I'll have a much easier time guarding you if you would guard your tongue.{pp}It'll mean my neck if I don't bring you back safe to Coritanae.
{np}Sir Alfred, it's the Walister!
{np}Now's my chance...

{np}What?
How!?
{np}Is that...Ravness?
{np}Damned woman!
{np}She's sealed her own fate. We've cause enough to kill her now.{pp}Kill kinslayer and rebels all!
{np}If you mean to seize me as a traitor, then do so. Else return to your duties.{pp}Tarry here too long and your master may wonder at your absence.

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} You are a friend, then?
2. I cannot leave you here.
{np}My lady, the Resistance hunts you, yet you act as a friend to us. Why?
{np}If you name "friend" only those who follow you blindly, then I am no friend of yours.
{np}A simple answer would have sufficed.
{np}The cards seldom give us simple answers, do they.{pp}But I will offer you this: so long as we share a common foe, I will not raise my sword against you.
{np}Wherever your loyalties lie, I cannot simply leave you to your fate.
{np}Not words I'd expect from a man with the blood of Balmamusa on his hands. But still only words.
{np}Believe me or not, as you will.
{np}He speaks plain enough. Perhaps the horrors of that day have wrought some change in him.{pp}I think I shall see for myself.

{np}If I fall now, all comes to nothing.{pp}I will not die here!
I must go on!

{np}Ravness!
They didn't hurt you, did they?{pp}When I heard the Galgastani had captured you, I feared the worst.
{np}Abuna Donnalto... You speak with such sincerity, I half believe you're worried.
{np}I deserved that. I've not forgotten the way we treated you at Balmamusa.{pp}But believe me, I want only to save you.
{np}To save me, you say? Well, I do believe you, actually.{pp}Only I wonder... What form this salvation?
{np}I do not think to mend the wound in your heart, but I can help save your life.{pp}And where there's life, there is always hope of salvation.
{np}I turned my back on my country... For what?
{np}Ravness, no!
{np}When a dog turns on its master, it must be put down!
{np}I let her die...{pp}She was no enemy, but a woman true and just. What have I done?
{np}Should have...killed her while I...had the chance.
{np}What do the Galgastani want with her...and she of them?
{np}I suppose I should thank you.{pp}Even if you lead me away a traitor, I owe you my life.
{np}Are you a traitor?
{np}She has Galgastani blood in her. Is it any wonder some tie remains?
{np}You speak as though she betrayed the Walister outright, Sister.

{np}Only words. Though no doubt there are others who share her thinking.{pp}Those who claim that, fearing for my life, I struck a deal with the Galgastani, who were only too willing to embrace one of their own.{pp}And there is some kernel of truth to it.{pp}I doubt even those Galgastani nobles who do not take so hard a line as Balbatos would have offered me shelter were it not for my blood.{pp}But in the final lay of the cards, I am a woman without a country.
{np}I'm sorry.
{np}I had always told myself I was a Walister, and I acted the part as best I could.{pp}But this... I am shaken to the core. I no longer know what I am meant to be.
{np}Ravness, come back with us. Warriors of your skill are in short supply. We could use you.
{np}I am cheered to hear you say so, but I...I can never go back.{pp}I cannot forgive the duke for what he did at Balmamusa...nor the disgrace I suffered there.
{np}I see.
{np}But my gratitude is heartfelt. Both for saving my life...and for setting me free.
{np}The duke wants her captured. Can we really just...let her go?
{np}Leave it be, Sister.

{np}You may find it hard to believe, but I love the Walister.{pp}I was born in Almorica―spent my childhood there. It will always be my home.{pp}Even now, I do only what I feel best for the Walister people.{pp}Farewell, {hero}. Perhaps we'll meet again someday.
{np}Are you certain this is the right choice? What if she joins forces with the Galgastani?{pp}Should you face her on the battlefield, it will not go easy for you.
{np}If she becomes an enemy for true, I will face her as any Walister soldier would.{pp}Do not worry, Sister. All will be well.
{np}Come, let's be off.

{np}What am I to do with you, Barbas? Hmm? One cannot deny your insubordination.{pp}To act without leave of the high champion is strictly forbidden, whatever the circumstance.{pp}Time and again you were ordered to return, and each time you've ignored your orders!{pp}Only now do you deign to grace these halls. I am galled.
{np}Galling, yes, the obstinate lout. Go on, beg forgiveness.
{np}You talk too much, Martym. And I have an ill temper.
{np}What was I to do? Deny the regent? Impossible.
{np}We do not answer to Brantyn!{pp}Speak true. You learned that the Xenobian knights were in Rhime and sought to do battle. Is it not so?

{np}Enough, Balxephon.
What's done is done.
{np}Welcome back, Lord Commander. I see Ozma and Oz accompany you.
{np}What word of the Walister?
{np}They rally their troops on Golborza, yet they do not make to march.
{np}I should think not. The duke has but a tenuous grasp on Galgastan.{pp}Dispatch an envoy. Explain our position to the duke and renew our vow to remain unaligned.
{np}And the Bakram? I cannot imagine the regent sits idle.

{np}Brantyn will be made hierophant, his age-old wish fulfilled. If that does not content him, nothing will.{pp}Controlling the isles is not our mandate. Nor can we afford the Xenobians to perceive elsewise.{pp}If we are to avoid giving them cause to intervene in Valeria, we must shun the sword in favor of the olive branch.{pp}So long as we are the advocates of peace, they dare not act. Is that clear, Barbas?
{np}...Aye.
{np}I'm sending you to Heim.
{np}But Heim is leagues from the front!

{np}Steady, Barbas. I do not intend for you to serve as castellan for the regent, if that is your fear.{pp}Abuna Prancet was being held in Heim Castle. Unfortunately, a band of rebels saw fit to free him.
{np}The work of the Liberation Front, no doubt. Regardless, I would prefer our true task remain secret.

{np}Mannaflora's whereabouts elude us, and now the abuna, the only man who might know, has gone missing as well.{pp}Barbas, I task you with a mission of utmost import. Recapture Abuna Prancet, whatever the cost.
{np}Yes, Lord Commander.
{np}The two of you are to deal with the Liberation Front. Too long have we suffered them to move unchecked.
{np}On the honor of House Glacius, my brother and I will see it so.

{np}Common rabble.
They'll be little trouble.
{np}Andoras's search for Mannaflora is to continue.{pp}You and Martym are to proceed with our negotiations with the duke.
{np}As my lord wishes, so shall it be.
{np}What part of the Galgastani have joined our cause?
{np}Half their men, perhaps a little more. Another third have deserted.
{np}Hmm. Then the rest are loyalists who will cleave to Balbatos unto the bitter end.
{np}Few as they are, they were the backbone of his army. The best of the best.{pp}Their support in the crofts and villages runs deep. They'll not fall easily.
{np}Who better to see that they do. Spare not a moment.
{np}It shall be done.
{np}The Bakram show no sign of moving farther south. There's solace in that.{pp}Perhaps some faint breath remains in our pact with the Dark Knights.{pp}Let us send another envoy and remove all doubt.
{np}And you, my Hero of Golyat, are to hunt down Vyce Bozeck, who fled behind the enemy's line scarce a month past.
{np}Must we avenge ourselves upon him?

{np}You do not understand the creature you hunt. Indeed, he must seem a strange species to you.{pp}You and I share common conviction, however different our methods and means.{pp}Else why would you have returned to my halls?{pp}Vyce is different. He fights not for convictions or ideals but out of some base bloodlust.{pp}Unguided by higher philosophy, he acts without thought.{pp}Judged by your measure, he is useless―and how that must enrage him!{pp}Now he thrusts this rage at you, his onetime friend, a hero to all the world.
{np}I had held out hope that Vyce might return this past month.{pp}But too much time has passed.{pp}Were we to wait any longer, we risk him becoming a grave threat to our Resistance.
{np}But to put a price on his head... Is that not going too far?

{np}It pains me, truly.
But it is the needful course, Catiua.
{np}Will you say nothing in his defense, {hero}?
{np}Do not look for Vyce to return. Not while I'm still here.
{np}As ever, my words fall on deaf ears.

{np}Fine.
Do as you like.
{np}Catiua!
{np}Let her go, {hero}.
{np}Then we are agreed?
{np}Ah, I'd nearly forgotten. Sir Mirdyn has returned.

{np}He has?
Were there any others?
{np}He and Warren. That's all.{pp}Warren suffered a grievous wound. No doubt a visit from you would do much to cheer him.
{np}The men stand ready, Sir Leonar.
{np}I'll join them with all haste.
{np}{hero}, let's away. I know this sits ill with you, but it is our duty.
{np}I make my offer one final time. Answer me, and your lives will be spared.{pp}Who leads your band of stragglers, and where is he? Your answer!
{np}You may take a Galgastani knight's freedom, Leonar, but never his pride.{pp}We do not sell friends, not even for the unkindest price. Would you do any different?
{np}I suppose I wouldn't. Very well.
{np}Then...

{np}Then we shall hold a public execution... However!{pp}In deference to your honor, we will not bind you, and will furthermore arm you as befits your former station.{pp}If you truly desire freedom, fight for it!
{np}Clansmen of Galgastan!{pp}Tell our wives and children of how we died here today, of our last service to our homeland!{pp}And tell them to avenge us!
{np}Words in the wind, soldier! Our ears are deaf to your cries.{pp}We know you who pledged fealty to Balbatos are the true blight upon this land.
{np}Glory...to Galgastan.
{np}Your leader's sword lies silent. Will you fight on?
{np}Then justice has been served. Those surviving will join our ranks from this day forth!{pp}We will show them that Walister do not scorn those who embrace our cause!
{np}Your leader's sword lies silent. I would ask that you sheathe yours.{pp}No more lives need be taken here today.

{np}Good. Then this brutal bloodshed ends now. The survivors will join our ranks, and we will treat them as brothers.{pp}Soldiers of Walister, understand that we must clasp hands, not swords, if we are to know peace.
{np}Canopus!

{np}And {hero}, too!
I am glad to see you both well.
{np}And you, Sir Mirdyn.
{np}How is he?
{np}The Star Seer remains lost in the mists of sleep. But he draws breath and is whole of body.
{np}That is well, then.{pp}And Lanselot and Gildas? Have they not returned?
{np}I've seen neither since the night of the Bakram attack.
{np}It was Sir Gildas who saved me from the Dark Knights' swords that night.
{np}Would that I had been warrior enough to return the favor...
{np}I am sure both will return unharmed. And besides, there was little you could do.{pp}...I hear you search for Vyce. You know where he makes his den?
{np}No, but there is a price on his head.{pp}Not many places where a wanted man can hide.
{np}He would have to go to ground―or well under it―to hide from both the Resistance and what remains of the Galgastani.

{np}Aye. As we were leaving Rhime, I received report that a company led by an unnamed Dark Knight had taken to the highroad.{pp}A commander he was, called to Heim to help defend the town from partisans.
{np}Of course. These partisans must be the Liberation Front.{pp}They intend to strike the fortress at Boed, I'm sure of it! If Vyce should be there...
{np}They'll have his head in a sack by the morn!
{np}We ought make for Heim at once, {hero}!
{np}How will you ride, Mirdyn?
{np}With your party, of course.{pp}{FF 92}{hero}, I know you serve His Grace, but I also know you would not leave Vyce to die an ignoble death.

{np}Good.
Let us ride.
{np}{FF 9A 03}You received a White Knight's Mark.
{np}Sir Mirdyn, it is good to see you well.{pp}Tell me, how fares Warren?
{np}That's some relief, then.{pp}And Lanselot and Gildas? Have they not returned?
{np}Then I must go at once!
{np}Wait. I will ride with you.
{np}I know you serve His Grace, but I also know you would not leave Vyce to die an ignoble death.
{np}Gave us quite a chase, Abuna, but now it's back to Heim for you.
{np}Godless woman. You...you killed them all!

{np}Our work is done, Oz.
We withdraw.

{np}Hold, Sister.
I've another prize: the leader of the rabble.
{np}Bring her forward!
{np}Slew every Bakram soldier that marched with us from Rhime, this one did. A real firebrand.{pp}But she doesn't hold a candle to you, dear sister.
{np}Kill me and have done with it!
{np}Cerya! You live!
{np}Forgive me, Abuna. This is not how I meant to meet again.
{np}You've no cause to seek forgiveness. It is I who have troubled you.
{np}If you see my father, tell him his daughter met an honorable death.
{np}Is this touching melodrama played out?
{np}Take him away.
{np}Think not on the grave, Cerya. Live. And know they dare not kill me.
{np}What do you plan to do with her, Oz?
{np}She'll make a fine gift for the high commander, I should think.
{np}Oh? I recall no order to take her alive.{pp}Besides, look at her.{pp}She'd sooner choke on her own tongue than go a willing captive.
{np}Her eyes give the truth to your words.{pp}What am I to do with her, Sister?
{np}You rely on me too much, little brother. Decide for yourself.
{np}Such bile. So be it. But where to begin?{pp}{FF 92}Darkest lords of Vuira Viou, grab fast these legs and drag them down!
{np}You've a wicked streak, Oz.{pp}Enjoy your games, but don't tarry too long.
{np}Run, if you can.{pp}Name your conspirators and the location of their fastness, and I'll spare your meager life.
{np}Damn! We're too late!
{np}Cerya! We're coming!
{np}Feh, I've drunk my fill of these Walister dregs. A Dark Knight's work is never done.

{np}Cerya!
My dear sister!
{np}A sister? I'll be sure you're close at hand to watch your sibling draw her last breath!
{np}Why have you come back, Cistina? Leave this place while you can!{pp}You walked away from the Liberation Front. This is not your battle!
{np}I've come to save you, you ungrateful fool!{pp}I cannot bear to lose my sister. And the Front cannot bear to lose its leader.
{np}Senseless blather. The Liberation Front is dead.{pp}We hacked its body to bits with our swords. Only the head, such as it is, remains.
{np}Front or no, while we draw breath, our deeds can yet change Valeria!

{np}Cerya!
Are you unharmed?
{np}More vermin come out of the woodwork? This place teems with you rabble!
{np}Why have you come back, Folcurt? Leave this place while you can!{pp}You walked away from the Liberation Front. This is not your battle!
{np}You might show a bit more gratitude to a man who's come to save your life.{pp}Regardless, you'll not be so easily rid of me. The Front is oathsworn to aid those in peril.
{np}So long as we have friends of like conviction, we will never fall to you!
{np}I never thought to see you captured by the likes of these scoundrels. You disappoint me, Cerya!
{np}You! Old man! You know this woman, do you?{pp}Ah, another of her rats, no doubt.
{np}Why have you come back, Bayin? Leave this place while you can!{pp}You walked away from the Liberation Front. This is not your battle!

{np}This is no time for posturing, Cerya. We've come to save you.{pp}What matter the difference in our banner or philosophy?{pp}Our ends are the same, if not our means. Did we not start this battle to save the lives of our kinsmen?

{np}Have you not eyes to see the warriors before you? You've killed nothing!{pp}Fell one group, and another will rise to take its place.{pp}If a lasting peace you seek, you will leave these isles and never return.

{np}Your father, {hero}.
He...lives.

{np}My father...?
What? How!?
{np}You must...rescue him from the Dark Knights. Your father knows... He knows.
{np}Cerya!
{np}Cerya, no!
{np}You're a formidable lot. Still rabble, yet perhaps not so common.
{np}Now that you know your enemy, you would do well to lay down your sword. To do otherwise is to throw yourself upon it.
{np}You dare threaten me, baseborn knave? How I hate these wretched isles and all who dwell upon them!{pp}You squabble over Valeria like beggars over scraps. The sooner she is rid of you, the better!
{np}Show him no quarter!
{np}If you had an inkling of all this world encompassed, you would know the piddling place you held in it.{pp}But you do not, and so are your isles forever mired in blood and death!
{np}You and your kind brought this war to our shores!
{np}No! You have summoned us here. We come to quiet the storm.{pp}We bring order where there is chaos―peace where there is war!
{np}Do all knights of Lodis mantle themselves in such twisted truths?

{np}The dwarf lectures the giant? Ha! You are more fool than I thought.{pp}Lodis is a land of kings! Think you we care about the scraps of some unruly rabble?{pp}What can you know, you who hasten toward your own destruction? Destroy yourselves as you like, but do not visit your ruin upon us!
{np}You there! Dark Knight! Do you always justify your own misdeeds by finding fault in others?
{np}The listless drawl of a Xenobian... You must be Canopus. We encountered your countrymen at Rhime.
{np}How...?
{np}Any truth to the rumors that you were driven from your homeland? Such a sad tale.{pp}What's this now? The color has fled your cheek.
{np}If you set out to anger me, job's done. I'll carve you like a roast!
{np}You would make a poor mummer, Canopus.{pp}I see you for what you truly are.
{np}Let's hear it then.

{np}Once, in a battle, you weighed duty against friendship...and friendship won. You renounced the sword that day.{pp}So why do you play these piteous islanders false?{pp}You act the plain-spoken man to divert them from Xenobia's true intent!
{np}A fair speech for so foul a tongue. Tell me, are all knights of Lodis so long-winded?{pp}Just as well for you to savor your last words, I suppose.
{np}Your kind ever were an ignoble lot. Pity my sister is not here. She would have pleasured in your death.
{np}It's a dark day sees the likes of you...get the better of me.
{np}Where is my father? Why did you take him from Golyat?
{np}So you're the...abuna's boy...
{np}It's a dark day sees the likes of this rabble...get the better of me.
{np}My friends may be lost, but my battle is not over.
{np}{hero}...your father, Abuna Prancet. He lives.{pp}We held him safe in our care until a short while ago.

{np}What? How...?
Where is he?
{np}The Dark Knights left with him just before you arrived.
{np}Why would they bestir themselves over one man?
{np}The Dark Knights care nothing for who rules the isles.
{np}{hero}, it is your father, Prancet Pavel, whom they seek.
{np}What could they possibly want with him?

{np}I know little more than you. But I can offer one piece of the puzzle.{pp}They seek someone―or something―called Mannaflora. Whatever it may be, they are bent on finding it.{pp}And there is but one man who knows where it is.
{np}My father.
{np}Your father holds the key to this war.
{np}Is it possible―was he the reason they attacked Golyat?
{np}You had best leave. There's no knowing when they might return.
{np}And what will you do, Sister?
{np}I...I mean to help Abuna Prancet.
{np}Alone? Foolishness! What can you hope to accomplish?
{np}She'll not listen to me. Perhaps you can dissuade her from this madness!
{np}Madness is a bit...well, yes. What if you were to come with us?
{np}I am sorry, but I will not serve under a duke who sanctions the slaughter of innocents.{pp}Besides, I have my own duties as head of the Liberation Front.{pp}I owe it to our fallen to carry on.
{np}Sister...
{np}Look after Cistina for me.
{np}Our father is alive... I must tell my sister!
{np}Why would the Dark Knights go to such lengths to capture one man? It's absurd.
{np}They care nothing for who rules the isles.{pp}It is your father, Prancet Pavel, that they seek.
{np}And what do you intend, Cerya?
{np}I...I plan to help your father.
{np}Alone? You can't be serious! What can one person hope to accomplish?{pp}Join us. You know it to be the wiser course.
{np}I understand.
{np}My thanks. I could ask no more.
{np}Father lives... I must tell Catiua!
{np}Then you're telling me we don't know where Bozeck has gone?
{np}That's right, my lord. Nor did the Dark Knights give any indication they knew.
{np}This business with the Dark Knights―why did you engage them?
{np}I...I don't understand, my lord.
{np}You knew full well that Galgastan had not yet been brought to heel.{pp}But still you slew a commander of the Dark Knights.
{np}We can ill afford to make an enemy of them now.{pp}You were tasked with finding the renegade Vyce Bozeck, were you not?{pp}Better to have left that rabble rouser to fend for herself!
{np}I...I couldn't...

{np}Enough.
What's done is done.
{np}Dispatch an envoy to Phidoch. There is yet time to settle this with ink and quill.
{np}Yes, my lord.
{np}Further, we will raise the price on Bozeck's head to 10,000 goth.

{np}We cannot suffer him to come and go as he wills.{pp}With a bounty so high, he will think twice before making his presence known.{pp}As for the rest, it is in the hands of the headhunters.{pp}Our foremost concern is rooting out what followers of Balbatos remain and securing Coritanae.
{np}To which end, I want you to travel to Asyton.
{np}To find these followers of Balbatos?

{np}Difficult to say. We know only that you face a formidable foe.{pp}We've not heard from one of our companies stationed in Asyton for some time now. We believe they are responsible.{pp}What's worse, the casualties were not limited to our soldiers. Many smallfolk have turned up dead as well.{pp}Our response must be swift, decisive. I wish for you to lead it. I trust I may rely upon you?
{np}...Yes, my lord.
{np}Splendid. You're to leave at once.{pp}Oh, there was one other thing. Scarce more than a rumor, in truth.
{np}We are told that a man matching the description of the Xenobian knight Sir Gildas has been seen in Asyton.

{np}Sir Gildas?
What would he be doing there?
{np}Took fright and fled from Rhime, no doubt. Bloody coward.
{np}Sir Gildas is no coward!

{np}Silence!
I'll not have you at each other's throats!
{np}Go to Asyton. Send back word of what has happened. I know our hero will not disappoint.
{np}Sister, wait!
{np}What does the great hero need of me?

{np}Please, don't.
You're still upset, aren't you.
{np}If you have no urgent need, I'll be on my way.
{np}It's Father. He's alive!
{np}What?

{np}So he lives.
What now?

{np}What now?
We rescue him! What else?
{np}Even if he is no true father to us?
{np}I mean we are orphans, Brother. He is not our father. Not by blood, at any rate.
{np}No... Who told you this? It's a lie! It must be!
{np}It is no lie. I overheard him talking about it once, long ago.{pp}In all the world, you're the only family I have.
{np}Why tell me this only now?
{np}Because you're leaving me.
{np}Leaving you? Scarce a moment goes by we are not at each other's side!{pp}And so it shall remain. I will never leave you.
{np}There is the lie!{pp}Someday, you will cast me aside as you did Vyce!
{np}No, Sister.
{np}I'm alone without you...
{np}I remember you, boy! The Wheel brought us back together, has it? Someone up there must like ol' Ganpp.{pp}Obda! Berda! To me!
{np}You're well acquainted with Berda and Obda, but I been brewin' something special for just such an occasion!{pp}Banga! Zanga! To battle!
{np}Time to repay His Eminence's kindness. Today you feed on the rich stew of vengeance!
{np}Obda! What have they done to you! Your sorrow is my strength!
{np}Berda! My sweet Berda! Your anger feeds my own!
{np}Forgive me, Banga! Your soul will live on in me!
{np}They'll pay dear for this, Zanga! My heart ain't so gentle as yours!
{np}Piss and blood! The day is theirs!
{np}Next we meet will be the last! I won't forget what it was you done here!
{np}The Balbatos loyals fell upon them at Tynemouth. A tenacious lot, I'll give them that.{pp}We lost near twenty men uprooting those who had gone to ground in the city.
{np}What business is it of his? Why are you here, Hero?{pp}Come to aid the hierophant's men as you did the partisan rats in Boed?
{np}Enough.
{np}But he is a traitor!
{np}I said enough!
{np}Forgive her, {hero}. She speaks in anger.
{np}Hmph.

{np}I hate to part so soon, but I fear I must.{pp}They've taken captives and holed themselves up in Qadriga Fortress.{pp}I douse one fire, only to have ten others kindle in its place. No rest for the weary, eh?
{np}Do not let her words dishearten you, {hero}. I know you for the man you truly are.
{np}Dievold, Brother!
{np}What's going on down there?
{np}Gildas! Wait!
{np}No, stay away!
{np}Stand back, Oelias!
{np}Help... Please, help us!
{np}We'll be there as soon as we can!

{np}Dievold, no!
No...how could this have happened?

{np}Oelias! No...
Great Father! What have I done!?

{np}The dead drag me...down.
Forgive me, Oelias.

{np}Now I see...
With my dying breath...I curse you, Nybeth!
{np}What has befallen Gildas?
{np}Thank you for your aid, knight. I am Oelias.
{np}And this is my brother. Forgive his silence. He is not given much to conversing.
{np}No, I would thank you myself.{pp}My name is Dievold... Forgive my rasp.
{np}My brother is...ill. It has ravaged his throat.
