{np}Great Father Philaha.
Forgive the sins of this, your child.

{np}Please, no!
Call Brantyn―he'll tell you!{pp}I did as he ordered, no more!{pp}Please, I don't want to die!{pp}{FF 92}{hero}! {hero}!!!

{np}{FF 9C 0101}{FF 8D 0102}{FF 85 013d}It was two days before I learned of
{FF 8D 0102}{FF 85 013d}the execution...{FF 98 0105}
{np}And what if it is?{pp}The Walister and Galgastani will hack each other into the ground.{pp}What more could we want for? You see fortune and call it calamity, Balxephon.
{np}We've received word that they rally on the Psonji Weald.

{np}They think to bring the fight to Almorica in the duke's absence. Good. Send a messenger to Volaq.{pp}Tell him to double their watch to ensure the Bakram―rather, the regent does not move without permission.
{np}As you command, sir.
{np}Barbas, I'm sending you to Heim.
{np}Steady, Barbas. I do not intend for you to serve as castellan for the regent, if that is your fear.{pp}The Liberation Front has freed Abuna Prancet from Heim Castle.
{np}Those partisan rebels might well catch wind of our true task.
{np}Andoras's search for Mannaflora is to continue.{pp}You and Martym will keep a close eye on the Walister and Galgastani for us.
{np}{hero}, wait.
{np}What, Catiua?
{np}Do not tell me you intend to cross the Brigania Flats!
{np}This again? The pieces are already in motion, Sister.{pp}If we do not move, then Vyce makes for his own doom in Psonji.

{np}You would match his folly with your own?
The enemy has twice our number!
{np}What would you counsel us to do then? Wait here, polishing our armor!?

{np}Enough of that, Peyton.
The Resistance is clearly unmanned.
{np}I see. First, they lose their duke, and now they can't find their spines! Ha!
{np}Stop it, both of you. What point in arguing amongst ourselves?{pp}The Resistance, the Alliance...these are old names without meaning. We are the Order of {order} now.
{np}It's as Vyce says. If you wish to argue, you're free to leave!

{np}The forces massed at Psonji are nearly the Galgastani army entire.{pp}Our scouts report that even the garrison from Coritanae has taken the field. Do you understand?{pp}The opportunity presents itself to strike at the hierophant directly. If another means to victory exists, I do not know it.
{np}All well and good if we can reach Coritanae, but how do we do that?
{np}There is only one approach to Coritanae that will not alert them to our intent.{pp}We must advance from behind the keep, from the Brigania Flats.
{np}Impossible!{pp}The Brigania Flats are a frozen wasteland, covered in snow and ice the year through.{pp}For every step forward, we would slide back two!

{np}And yet, there is no other way.{pp}Think on it: the hierophant would never expect attack from the flats.{pp}And Brigantys Castle stands alone in that waste. We could hardly ask for a better fortified waypoint.
{np}The idea isn't entirely without merit...
{np}I've no doubt you're up to the task, {hero}.
{np}You'd better be. Or we'll be sitting decoy for naught!
{np}Let us pray to the Father that the cold does not wither your courage, hero! Ah ha ha!

{np}Flee? Now?
Don't be ridiculous!

{np}I knew it.
You're going to leave me.
{np}It's always about you, isn't it? Well I've had enough!{pp}If you want to go back to Golyat, go! I'll not stop you.

{np}We'll go on ahead.
You finish up here.

{np}Vyce...
Can you forgive me?
{np}There's no forgiving what you've done.{pp}You were the duke's hand in the massacre. There are no words for one so low.

{np}But a man can repent.{pp}You did what you thought best. If I were a greater fool, I might have done the same.{pp}End this war, {hero}. You owe the people of Balmamusa that much.{pp}Let that be your atonement.
{np}You...you have no right!

{np}No, Sister.
He has every right.
{np}Farewell, {hero}.
{np}And you, Vyce.

{np}Someday the gods may forgive you.
But I haven't.

{np}It's colder than a witch's teat.
We'll not find trouble out here.
{np}I'd sooner be back in Brigantys, m'self.

{np}Quit your griping.
We have a patrol to finish.
{np}Beggin' your pardons, Sir Hektor. I weren't doin' no gripin', honest.
{np}Easy, lad. Who wouldn't rather be home in front of a roaring fire, eh?
{np}What is it brings you out all this way, Lord Commander?
{np}I'm no lord. Just a common soldier, like yourselves.{pp}I was ordered to hold Brigantys, and this I have done.
{np}You were ever a loyal follower of House Orlandeau. Still, a man like you, serving under Xaebos... It's a disgrace.
{np}I'll string you from the gallows myself if you speak of the High Commander like that again!

{np}Of-Of course!
Forgive me, sir.

{np}A knight's first duty is to liege and kingdom.{pp}My father, Sir Briam, taught me this, as his father, Sir Cornelius, taught him.{pp}Perhaps you think these age-worn vows bind us, but it is in times such as these that their true worth becomes clear.

{np}Forgive me, Sir Hektor.
I spoke out of turn―

{np}Rouse yourselves!
The enemy is upon us!
{np}I didn't think to encounter Galgastani scouts so far afield.
{np}We haven't come all this way for naught, then. To arms!
{np}I am Hektor Didarro, son of Briam, knight of Galgastan.{pp}Speak your name, Walister!
{np}I am {hero} Pavel of the Order of {order}.

{np}The Butcher of Golyat.
Your infamies precede you.{pp}You're to be commended. Few Walister have tread so deep into these lands.{pp}But you'll not reach Brigantys on our watch!
{np}Your hand is unsteady, {hero} of Golyat.{pp}Is it knowledge of what you've done that weighs on you? Or knowledge of what you will do?
{np}Who are you to question me? How many have {pal 16}you{palreset} slain, creature of Balbatos!?
{np}Then cast down your sword and surrender! It's Balbatos we're after!

{np}No matter how futile my struggle, I'll never surrender.{pp}I will not break the vows I swore to my kingdom. I will not bring disgrace upon my house!{pp}Fate ordained our meeting. To do less than fight to the end is to dishonor those who've fallen!
{np}The tide turns... We withdraw!
{np}I'll be waiting for you at Brigantys, {hero}!

{np}Greetings, Butcher of Golyat! You'll not find the warriors of Galgastan such lambs as the people of Balmamusa!{pp}Like a fox you creep in the shadows toward Coritanae―but we've got your tail, fox!
{np}Hrah! Stronger than I thought... Perhaps those rumors of an alliance hold some water?{pp}Where's our reinforcements? Where's Sir Hektor!?
{np}The Wheel turns against you, {hero} of Golyat!{pp}None have faced Bingham, Lord of Slaughter, and lived to tell the tale!{pp}Curse the gods or curse your sorry self, for your luck has run dry.
{np}Old man. This squawking mercenary who he say he is?
{np}Bingham? Not a name I've heard. And High Commander Gatialo's the one they call the "Lord of Slaughter," last I checked.
{np}Mayhaps the mercenary thinks a flow'ry title will raise his fee?
{np}Of course, were he telling the truth there'd be no witnesses to it. They'd all be dead.
{np}Eh. You think too much. I say we gut the buzzard and prove the lie.
{np}I see you save the sharpest tongue for your own, winged-one.
{np}Bah! This goes poorly. Why does the keep not march?
{np}For a "Lord of Slaughter," I daresay you'd have trouble defeating a side of pork at the breakfast table!
{np}Watch your beak or I'll clip yer wings, bird-man!
{np}Bird-man!? I'll stuff a pillow for my weary arse with your feathers!
{np}The pot's calling the kettle black, if you ask me.
{np}Errgh. A nobler death...I deserved.
{np}But the Walister have already breached the gates! We must send a rider to inform Coritanae!

{np}Do that, and you sign your own writ of execution. His Eminence tasked us with this castle's defense!{pp}By the honor of House Didarro, we will defeat these interlopers and stop their advance here.{pp}Or have you lost your courage so soon!
{np}But our dungeon holds scores of men who want nothing more than to see Galgastan fall! Should they join forces with the Walister―

{np}It shall not come to pass! We won't allow it!{pp}Consider that our enemy has fought across harsh, unfamiliar terrain outside our walls.{pp}They are fatigued. We will draw them inside the castle and finish them!{pp}Did you not wonder why I kept our forces from the field? Do you understand nothing of what I say!?

{np}House Didarro has never fallen short of its word. My son, Hektor, will not see it do otherwise now.{pp}If you are a knight of this house for true, you will follow your liege's orders with all due obedience.
{np}Yes, m'lord!
{np}By your leave, Father.
{np}You have it, and the pride of House Didarro as well.
{np}Praise of which I am unworthy, in truth.
{np}No, it is I who should apologize. I'm sending you to your death.

{np}You do not understand, Father. This is the opportunity I've long awaited!{pp}How many times I spoke of dedication to my land, my people―while my heart pained with every word.{pp}I could ask for no clearer sign than the Walister's arrival here, today. I was meant for this!

{np}Doubtlessly, they seek to take this castle and use it to launch an assault upon the weakly defended flanks of Coritanae.{pp}You see, this is their main force. The rabble at Psonji are no more than a feint.{pp}A clever, if reckless, stratagem...and yet, this may just give them a hope of toppling the hierophant.
{np}If it will mean an end to this conflict, then my life is a small price to pay.{pp}The castle is yours, Father. I leave her charges, and Galgastan, in your hands.

{np}Retreat! ...broken through...
...inside the walls!
{np}I am needed below. Know this: the honor of House Didarro will not falter this day.
{np}Our honor is greater for your sacrifice. Godspeed.
{np}You've come a long way to die, {hero}.{pp}You'll find these walls will not yield to you easily. Nor will they offer up her prize without a fight.
{np}What prize?
{np}Those enemies of the hierophant who languish in her dungeons.{pp}You mean you're not here to rally them to your cause? Then why...?{pp}Well, no matter. The dead seldom accomplish much of note!

{np}A victory here might gain us more than a strong base for an attack on Coritanae.{pp}An alliance with those Galgastani who turned against the hierophant could well lead to a lasting bond between our clans!
{np}I see your plan.{pp}You've drawn our lines off to Psonji in order to strike at Coritanae's undefended flank.
{np}True enough, for what good the knowledge will do you.{pp}You're finished, knight. Your castle will be ours. Bend the knee to us, and we'll spare your life.
{np}You dishonor me by the mere suggestion, Butcher of Golyat.{pp}I am a knight of Galgastan. You will not take this castle while I yet draw breath!
{np}Something about this rings false...

{np}What's wrong, {hero} of Golyat? Do not tell me the butcher hesitates to draw blood!{pp}You and I are foes, of this there is no doubt. One of us will triumph here, and the other will be cast into the abyss!{pp}Now, come, show to me the quality of a hero among Walister!

{np}Ah...it ends. The castle...
In your hands, Father...

{np}In the name of the armies of Galgastan, I, Briam Didarro, surrender this castle to you.{pp}What defenders remain have already thrown down their arms. I beg you, take their freedom, not their lives.
{np}You are not the first Didarro I have met this day.
{np}Aye. You slew my son, Hektor. But I do not weep.{pp}He died in utmost service to his sovereign, and with bravery in defense of our house's honor.

{np}The men and women behind me are those whom the hierophant imprisoned here for treachery.{pp}You requested them brought here, and I have done so...yet my clansmen they remain.{pp}Tell me, Walister. Are these enemies of the hierophant your enemies as well?

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} Of course they're not.
2. How could they be?
{np}No, of course not. But we did not take this castle to free them.{pp}They've done us no harm, so we've no cause to fight.
{np}So the enemy of your enemy is a friend, yes? Very well.
{np}Know that I have no intention of taking the lives of your Galgastani garrison.{pp}Though I do intend to free your prisoners, and they may feel otherwise.
{np}Well, you heard him. What say you?
{np}Jeunan. I would hear your thoughts.

{np}You have taken the castle and released us from our bonds, {hero}.{pp}I have not the words to express my gratitude...but let me say this:{pp}Your present course will not bring an end to this conflict.{pp}As you lift your voice and sword against a tyrant, one day another shall do the same unto you.{pp}Your struggle...changes nothing.
{np}Enough, Jeunan. He asked to know your heart, not your politics.
{np}Pay him no heed. He has languished overlong in the dungeon.
{np}No. His words ring far too true to be ignored.

{np}What wrong have they done us? We are not the Resistance of old.{pp}Our quarrel is not with the people of Galgastan.{pp}The generations-long conflict between your clan and ours never was!{pp}Always it has been men with power, men such as the hierophant and the duke, who throw their people at one another to further their own ambitions.{pp}It is not the Galgastani who must answer for this bloodshed...it is Balbatos and his ilk.
{np}Springtime words from the mouth of a youth...{pp}Let us pray to the Father that they remain true through the winter to come.
{np}What will you do, Jeunan?
{np}I am inspired to throw my lot upon the Wheel and trust this Walister.

{np}{hero} of Golyat. This man before you once aided the hierophant in his blood war against your people.{pp}Yet he knows now the error of his ways and seeks to atone.{pp}Allow me one request: take him with you. Give him his chance.
{np}If he has sinned, then my sin is greater still. I bear him no enmity.{pp}You are welcome to join us, Jeunan.
{np}Wish they'd sent us to fight at Psonji.{pp}Beats a supply run to Brigantys at any rate.

{np}And now it snows.
Bad to worse, eh?{pp}Who's there?

{np}Galgastani outriders...
More swift than I expected.
{np}Walister? In these god-forgotten lands? They must have crossed the Brigania Flats.
{np}Troops on their way to resupply Brigantys, by the look.{pp}They must not know the castle has already fallen.
{np}The roads to Asyton are shut off, and we'd have heard if Asyton had fallen.{pp}Could this rabble have taken Brigantys!? Impossible! Sir Hektor would never surrender the castle!
{np}Balbatos has not taken notice of us―a rare stroke of luck.
{np}Sir Hektor's doing, {hero}.

{np}Sir Hektor?
Why?

{np}He has no love for Balbatos.{pp}But you know Sir Hektor―loyal to a fault. He and his father both. They would never oppose Balbatos openly.{pp}When you arrived at Brigantys, he understood your true purpose.{pp}He and his father set in motion a plan to ease your way.
{np}What plan?

{np}Sir Hektor and Sir Briam made certain word of your approach would not reach Coritanae.{pp}They even ordered the garrison's forces divided, else your siege of Brigantys would never have succeeded.{pp}House Didarro values loyalty and honor above all else, so none doubted their intentions.
{np}Why not join our cause outright?
{np}For one thing, they did not know if you were a worthy ally or just another would-be duke.{pp}For another, they hold their honor too dear. They could not openly betray their lord.
{np}Sir Hektor let us take the castle?
{np}Aye, and his life.{pp}I am sure that by now, his father, Sir Briam, joins him―
{np}Never should've come to this...blasted place...
{np}Balbatos must fall, or they died for nothing.
{np}What is it, two days since we last heard from Brigantys?
{np}Two at least. It's not like Sir Hektor.
{np}Perhaps the weather turns foul. Brigania Flats is often beset with storms this time of year, no?
{np}True enough. But if snows had blocked the roads, I expect the company we sent to resupply Brigantys would have turned back by now.
{np}When did you find time to sharpen that dull wit of yours?
{np}Dull or not, I'm right, most like.{pp}If the high commander finds out aught is amiss, it's your neck, not mine.
{np}I'll worry about my neck; you worry about yours.

{np}Decurion!
A party approaches!
{np}Friend or foe?

{np}Can't say...
But they're not from Brigantys.
{np}A Galgastani patrol... We can't let them alert Coritanae.{pp}To battle!
{np}So these Walister dogs are the reason Brigantys has fallen silent.{pp}Their heads will make fine gifts for Sir Xaebos!
{np}No wonder crossing Brigania Flats gave you no trouble. You fight like lions!
{np}Hoping to take Coritanae from the rear, I reckon.
{np}Truly we face one of Galgastan's finest military minds.
{np}When our armies return from Psonji...your time will come...
{np}Coritanae isn't far now. We must press on!

{np}So it's done.
The Walister are broken!

{np}Just so.
Sir Xaebos does not disappoint.
{np}Indeed not. Now all that remain are Brantyn and the Dark Knights.{pp}Still, even with Almorica, defeating them will be no small task.

{np}My lords!
The Walister... They're here!

{np}Here?
What are you talking about?
{np}They lay siege to the castle!
{np}How many are there?

{np}I-I don't know, sir.
What do we do?
{np}Meet them with every man who can hold a sword!
{np}Yes sir!
{np}The remnants of their army couldn't have broken through our lines, unless...Psonji was a diversion!

{np}They are, my lord.
Sir Xaebos does not disappoint.

{np}Calm yourself!
You speak in tongues, soldier.

{np}I am {hero} Pavel, of the Order of {order}! Hear me, Leundar Balbatos!{pp}Open the gates of Coritanae and surrender!{pp}Kneel without a fight, and I will ensure you a fair reckoning.{pp}Resist us, and we will release heaven's judgment upon you for your crimes!
{np}What hole did they crawl from!?{pp}Listen up, boys. We only need hold these walls until our main host returns! Let not one of them into the keep!
{np}Listen well, interlopers! The Walister host was routed in the field!{pp}You're fighting for a lost cause!
{np}So they weren't able to hold in Psonji...{pp}Unfortunate, but our course remains the same. We've a keep to take!
{np}Make your peace with the Father now, for when Sir Xaebos returns with his legions, you will die!
{np}Sounds like another way to say you're doomed unless your friends come to save you.
{np}Wishful thoughts, cur!
{np}It is a long way for word to travel to Psonji...and as long for your legions to return.

{np}So...
So close.
{np}I know you!{pp}Bless my mending wounds for keeping me here and granting me this chance to face you again.{pp}Have no fear, boy. I'll show you all the mercy you showed our arkhiatros!
{np}Well met, Gatialo. I've awaited this day too long.
{np}Jeunan Avertif! I see you harbor traitors in your ranks, boy.{pp}Unfortunate for you that your newfound ally is craven to the bone!
{np}You call me craven? When you cannot face your own deeds in Vasque!?
{np}My deeds? My deeds!? 'Twas you who did the killing there that day, Avertif!
{np}Harken well, {hero} of Golyat. Know the true nature of your comrade in arms.{pp}His sword is wet with the blood of innocents, and his boots dark with the ashes of their village!
{np}Who sent us there under orders to scour the streets? Who told us that village was a traitors' nest!?

{np}I may have sent you there, but I did not blind you to the truth of what you found.{pp}Why not question your duty when no resistance was offered?{pp}Blame me all you wish―it will not remove the stains from your blade!

{np}True. Killing you now would do little to absolve my guilt.{pp}I was a man changed then. Those villagers―an ogre inside me moved my hand to cut short their cries for mercy.{pp}I believed, in my black heart, that I did my duty for Galgastan. That I served my people even as I slew them.{pp}But what did I serve, other than death?{pp}I watched as the light faded from the eyes of our people and fear grew in their hearts.{pp}I watched as the beauty that was Galgastan...perished.

{np}What a simpering fool you've become! Shedding a tear for beauty? Bah!{pp}Fear is a weapon to be wielded!{pp}We are strong! We bloody our hands with the toils of victory! There is no shame in triumph!{pp}And the weak? It is our right to trample the weak, and their duty to be trampled!
{np}I knew you were too venomous a creature to let live!{pp}You are the thorn that keeps war's wounds fresh!
{np}Bah! Enough talk! Let's see what you and your whimpering blade can do!
{np}To meet death at the hands of these Walister swine... Forgive me...
{np}A crafty ploy, {hero} of Golyat!{pp}But this keep still stands, and by the might of Galgastan she will not fall!
{np}You... Jeunan!? What are you doing with those Walister blackguards!?
{np}Daesi... How many seasons have passed since we last met.
{np}If you are here...then Brigantys has fallen, and the traitors to the hierophant conspire with the Walister!
{np}True enough, though I mislike your choice of words.{pp}We are not criminals, but brothers-in-arms, seeking not more conflict, but peace.
{np}You do not know the past of this man you call your ally, {hero} of Golyat.{pp}His sword is wet with the blood of innocents, and his boots dark with the ashes of their village!

{np}It is true. I have no desire to deny what I have done.{pp}Nor do I deny that it was a terrible mistake, a weighty sin upon my soul!{pp}All those who lent aid to Balbatos's blood war were ogres...ogres in men's flesh!
{np}You blame His Eminence? It was you upon the field of battle! You who mistook friend for foe!
{np}You speak as though your own hands were not stained dark with the blood of innocents!
{np}Innocents? Do not brand me with your iron, traitor!{pp}I fought only the enemies of this kingdom...gnawing vermin like you, who place the blame for their own sins upon our lord!

{np}True. Killing the hierophant now would do little to absolve my guilt.{pp}I was a man changed then. Those villagers―something dark inside me moved my hand to cut short their cries for mercy.{pp}I believed, in my black heart, that I did my duty for Galgastan. That I served my people even as I slew them.{pp}But what did I serve, other than death?{pp}I watched as the light faded from the eyes of our people and fear grew in their hearts.{pp}I watched as the beauty that was Galgastan...perished.

{np}Foolishness! You'd have us return to the years of Dorgalua's rule, is that it?{pp}When the Bakram and Walister dined at the king's table, while the Galgastani were left to forage for scraps?{pp}You would throw away all we built this kingdom for! Where is the beauty in that, I ask you!?

{np}You decry the injustices of Dorgalua while you wish them upon the Walister!{pp}You would strip them―and your own clansmen―of their freedom.{pp}The hierophant's justice has failed, and his people abandon him. Surely you see it, Daesi!{pp}You cannot build a castle upon shifting sands.
{np}As you wish, Jeunan. We will let the battle decide who has the right of it!

{np}Our forces have taken the keep.
It is over!
{np}No closer, Walister! I'll never kneel to the likes of you.
{np}You have no choice.
{np}Foulest of days...{pp}We won in Psonji! We won!
{np}I said stay back, insolent cretins!
{np}Your keep is taken and your men are slain, Balbatos. Yield!
{np}You were wrong, Walister...
{np}I do...have a choice!
{np}He's dead.
{np}I wonder how Vyce has fared...
{np}Where is {hero}? Speak!

{np}How should...I know?
Run off somewhere...I'd wager...
{np}You expect me to believe the hero of the Walister turned tail and fled?{pp}Tell me what you're scheming, or I'll quiet you for good!

{np}Sir! The Walister―
They've taken Coritanae!
{np}What!? How is that possible?
{np}A force crossed the Brigania Flats and assaulted the keep from her flank!
{np}Madness!{pp}What of the hierophant? Surely he's not―
{np}Slain, sir. The dogs showed no mercy.
{np}The hierophant...slain?
{np}Ha! He did it! He really did it! Ha ha!
{np}You...vile, scheming creature!
{np}Unh!
{np}...How stand our ranks?
{np}Sir. We have... Roughly four companies remain, sir.
{np}Godspit! We've lost more than I thought.

{np}Send Brutakos and Muntzer to Coritanae!
We will march on Almorica!
{np}At once, sir!
{np}That demon of Golyat will pay for this!
{np}You'll pay for the hierophant's death with your own, {hero}!
{np}Grk... A hardened Walister force. We can't take them with our armies divided.
{np}Forgive me, Your Eminence...
{np}Onward! We take back Almorica!

{np}I expected a coward like you to slink away from the battlefield at Psonji...{pp}But you've made a misstep. Look down at your feet, deep into the marsh.{pp}See something familiar? That's right... Your fallen comrades have been waiting here for you.{pp}And who am I to deny them the reunion for which they long?{pp}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you! Darkness to me!
{np}It'll be just like old times!
{np}No wonder Coritanae fell to you.
{np}Galgastan is finished. Whether Xaebos realizes it or not, the ground has shifted beneath him.{pp}If you live through the coming battle, I am sure we will meet again. So long!
{np}I may spend my days hunting heads for a paltry fee, but I've not forgotten my debt to His Eminence.{pp}There's a legion of Galgastani dead who can't wait for you to join 'em!
{np}Keep walking!
{np}Their leader, my lord.
{np}Doesn't know when to die, does she.
{np}Go on... Kill me.
{np}You're in no position to be making requests.

{np}She's yours.
Enjoy the spoils of war.
{np}We'll put her to good use, won't we, boys?
{np}Go on and...try!
{np}So you're the commander of the Walister forces who took Coritanae?{pp}You'll pay for the disgrace you brought upon the hierophant, {hero} Pavel!
{np}Soldiers of Galgastan! Release your captives and throw down your arms!{pp}Balbatos is no more! There is no longer cause to fight!
{np}Fool! Why should we heed you? We're the victors here!{pp}We will see His Eminence's vision through: an end to your befouled bloodline!
{np}Victors? But you've lost.{pp}The people of Coritanae and Brigantys both have joined us. They follow you no longer!
{np}The people? They're as fickle as a weathercock, turning whichever way the wind blows.{pp}Once you are buried and Almorica is ours, we'll see how quickly they return to their former masters!
{np}And how will you lead them? With fear? You follow the same dark course as the hierophant!

{np}Never have I heard so many words mean so little. The people respect fear!{pp}How would you lead, you Walister filth! This world yearns to be rid of you!{pp}If only you were gone, how perfect these isles would be.

{np}So you would eliminate the Walister...then what? Who is next? The Bakram? And after them?{pp}I know. After the Bakram were gone, you would kill other Galgastani.{pp}The slightest difference in custom or faith, the first sign of weakness, and they would die.{pp}That is what you want. That is who you are!
{np}The pondscum passes judgment on the fisherman!
{np}I do not fight the Galgastani. I fight those who deceive, who incite fear to better their position.{pp}I fight you! You are the true enemy of these isles!

{np}Forgive me...hierophant.
I...have failed you.
{np}We may be all that's left of Galgastan's armies, but we'll not surrender to you!{pp}Look well, boy. This is how men of honor meet death!

{np}You. You're Jeunan Avertif.
Rebels taken you under their wing, have they?{pp}A fine pair you make.
{hero} is no better than the duke.
{np}Have you forgotten Balmamusa? You seemed only too glad to carry out the duke's orders then.{pp}I know you for what you are, boy: a butcher, and ruthless.
{np}So quick to find fault, but these are past sins for which we seek to atone!{pp}What about yourself, Xaebos? You lead your men to their doom.
{np}Hmph, I might have expected as much from you, Jeunan.{pp}You and {hero} are cut from the same cloth.{pp}You speak of the good of the people, yet think only of yourselves!
{np}All our plans, ruined by you Walister filth!
{np}Walister, Galgastani―that's how men like Balbatos and the duke wish to paint us.{pp}They play us against each other for their own purposes. But we have had enough!

{np}You quibble over words.
In the end, each of us fights for our own reasons.{pp}You convince the people that you are their champion. Perhaps you've even convinced yourself.{pp}But it is naught but a convenient lie.
{np}I don't have to convince myself of anything.
{np}Sir Xaebos, lay down your sword!{pp}There is no honor in a meaningless death!
{np}We gladly give our lives for the sake of the hierophant's cause.{pp}A noble act...lost on the likes of you, Ravness.
{np}It is not honor you seek but glory!{pp}You have a sacred duty to your kinsmen. Where is the nobility in abandoning them?
{np}Who are you to speak to me of duty?{pp}You're nothing but a mongrel bitch who betrayed her better half!
{np}A sorry sight...I must make.{pp}Remember it well, {hero}. Someday...this will be your fate.
{np}I'll not sink so low.
{np}It takes...only one false step.
{np}If ever I turn against my people, death seems a just reward.

{np}Ha... Might be that it is.{pp}The people aren't half as smart as...you credit them. But nor are they...fools.{pp}Betrayal...retribution...righteousness.
Words on the wind.{pp}Enjoy your victory...while it lasts, boy.

{np}And {hero} and Vyce besides!
I am glad to see you well.

{np}I've not seen him since the night of the Bakram attack.{pp}They held us at a camp outside Rhime, but we managed to escape.{pp}What is next for you?
An assault on Phidoch, I suppose?
{np}That's the plan.{pp}But first we must do something about the Bakram armies at Rhime.{pp}If our casualties there are too great, we'll never take Phidoch.
{np}What we need is some way of taking Rhime unawares.{pp}What we have is a frontal assault across the Golborza Plain.{pp}Hardly an ideal stratagem.
{np}There is one way...

{np}There are hidden passes through the Burnham Massif―ways known only to the goatherds and peasants who make the mountains their home.{pp}We can use these trails to approach Rhime from the west.{pp}It's the last thing they'll expect. The city will fall in the confusion.
{np}Let's be about it, then!
{np}{FF 9A 03}You received a Brave's Mark.

{np}{hero}!
And Vyce besides!
{np}What we need is some way of taking Rhime unawares.{pp}What we have is a frontal assault across the Golborza Plain.{pp}Feh. Hardly an ideal stratagem.
{np}We can't afford to lose a single man to these fiends. Watch yourselves!
{np}Onward to Rhime!
{np}The whole might of the Order of {order}. A host equal to our own. Perhaps greater.
{np}How have they mustered such a force in such short order?

{np}Perhaps Hierophant Balbatos had even more enemies than we suspected.{pp}It is true that, on word of his death, men deserted his armies like rats from a foundering ship.{pp}What's more, the New Walister Alliance enjoys the support of the slaves and commons.{pp}It would seem this young {hero} is as much at home before a crowd as he is at the head of an army.

{np}You speak as though it was not your doing that brought us to this unhappy pass.{pp}We ought have marched on Almorica as soon as we took Rhime.{pp}Perhaps it's not too late.
Summon my war council!{pp}Inform them I plan to lay siege to Almorica.
{np}I beg you reconsider, Lord Regent. Surely the Bakram armies alone are not sufficient to the task.
{np}What? The Dark Knights would abandon us now? You wouldn't dare!
{np}You have an arrangement with the high champion. An arrangement with certain...obligations.
{np}Stay your anger, Lord Regent.{pp}I meant only to suggest that you avoid rousing the Order of {order} before there is need.{pp}Have patience, you'll see.
{np}And how will you reward my patience?{pp}I half fear you mean to betray us for a new suitor.
{np}Do you not trust us, Lord Regent? That would be most unfortunate.
{np}I spoke without thinking. But understand, my patience is not without limit.

{np}Not to worry, Lord Regent.
We'll take care of everything, I assure you.
{np}Very well―we wait.
{np}As you say, my lord.

{np}You there!
No going out of doors after dark.

{np}Is it night already?
I hadn't noticed.{pp}An error you'll not begrudge a blind man, I pray?

{np}Think you're clever, do you?
Let's have your name!
{np}What trouble is this?
{np}Found him lurking in the shadows, Dame Ozma.

{np}Turn.
Show me your face.

{np}Are you deaf as well?
Do as you're told!

{np}Hobyrim? Is that you?
How is this possible?
{np}You have me mistaken, my lady.
{np}Don't be absurd, Hobyrim. Where have you been? Why have you come to Valeria?
{np}Who goes there!
{np}I am {hero} Pavel, captain of the Order of {order}!{pp}Throw down your swords or die. The choice is yours.

{np}A blind scout.
That's a bloody laugh!

{np}Spare the swordsman!
I want him taken alive!
{np}All due respect, Dame Ozma, but if it's his neck or mine, I'll save mine.{pp}We can't let the city fall! Drive them back!
{np}Attack!
{np}And so...it ends. Would've liked to get in...one more cut.
{np}Hobyrim! No!
{np}Over there―those Bakram are chasing someone. To his aid!
{np}Hobyrim, say something! It is I, Ozma!{pp}Your eyes... What has befallen you?
{np}Have you forgotten even the sound of my voice?{pp}Please, tell me what happened!

{np}You look...frail, Hobyrim. Where have you been these past six years?{pp}I had it from Balxephon that you were dead! ...Was he in error?{pp}But no, he would not make such a mistake. Then, was it a lie?
{np}Stop! Do not attack him!
{np}Odd. That woman of the Dark Knights seems to know the swordsman they chase.
{np}It pains me...but we must withdraw!
{np}I'll leave Hobyrim to the Order of {order} for now.{pp}I must hear the truth of the matter from Balxephon first, lest I place him in harm's way again.
{np}Hold, you!
{np}Could that truly have been Hobyrim?{pp}But how is it possible? I must consult Balxephon on this matter. I must know!
{np}I thank you for your aid. You are the Almoricans at war with the Dark Knights, I take it?
{np}I am {hero} Pavel, captain of the Order of {order}.
{np}Ah. The one they call the Hero of Golyat, yes? I am Hobyrim Vandam.
{np}Rhime is turned battlefield since the Bakram invaded. What was your business here?

{np}I heard you were bringing the fight to the Dark Knights. I thought to lend you my sword.{pp}As you can see, I am without sight. But I am gifted in other ways. I wield a blade better than any common soldier you'll find.

{np}You're confident, I'll give you that.
Tell me, where do you hail from? You're not of this island, are you.
{np}Ah, the lad has a sharp ear. You're quite right. I am Lodissian.{pp}But do not think that makes me enamored of our Dark Knights. Quite the contrary. I revile them.
{np}Only, allow me one question.
{np}What might that be?
{np}The Dark Knight that was after you―the woman. Do you know her?

{np}Aye, that I do.{pp}I'm sure you have doubts regarding my intentions, but I must ask that you do not inquire further.{pp}I will tell you all when the time is right... But for now, know that I am a sworn enemy to the Dark Knights, and no enemy of yours.
{np}Very well. I'll give my trust, in hopes it will be soon earned.
{np}That it shall.
{np}Well... I cannot fault you for distrusting a sightless swordsman, can I.{pp}I am sure we will meet again, youth of Golyat. Until that time, fare thee well.

{np}You're certain?
It was Hobyrim?

{np}I know who I saw.
And a wretched sight he was.

{np}Of course.
I did not mean to doubt you.
{np}You told me he was dead―taken ill in the dungeons of B'landone.
{np}Indeed. He was given funerary rights―a meager ceremony befitting a criminal, but even so.
{np}So you bore witness to his corpse. Perhaps I was mistaken after all.
{np}As I have said.
{np}I want to believe you, but I cannot deny what I saw.
{np}Not interrupting, am I?

{np}A private matter.
No concern of yours.
{np}Now now, Balxephon. That's no way to speak to the brother of your betrothed.

{np}Brother or no, I am your commander.
If you've business with me, I would hear it.
{np}Our front line is breached. It's only a matter of time before Phidoch falls.
{np}So the Bakram were not enough to hold them after all.
{np}Ozma, take a detachment of men and leave the castle. Oz and I will delay them as long as we can.
{np}Oh? Am I to flee like the thrush before the storm?

{np}Nothing of the sort.
You are to guard the high champion.

{np}Of course.
He and the princess must be kept safe.

{np}You have your orders.
Go!
{np}Ozma―we'll continue this later.

{np}Everything is in order, my lord.
Come, you'd best be on your way.

{np}Ozma awaits you without.
Oz and I will handle this.
{np}See that you do.
{np}You must be {hero}. It was an ill turn you did my sister at Rhime.
{np}We must be going, Catiua.

{np}The whelp has grown.
Let's see how much!

{np}I like what I see, boy!
You're determined, with a good eye and a steady sword arm.{pp}Not to mention the notches in your blade! To think you've slain my captain, your liege...and all those at Balmamusa.{pp}Why, I might even consider letting you minister here in Valeria. In our name, of course.
{np}Don't waste your breath telling me of the stains on my shield. I know them all too well.{pp}But know that I will not let Lodis take these isles. Her peoples will not abide you!

{np}And I see you are at peace with your own baser nature! Marvelous!{pp}One could hardly ask for more in a ruler. For who can deceive others who cannot deceive himself?{pp}No. We cannot dwell upon our missteps along the path to domination.{pp}A bit of repentance, a touch of regret, perhaps. But do not shed a tear for the wretches―let their wounds weep for them.{pp}These things we do are necessary. The pruning of ill-formed branches, that our children might enjoy the fruits of our labors, yes?{pp}This is the heart of the conqueror! This is you!

{np}You, boy!
I owe you thanks for showing such hospitality to my sister.
{np}His sister? The Dark Knight! The resemblance is striking.

{np}Ah, but how best to thank you?{pp}A meal perhaps? I'm quite the chef, you know.{pp}I'll tell you my secret. Preparation is everything. A silver fork, a silver knife...{pp}First I'll cut off both your arms, run the left through with the fork, and the right with the knife, I believe.{pp}And for the soup, molten lead goes down best. I'll slice your neck and pour it down your throat, so there'll be no need for a spoon.{pp}Then, I think, a thin cut of flesh from your back. Raw. Bleeding. You like steak, no?{pp}And next―
{np}Enough, Oz! This is no time for your games.
{np}What are {pal 16}you{palreset} doing here, Hobyrim!? Come to repay my mercy with murder?
{np}That voice... Well met, Balxephon! Though, I am puzzled by this talk of mercy.{pp}Was it mercy robbed me of my sight? Mercy that killed our father?

{np}You've traveled a long road for your revenge, Brother.{pp}You question my mercy? In truth I question it myself!{pp}I gave you the chance to begin anew, and you tread the same old tired steps back to where you began.
{np}So you {pal 16}do{palreset} live, Hobyrim. I thought you long gone to the worms!
{np}No, Oz. Though I remain as sightless as those creatures which crawl through the earth.
{np}You do much resemble a worm, yes. How my sister recognized you, I haven't the faintest idea.
{np}She knows nothing of what happened, does she.

{np}Aye, for the criers declared you imprisoned for treason and perished in captivity.{pp}My sister tried to free you, you know.{pp}If only you had not so pigheadedly refused to serve Loslorien in your trial.{pp}You remember? Your own advocate―whatever was his name?―pleaded with you to reconsider, but you would not listen.{pp}Your jurors were well ready to absolve you, had you only said the words. You could have walked free.{pp}And why was that, I wonder. Ah, perhaps because my dear sister bought every man in that room!{pp}All her efforts...for naught.{pp}In her eyes, you died that day.
{np}She did this?
{np}Yours was a life hardly worth saving, Hobyrim. Mother would weep to see your unthankful nature.
{np}Mother? You poisoned our mother, Balxephon!
{np}Hmm. You're well informed. It seems that some of your rebellious friends linger yet in the empire.

{np}You slew the senators, you slew our lord father, and you call me the rebel!?{pp}You tricked those fool abbots into lapping up your envenomed words and made a marionette of the high priest.{pp}Blind as I am, I can see how you led the people to war in the name of god.{pp}And you expect me to flee? To hide? You are an ogre of Lodis in the flesh, and I cannot suffer you to live!

{np}You are a fool if you cannot see the good we have done for Lodis. The wrongs we have righted!{pp}The senators were a contagion upon the republic; it was but one pace from death.{pp}Ours was a harsh leeching, yes, but had we left our homeland to fester the Bolmoccans and Xenobians would have rent her asunder and kept the pieces.{pp}A plague upon the heavens to have cursed me with a brother such as you!
{np}Where's my father? Where have you taken him!?
{np}What is he talking about?
{np}Balxephon. That boy is none other than the abuna Prancet Pavel's son.
{np}Hmm, thus his ardent temperament.{pp}Boy! I cannot reveal your father's whereabouts...but I will tell you he lives.
{np}Why do this? What reason could you possibly have to hold a mere abuna?
{np}Our reasons are for you to discover, as you doubtless will in time.{pp}Though information comes with a price.
{np}Not as dear as the price you'll pay for this.

{np}The boy has spirit!
I approve.
{np}Feh, this could have gone better. Perhaps it's time for a change in tactics?
{np}Fleeing, you coward? They say the feeblest hound barks the loudest, and now I see it to be true.
{np}I should have your tongue out for that!
{np}I think we've won ourselves time enough. The moment is ripe for our departure.
{np}Oz!?
{np}Th-This...was not supposed to happen.
{np}Fool! You never did know when to retreat...and now it has cost you.
{np}As it will cost you, boy!
{np}We've held out as long as we can, Oz!
{np}Go on, Balxephon! I will buy you time.
{np}And throw away your own life in the bargain? I won't allow it!

{np}What have you done, boy!
This...was...unexpected.{pp}Sister, help. Help...me.
{np}You have wounded my flesh and spat upon my honor this day, wretch of Golyat!
{np}I leave you with your worthless life, Hobyrim... But it will not be so next we meet!

{np}Hold, Balxephon!
Blast!
{np}You will pay thricefold for this when your time comes. Mark my words!
{np}Why, Catiua...why?
{np}We'll both be caught here. I'll stay and slow the enemy―you go on ahead!
{np}I owe you an apology, Ravness.{pp}I thought you could not be trusted. Forgive me.

{np}You're kind, but there's naught to forgive.
Now go. See to our young lord of Coritanae.
{np}Thought you could slip away, did you?

{np}Warriors of Galgastan!
Coritanae has fallen! Balbatos is slain!{pp}Surrender and save yourselves!
{np}I did not think Coritanae would fall so swift.
{np}Walister lies!

{np}Shut your ears to their slander.
Seize the woman, slay the rest!
{np}Dame Ravness, rally to us!
{np}Already you lead the armies of Almorica.
{np}Sir Leonar gave his life to make it so.{pp}Balmamusa, Sir Leonar...how many more must I send to their death?

{np}A brave man, Sir Leonar.
I knew him well.{pp}He would bear any dishonor for his country.
{np}It is a great burden he has passed to you.{pp}But who am I to fault him for that?
{np}You're too hard on yourself.

{np}Am I?
Balmamusa was a foul business.{pp}It was unfair of us to ask one so young to bear so much.{pp}We trusted to your strength, when we ought have heeded our own wisdom.
{np}I might have chosen another path at Balmamusa. I might have died in Sir Leonar's place.{pp}But there is no undoing what is done.
{np}You press on because you must, bearing your shame upon your shield.
{np}So this is Dame Ravness.
{np}She's no enemy of ours.

{np}Easy, {hero}.
Sir Briam told me all.{pp}A Walister knight who toils for Galgastan is a rare creature indeed.
{np}She's well regarded among those who oppose Balbatos.{pp}And Balbatos's men think of her less as a Walister knight than a rogue within their own camp.
{np}Dame Ravness, a Galgastani rebel?
{np}I'd sooner have the tale from her, but she'll not talk if she's dead.
{np}You're looking well, all things considered.
{np}I see you've not changed, Canopus.

{np}Not as you have.
There's a rose in your cheeks. It suits you.{pp}You had a grim look when first we met at Almorica.
{np}I was confused about a great many things. But no longer.
{np}To the business at hand then. So many foes in need of mortality.

{np}Walister... Galgastan...
May peace...find you someday.
{np}She's gone...
{np}Her strength will be missed.

{np}Dame Ravness!
Are you all right?

{np}Thank you, yes.
I live to fight another day.
{np}It was the Galgastani who pursued you, and a Galgastani whom you helped escape.{pp}I admit I'm rather...confused.
{np}The knight you saw opposes the hierophant. It was Balbatos's loyals who gave chase.
{np}To what end?

{np}The lord of Coritanae is the rightful ruler of Galgastan. Hierophant Balbatos is merely his steward.{pp}As the young lord was not yet of age, Balbatos was free to reshape Galgastan as he saw fit.{pp}The poor child was a piece in a game he scarce knew existed.{pp}We had hoped to reach him before your assault on Coritanae.
{np}Where is he now?
{np}Balbatos's enemies shelter him.{pp}With Coritanae sacked and Balbatos dead, I should think they'll take him to Brigantys.{pp}A great many of their number hold the castle.
{np}Good people, and true.
{np}That's right―you've met them, haven't you.{pp}It is they who reached out to me to aid in the reformation.
{np}Of Galgastan, you mean?
{np}Of course. Not everyone in Galgastan wanted war with the Walister.{pp}What better way to bring peace to both people than to change Galgastan from within?
{np}Peace without bloodshed.
{np}With my mixed blood, I thought myself a fitting standard-bearer for the cause.
{np}I had but to open my eyes and see.{pp}And when I did, a new truth emerged―a way for Walister and Galgastani both to emerge victorious.

{np}A worthy goal.
One I share.

{np}Join us, Ravness.
Fight at our side.{pp}Our paths parted at Balmamusa, but we seek the same thing.{pp}Look past what is done, and lend me your steel.
{np}You've grown much since Balmamusa. My sword is yours.
{np}You've grown much since Balmamusa.{pp}Continue your efforts with the Walister, and I will do the same with the Galgastani.
{np}Perhaps together we will find a way toward peace.
{np}Hmph. You still live.{pp}Leave us!

{np}...Another uprising...companies...
...to the highroads...
{np}Can you hear that, knight of Xenobia?
{np}It is only a matter of time before you fall.
{np}Who rules in Valeria is a trifling matter.{pp}You of all people must understand this.

{np}...Need more men...nearly enough...
Loslorien!{pp}...Not be able...quell this rising...
{np}Let me guess. Unable to stem the tide that rises from the hamlets and villages?
{np}Perhaps we asked too much of the Bakram's soldiers. They are not the soldiers we are, you know. Or the men.
{np}Always binding people to your will, fettering them lest they show signs of free thought.{pp}Perhaps therein lies your problem?
{np}They {pal 16}ask{palreset} for a stern hand to rule them.

{np}They...{pal 16}ask{palreset}?
You're mad!

{np}You have it wrong. It is the world that is mad.{pp}Tell me, how many of these peasants would even lift a hand to better their lot were they given a chance?{pp}How many would bloody their hands, risk their necks, walk without leaning upon another?
{np}Think back to your own uprising. Where were the people for whom you shed blood?{pp}Safe at their hearths, grousing that more was not done for them!
{np}Times were hard. They had all they could do to keep themselves fed...

{np}Nonsense. They chose to be victims!{pp}They think that only from without the castle walls may one voice discontent.{pp}Not realizing that the quickest way to the throne is a knife to the king's ribs.
{np}These people have the right to live out their own lives, not some part in a play of your design!

{np}You have both your eyes, and yet you see less clearly than do I.{pp}{pal 16}True{palreset} freedom is not granted from above, it is won from below.{pp}And yet the commons look without for a savior, even as they claim sovereignty over their own fate!{pp}They wait and they wait for this savior, never taking that first step toward saving themselves.

{np}Man is not so slothful a creature as that...
They...merely lack our strength.
{np}You are much too pure of heart, holy knight.{pp}The people have no need of dreams. We give them all they need.
{np}And what is that, pray tell?
{np}A strong, unwavering ruler.
{np}You {pal 16}are{palreset} mad.

{np}All men are born with a terrible burden upon their hearts, this insatiable yearning for pleasure.{pp}They do not hesitate to take the lives of others if it will better their own.{pp}And yet, even these base creatures can know guilt. So what do they do? They turn it round.{pp}This is not {pal 16}my{palreset} fault, man says. The world has failed {pal 16}me{palreset}.{pp}Someone must bring order to this chaos!{pp}If the commons want to pursue their pleasure, let them do it in our service, under our rule!
{np}You call this "rule"? This trampling underfoot of all who disagree with you?
{np}We trample no one.{pp}All we do is reach beneath the suppurating flesh of this world and wrench out the source of its ailment.
{np}No. As the body strives to mend itself, so does the heart.{pp}These people you so despise may one day astonish you with their valor!
{np}You have far too much faith in the creature called "man," knight.{pp}People are drawn to power, drawn toward safety. They will betray even their most beloved to obtain it―{pp}Catiua, come!

{np}Catiua!
What are you doing here!?
{np}Allow me to introduce you to your liege, knight.{pp}For this girl is none other than the gift left us by Dynast-King Dorgalua: the Princess Versalia, rightful ruler of Valeria!
{np}As you say, the Bakram are not long for this world.{pp}But, with the princess in our hands, Valeria will beg to serve under Lodis.
{np}Catiua, how... Is this true?

{np}I loved {hero}. As my brother, I loved him.{pp}But he was no brother to me.{pp}He abandoned me.{FF 92}
And now I, him.
{np}Though it pains me to part with the man who took my eye, I see no need to further torment the vanquished.
{np}Wait!
{np}Farewell, knight of Xenobia.

{np}The princess has not been seen since the ceremony.{pp}Not even the officers among the Bakram know her whereabouts, and the regent has lent his spies to the search.{pp}I see no other explanation but that the princess has sided with the Dark Knights.
{np}Then the rift between Brantyn and Tartaros widens.{pp}What word of the Dark Knights?
{np}Most remain garrisoned in Heim.{pp}But many of their commanders, including Tartaros, are conspicuously absent.
{np}Perhaps this is why the Bakram do not move against us.{pp}What could they be scheming?
{np}You asked me to search for the holy knight of Xenobia...
{np}Yes. Have you heard something?
{np}A confession wrung from a scullery maid.{pp}It seems that the holy knight languishes in the dungeon below Heim Castle.
{np}So he lives!
{np}Yes, but under such a guard that not even the Bakram are allowed near.{pp}I was unable to mark him with my own eyes.
{np}Still, you have done much. Go. Rest.
{np}By your leave, Commander.
{np}Catiua...
{np}Commander, should we not move our forces on Heim?
{np}Not as yet.{pp}It would be rash indeed to strike without first knowing the Dark Knights' purpose.

{np}Yes, but the more time that passes before we strike, the weaker we become.{pp}Have you forgotten the way the men speak of the princess?{pp}Soldiers in your own ranks weep aloud at the thought of lifting a sword against Dorgalua's blood!

{np}I know. I know.
All the more reason to not act in haste!
{np}A report, sir!
{np}What is it?
{np}The soldiers at Brigantys have taken hostages and holed up inside the castle!
{np}What are their demands?
{np}Our surrender to the Bakram, sir!
{np}After all the fighting we've been through? Not bloody likely!
{np}So the Order of Philaha joins the fray...{pp}Their followers among the soldiers were many, were they not?
{np}Aye. And their influence has only grown since the princess's appearance.

{np}Not a situation we are like to change.{pp}My sis―the princess's arrival was, for many, the advent of a savior.{pp}Add to this the fact that the late Dynast-King was a fervent follower of Philaha.{pp}How natural for these new converts to rekindle his cry for accord and seek to abandon the fight.
{np}I see no other choice but to meet with these followers of Philaha and speak with them.
{np}Out of the question! It's too dangerous, Commander.
{np}Not if I go alone and unarmed. They will hear me out.
{np}I have looked forward to our meeting, {hero} of Golyat!{pp}You will pay for your crimes against Galgastan with your life!
{np}The bastard's...killed me.
{np}Not a step farther! State your business. Only the faithful are permitted within!
{np}Don't you recognize me? I've come for an audience with your high priest.
{np}I don't much care for your tone!

{np}Steady there!
That's {hero} of Golyat you're talking to.

{np}I am unarmed.
I mean no ill will.
{np}I'll be the judge of that. How do I know you don't have half a dozen soldiers with you?

{np}Leave off.
Sir {hero} isn't the sort to lie to us.
{np}I knew you were always {pal 16}their{palreset} man!
{np}A grave insult.
{np}Sheath your swords.
{np}You too.
{np}I am Olivya, a sybil of the order here.{pp}You wish to meet with our leader, Abuna Prancet? Come this way.

{np}What did you say?
Abuna Prancet?
{np}Yes, your father is here.
{np}I don't understand.

{np}Please, we must hurry.
There isn't much time.
{np}The Great Father Philaha calls him to his side. I'm sorry, {hero}.
{np}When we discovered him in the Corpsevale near Heim, he lacked even the strength to stand.
{np}What place is this "vale"?
{np}It is a small cavern where those afflicted with incurable disease or plague are kept.
{np}Plague...
{np}We did all we could to save him, but his condition only worsens.
{np}The Dark Knights had a hand in this, didn't they.
{np}He was tortured, yes, and made to quaff a vile draught meant to loosen the lips...and the mind.
{np}Father...
{np}Let us go.
{np}As I told you, I've come only to speak with the leader of your order.{pp}I want no bloodshed, nor do I intend harm upon any of your followers.
{np}Lies from the mouth of a murderer!{pp}Why bring soldiers if not to spill blood?
{np}I am true to my word, but if you attack, we will be forced to defend ourselves!
{np}We do not fear death, for the Great Father will receive our souls.{pp}But for those who abandon faith for the fist, only hell awaits!
{np}Lies from the mouth of a murderer!{pp}Why come bearing arms if you truly want no bloodshed?
{np}Lies from the mouth of a murderer!{pp}Why come attended by soldiers and bearing arms if you truly want no bloodshed?
{np}This parley has taken an ill turn...
{np}Sir, the enemy approaches!

{np}But that's {hero}!
What's he doing here?
{np}He's come to kill us―what else?
{np}Impossible! He would never do such a thing!
{np}You mean to suggest he has come to parley? Then why does he not approach from the front gates?
{np}You're right... He's not come to talk.
{np}I did not take you for a thief, come to stab us in the back!{pp}We will defend the Order with our lives!
{np}This castle shelters only the priests and followers of our order. We wish you no harm.{pp}Please, leave at once and do not return.
{np}I've come only to talk!
{np}Then why do I hear the cries of the wounded outside our walls?
{np}Leave here! You must leave! This is no place for your kind!
{np}What did you say? Abuna Prancet?
{np}Father, it is I! {hero}!

{np}Ah... {hero}.
You've come at last.
{np}There is something I must tell you...
{np}It's about my sister, isn't it?
{np}Catiua...is not your sister, as you know.{pp}She is the last remnant of Dorgalua's line...the Princess Versalia Oberyth.
{np}Catiua's mother was one of the queen's handmaidens...a girl named Mannaflora.
{np}You wanted to speak with me? What of?
{np}I was hoping, Your Highness, that I might be granted a short leave.
{np}I am dismayed!{pp}Do you not know you're the only one in this castle to whom I can confide my heart, Mannaflora?
{np}...The more your betrayal cuts to the quick.{pp}Did you think me blind?
{np}Forgive me!
{np}I should have known that a king risen from the peasantry would prefer a simple, country girl.
{np}Your forgiveness, I beg you!
{np}Forgive you!? I might as soon strangle you, you...{pp}You will serve me for the rest of your days, Mannaflora. Do you understand? My slave, till you die!
{np}Wait...surely you are not with child!
{np}She gave birth to Catiua not long after departing the castle.
{np}How is Mannaflora?
{np}I feared as much.{pp}The strain was too much for her delicate heart to bear.
{np}So...that is Versalia.
{np}Is that to be her name? Versalia?
{np}It was His Highness's wish to have his daughter named so.
{np}We should tell him. He will want to know.
{np}Have you not heard? Queen Vernotta will bear her own child a month hence.{pp}No. It is best that only you and I know of this.
{np}Then, what should I do with the child?
{np}Keep her.{pp}You lost a child recently...Catiua, was it? Raise this one in her stead.
{np}As my own flesh and blood?
{np}Yes. For her sake, and the good of Valeria.
{np}But how...
{np}I am sure you will find a way.{pp}Ah, I have something for you.
{np}Take these necklaces. They should fetch a good price.
{np}What? Where are these from?
{np}They were a gift from His Highness, to celebrate the birth of his child.{pp}He intended that the blue be given to a prince, the red to a princess.
{np}But...I could not sell these!

{np}You will need money if you're to raise a child. And a princess, besides.{pp}You and I both grew up commons. You know what it is to need. What we must do...{pp}Give it no more thought, Prancet. This is the only way.
{np}But Brantyn deceived me...{pp}He used his knowledge of Mannaflora and the girl to advance his position within the Church.

{np}I...erred, {hero}, when the king passed away.{pp}Had I only offered up Catiua then, this war might never have come to pass.{pp}But I...
I couldn't let her go.{pp}When I heard her call me "Father," I could not take that away from her...or her from me.
{np}I had no idea...
{np}The Dark Knights have searched long and hard for Catiua.{pp}But not to make her sovereign of Valeria. They pursue another purpose.
{np}You know this purpose?
{np}Yes...her crowning ceremony was for show...{pp}They don't want her upon a throne... They want King Dorgalua's legacy.
{np}What legacy? Some sort of artifact?
{np}I do not know what it is... Only that it rests with the king.{pp}Now that they have Catiua...they seek the tomb.
{np}And my sister knows where it is?
{np}No...she knows nothing.{pp}Yet her role is vital. Only one who shares the Dynast-King's blood can undo the seal upon the tomb.
{np}They're using her.
{np}Yes, and when she has...fulfilled her purpose...they'll―*cough*
{np}Father, you must rest!
{np}Listen to me, {hero}! You must save Catiua.{pp}You are the only one who can. You can lead her to her rightful destiny...{pp}Do this for us...for Valer―*cough*
{np}Father!
{np}Find Mreuva!{pp}He...was once Archiereus in our order... He can help you.
{np}Say no more, Father. You must conserve your strength!

{np}Know it is not about {pal 16}you{palreset}. Become a stone along the path to our salvation...{pp}You must look with clear eyes, {hero}! Make the right choice!{pp}Lead us along the true path...make our way...{pp}Do this...only this...
{np}You mustn't talk. You must rest!

{np}{hero}...
Forgive...me.
{np}Father!!!
{np}There is something else you must know.
{np}Can it not wait?
{np}No...{pp}It concerns you and the regent, Brantyn.
{np}He and your father were siblings. True brothers by blood.
{np}Brantyn's my uncle!?{pp}Then who am I?
{np}Your true name...is {hero} Morne...{pp}You are Bakram.
{np}That's madness! I won't believe it.{pp}Me? Bakram?
{np}Please, good sir. Calm. Think back.{pp}When you were quite young, you resided with Abuna Prancet in the Royal City of Heim.
{np}Sibyl...you lie!
{np}I wish it were so, but I speak true. As a child, you oft played on the grounds of Archiereus Mreuva's villa.
{np}Stop this, please!
{np}You spent your days in play with Mreuva's four daughters there...
{np}...Go on.
{np}You were closest to the girl who shared your birth year...{pp}One day, as you played by the water, this girl wandered too deep and began to drown.
{np}How do you know that?
{np}But...but that was my sister who was drowning...{pp}No, she saved me...I remember...
{np}In her struggling, the girl struck her head...leaving a small scar.
{np}It...was you?
{np}It was my eldest sister, Cerya, who fished us out.
{np}How is this possible?
{np}I am the daughter of Mreuva, who was once Archiereus of Philaha.
{np}I...I cannot...
{np}You can. You must, {hero}.{pp}You are who you were born to be.
{np}Now, stand, {hero}!{pp}What you are, who you are, has no bearing on who you will become!{pp}Surely you did not dream of a kingdom for one people only?{pp}Remember your father's words!
{np}Yes... It's as you say. It does not matter who I am.{pp}It matters only how I live, what I achieve.{pp}Thank you, Sibyl Olivya.
{np}I am pleased. You {pal 16}are{palreset} the {hero} I remember.
{np}Olivya!
{np}Cerya, Cistina! How I rejoice to see you again.
{np}What are you doing in Brigantys? Where is Father?
{np}...I know not where Father is.
{np}How is that possible? You were with him!

{np}He...blamed himself for your departure from the Order.{pp}His days were spent locked in his quarters, though I believe his heart wandered elsewhere.{pp}When he did leave the castle, on the night the Dark Knights attacked Rhime, he never returned.
{np}Where might he have gone?

{np}I may know. The Hagia Banhamuba.{pp}It is a place of worship to Ishtar, Goddess of Light. Father studied there in his youth.{pp}If he has left the Order, he has slipped from his faith. He would go there to find direction, I am sure of it.
{np}You may be right.
{np}Let us pray I am.
{np}We must go to the Hagia Banhamuba at once, then!
{np}Wait―where is our sister, Sherri?
{np}That's right. There were four of you, weren't there.
{np}Sherri has betrayed us. She's gone to Brantyn.
{np}What? That cannot be!
{np}I fear it is, Olivya.{pp}After leaving the Order, Sherri surrendered herself to the Bakram.{pp}She serves as Brantyn's right hand now.
{np}My sister... My sister.
{np}How I rejoiced to hear you were with {hero}, Cerya.{pp}When I learned that the Dark Knights had destroyed the Liberation Front, I feared the worst.
{np}Never mind me. What of Father?

{np}How is that possible?
You were with him!
{np}How is that possible? You promised to stay by his side, to watch over him!
{np}Please, Cerya. Have you any idea where he might have gone?
{np}Wait―where are our sisters, Sherri and Cistina?
{np}Cistina is dead.

{np}And Sherri―Sherri has betrayed us.
She's gone to Brantyn.
{np}We are alone now, Olivya―you and I.
{np}I last saw Cistina at Boed Fortress. We parted ways there.{pp}Neither Cerya nor I know what's become of her.
{np}What of Sherri, then?
{np}I fear it is, Olivya.{pp}After leaving the Order, Sherri surrendered herself to the Bakram.{pp}I hear she serves as Brantyn's right hand now.
{np}Cistina and I had misgivings about an alliance... She left the Resistance.{pp}I've not seen her since, nor do I know where she's gone.
{np}How I rejoiced to hear you were with the Resistance, Cistina.{pp}When I learned that the Dark Knights had destroyed the Liberation Front, I feared the worst.
{np}What!? Father's missing? Wherever could he have gone?
{np}I do not know. In truth, I hoped you might have some idea, Sister.
{np}I...how could I know?
{np}Just think. Search your memories for anything, anything at all.
{np}Wait, of course! The shrine to Ishtar!
{np}I've not heard of any such shrine on this isle.

{np}Of course you wouldn't have. It's known by a different name now. Few venture there.{pp}You've heard of the old hagia on Banhamuba? That is the shrine to Ishtar.{pp}Cerya once told me that Father studied there in his youth.
{np}And you believe him to be there now?
{np}But where are Cerya and Sherri?
{np}Cistina!
{np}Cerya is dead.

{np}Sherri...
Sherri has surrendered to the Bakram.
{np}I last saw Cerya at Boed Fortress. We parted ways there.{pp}Neither Cistina nor I know what's become of her.
{np}Cerya and I had misgivings about an alliance... She left the Resistance.{pp}I've not seen her since, nor do I know where she's gone.

{np}I received a report that Boed Fortress had been taken by the Dark Knights, and the Liberation Front destroyed to the last man.{pp}Yet Cerya's body was never found... If she yet lives, I know not where.
{np}Let us find your father, Olivya.{pp}Have you any idea where he might be?
{np}Perhaps...he lost his faith?

{np}It may seem odd, but as you rise in the ranks of the church, your duties become less of faith and more of politics.{pp}Men like Balbatos and Brantyn are such―their power as regent or steward becomes more important than their devotion.{pp}I watched as my father dirtied his own hands...full aware of what he did.

{np}After Dorgalua passed away, my father lost in a struggle for power with Brantyn, and so lost his rank as archiereus.{pp}But though he could now return to his faith, free from political machinations, he was not pleased.{pp}That is when my sisters left. They could not accept that he had changed, that faith and politics are links of a single chain.{pp}The teachings of god are a compass needle for the righteous man, a way for all to live in peace and happiness.{pp}Throw yourself into the maelstrom that is governance―as long as you follow the teachings, your course will be true.{pp}But my father... My father lost his faith. He set out upon the same path as Brantyn before him.
{np}So...perhaps he has left to find his faith once more?
{np}It...is possible.
{np}The temple to Philaha is in Heim...but he could not have returned there.
{np}Then where could he have gone? I've not heard of any other temple to Philaha in these isles.
{np}My father once spoke to me of an ancient shrine, a hagia on Banhamuba.{pp}We might start there.
{np}I can think of no other course of action... To Banhamuba, then, {hero}.
{np}Wait, you're {hero}! What are {pal 16}you{palreset} doing here!?
{np}I might ask the same of you! What are the Bakram about!?
{np}If you want to know, you'll have to beat it from me!
{np}You're after Mreuva too, aren't you? ...Waste of time.{pp}Too late... Our friends...have him by now!
{np}No use to feign ignorance, Father. I know you know.
{np}I do not. And I wouldn't tell you if I did!
{np}Is that any way to speak to your own daughter?{pp}Or...have you abandoned me, as you did Mother?
{np}I have abandoned no one.
{np}Then you'll tell me where to find the Apocrypha.
{np}You'll have no aid from me in that foolishness, Sherri. None!
{np}You leave me no choice but to bring you with me.
{np}What!? Unhand me!
{np}I'm sure you'll change your mind once we've reached Heim.
{np}Do not do this, Sherri!
{np}Prepare him for the journey.
{np}Time to leave.
{np}Abuna Mreuva, are you all right?
{np}Who are you?
{np}Would you know me if I said I was {hero} of Golyat?
{np}Prancet's son!
{np}There will be time for talk later. Let me handle this.
{np}Yes...but please, spare the woman.
{np}She is my daughter, Sherri.
{np}...Very well.
{np}The Father watch over you.

{np}I always knew LeRozza was useless. All breeding and no substance, that one.{pp}What about you, {hero}? I seem to remember you as a fey child, delicate as a rose...{pp}But no matter. Such fancies will not stay my blade.

{np}Sherri! Stop this at once!
We mustn't fight one another!
{np}Then surrender to the Bakram, and it will end!{pp}You prolong this by clinging to Father...a man who couldn't even guard his own wife!
{np}Surely you cannot lay that at his feet!{pp}The Bakram killed Mother, not him... The very Bakram you now serve!
{np}You are wrong, Olivya. When a man vies for power and loses, he pays a price.{pp}Mother's blood is on our father's hands!

{np}How can you say Father lost, when it is you who have lost your way, Sister?{pp}You saw him as he truly is, and you could not accept it. So you chose to throw it all away!{pp}It is you who have lost!
{np}Please, Sister, lay down your arms! We do not wish harm upon you!
{np}Harm to me? I am not so careless as that.{pp}My strength will not fail me!
{np}I fear that strength will be your undoing, Sister.{pp}The Dark Knights brought the Liberation Front to ruin, and they will do the same for the Bakram!
{np}And your Almorican friends are any different?{pp}Do you not wield {pal 16}your{palreset} strength against us? You take pains to find fault with me, when you only need look at yourself!
{np}We do not fight to seize power for ourselves, Sister!{pp}We seek an end this bloody conflict...even though it mean more bloodshed.
{np}Stand down, Sherri. Return with your men to Heim.
{np}A colder reception than I'd hoped for, Sister.{pp}Though I am glad to see you live, even though your Front does not.
{np}Yes, I live.{pp}And I will bear my shame until the Dark Knights are driven from the isles forever!

{np}Thank you for freeing me from the Bakram.{pp}I will not forget your loyalty and service.
