{np}I wish only for this warring to be over. Peace cannot come a day too soon.{pp}Nor will it come without the help of the Order of {order}.{pp}I expect great deeds of you.
{np}And you shall have them, even if it mean our lives.{pp}Your Highness, you are welcome to remain here in Phidoch―

{np}Abuna Mreuva!{pp}If I am to lead my people, I cannot afford to remain holed away, far from where the arrows fly.{pp}I will join the ranks, in the front. I will show my people and my soldiers who fights for them.
{np}But, Your Highness!
{np}Do not worry on my behalf. That...is an order, Abuna.
{np}As Your Highness wishes.
{np}About the front lines...
{np}The Bakram move independently now. The Dark Knights have lost the regent's trust.
{np}Then a resolution is at hand.{pp}Let us return to the city my father built. Back to Heim to end this for all time!
{np}Ready the troops!
{np}Well. How did I do?
{np}You've really come into your own, Sister. Father would be proud.
{np}Come into my own? Odd, when I felt like someone else entirely.
{np}Not to worry, Catiua. You will do splendidly.
{np}I hope you're right.
{np}Still, you should stay here in the castle. For your safety, and that of―
{np}I said I wouldn't, and I meant it. I won't be some figurehead for my people to hoist and carry about.{pp}You'll come to my rescue should I get in any real trouble, won't you?
{np}Well, of course, but...
{np}It's settled then.
{np}The late king loved the front no less. Must be in the blood.
{np}Yes. The Dynast-King's spirit will protect me.
{np}That's all well and good, but still...be careful.
{np}Don't worry. I will.
{np}{FF 9A 03}You received a Princess's Mark.
{np}Right yourself, {hero}! This is no time for maudlin reflection!{pp}Much remains to be done, and swiftly.
{np}I doubt that not. And all of it meaningless, without her.
{np}So was it fated. You cannot blame yourself.
{np}Fate? It was not Fate who killed my sister!{pp}It was me!
{np}Leave us.
{np}You must calm yourself, {hero}.{pp}If your men see you waver so, you will lose your command, and then the war.{pp}What is done is done. No amount of mourning will raise Catiua from the grave.

{np}With Catiua gone, only one path remains to us.{pp}The Dark Knights plotted her murder―what more reason do we need to brand them traitors and cast them from our shores!{pp}After all, it was they who drove the princess to her doom.
{np}No. It was I who robbed her of hope. I did this...

{np}What are you saying!{pp}Have you any idea how many lives you hold in your hand, {pal 16}Commander{palreset}?{pp}Prancet was right, you know. It is you who must lead us toward peace.{pp}Never forget that!

{np}The Bakram stir.
There is no avoiding conflict now.{pp}I have ordered our men to prepare for an all-out attack.{pp}You {pal 16}must{palreset} put this behind you.
Our armies need their commander, {hero}.
{np}{FF 9A 03}You received a Sovereign's Mark.
{np}Sadly, we were unable to save the Princess Versalia.{pp}I lacked the strength... The failure is mine.{pp}Forgive me.

{np}But do not forgive the Dark Knights!{pp}They abandoned the princess when they realized their own defeat was inevitable.{pp}I tried to persuade her to our cause, but the Dark Knights had sown deep the seeds of doubt and fear.{pp}She took her own life...
It is for her that we fight as well.

{np}We're ready to march, my lord.
Just give us the word.

{np}Good.{pp}We move against the Bakram and the Dark Knights with everything we have.{pp}The final battle awaits.
Onward to Heim!
{np}You did well.
{np}I tire of this theater!

{np}Do not say that.
{pal 16}You{palreset} must bring this war to an end.{pp}If that means enduring a little "theater," I think it a fair price.

{np}I watched as my sister died...
Was that part of the price as well?
{np}You must push such thoughts from your mind. Naught will come of it.{pp}Right or wrong, let history be the judge.{pp}Now you must focus on the task at hand, {hero}.
{np}Past time {hero} showed his face!{pp}Better men than him have died trying to cross Iorumza Canyon. His bones will join the rest!
{np}Done in by...Walister dogs...

{np}So they move from Barnicia...
They'll find these lines well defended.{pp}We will not let them reach the open desert. Move!
{np}Hope of redeeming my family's honor...dies with me...

{np}Listen well!
This town is the last before they reach the royal city herself.{pp}Should they reach her, they will plunder her stores and slaughter our families.{pp}If you find yourself wavering in the coming battle, let thoughts of {pal 16}that{palreset} rekindle your flame!
{np}Rest comes...at last...
{np}Hold them here! We can't let them into the castle!
{np}I am Versalia Oberyth. Withdraw your forces and convey a message to the regent:{pp}The Resistance and I want an end to fighting. We can resolve this with words, not swords.
{np}You talk of peace even as you occupy our city and besiege our castle?{pp}We will not parley at the point of a sword!
{np}Sherri Phoraena... Then your betrayal is no rumor.{pp}His Eminence gave you refuge, and this is how you repay him?
{np}I make no excuses for what I've done. Put tooth to your words, if you dare!
{np}A Loslorien knight marches with the Resistance―and a commander, no less.{pp}Has Lodis betrayed us?
{np}His Eminence has charged me with defending the postern gate. I must show him that trust was not misplaced!
{np}I've failed you...Eminence.
{np}You're bold to attack our front gates. Or perhaps merely foolish.
{np}I cannot open this gate, not even by your command, Majesty.{pp}Return whence you came...lest misfortune befall you.
{np}It looks like our audience with the regent must be won by force.

{np}The Magus Sherri?
So you have betrayed the Bakram!
{np}I have no words for you, save to say that you are my foe.{pp}Now draw your swords!
{np}Ozma of Loslorien? Could it be? What is she doing with those rebels!?{pp}Lord Tartaros remains at His Excellency's side, does he not?{pp}Or...has Lodis betrayed us!?
{np}They put up a good fight...but we must persevere!{pp}Let the gates fall, as long as the enemy falls with them.{pp}Lessen their numbers and we will ease Sir Latimer's task!
{np}Sir Latimer...this passes to you, now!
{np}The Almoricans are a fearsome foe. We are like to be overwhelmed.{pp}If you value your life above your honor, leave now, and I will look the other way.
{np}I'll not offer again.
{np}Good. You do the Knights of Bakram proud.
{np}If we are to die this day, let our deaths be glorious!
{np}Knights of Bakram! Sheathe your swords. We have no wish to see you die.{pp}Surrender, and let us put this senseless bloodshed behind us.

{np}No doubt you're right.
Surrendering would spare much blood on both sides.{pp}But honor demands we fight to the last!
{np}Glory...to the Knights of Bakram...

{np}Your Eminence!
They've breached the castle gates!
{np}{hero} goes too far!
{np}How stand the knights of Lodis?{pp}You've lost my trust. I hope you've not lost your nerve as well!{pp}Or do you fancy taking my city from me, as a coda to losing the princess in Barnicia!?
{np}Sheathe your anger, Your Excellency. It serves nothing here.
{np}I thought you in hiding, Lord Tartaros, so little have I seen of you.{pp}Finally muster the strength to stand in that armor of yours?
{np}You appear to be {pal 16}embattled{palreset}, Your Excellency.

{np}A jest, yes? We are two rabbits in the same pot.{pp}Is it the largely uncontested loss of Phidoch and Barnicia that weighs upon your shoulders, or shame at your own inadequacy?{pp}Perhaps you should ride out and {pal 16}face our foes{palreset} if you do not wish to become even more of a laughingstock!
{np}I did not come to talk strategy.{pp}I am come to bid you farewell.
{np}You would abandon us―your allies―now!?

{np}Your Excellency should learn to govern his tongue.{pp}Had you but followed our instructions, none of this would have come to pass.{pp}I include the matter of the princess when I say this!{pp}All you needed to do was abandon that Eltynaha puppet of yours and offer up the throne―{pp}It is what the people wanted!
{np}Your counsel is not welcome here, knight!
{np}Do you not see!?{pp}You are defeated, Your Excellency!
{np}Oh? Truly?
{np}It is you who have lost, {pal 16}sir{palreset}!
{np}Barbas! What madness has come over you!?
{np}Your time has passed, Brother!
{np}Enemies of Heim! Your march ends here!
{np}It is only a matter of time before your castle falls! Lay down your sword if you value your life.
{np}Would you do the same were you the defender here?{pp}Or would honor prevent you as it does me?{pp}The Bakram will fight to the end!
{np}An unexpected...turn.
{np}I'll be taking this.
{np}Traitorous worm!
{np}Is it not you who betray Lodis?
{np}You meant to use Brynhildr to break the seal, princess or no!
{np}This sword holds the power of the gods. No mortal seal can stand against it.{pp}Yet you had us scouring the islands for a woman long dead and an uncharitable princess.
{np}Is this true, High Champion?
{np}You wanted Dorgalua's legacy for yourself!
{np}Do you mean to...mock us to death?
{np}No need.{pp}When the Almoricans find you, they'll do it for me.
{np}Are you all right, Balxephon?
{np}Andoras. How can you have any part in this?

{np}Must I spell it out for you, Volaq?
How I have yearned for this day!{pp}The day my mother and father, my brothers and sisters are avenged.
{np}Still you cling to the Nildahme royal house?
{np}The reins change hands...{pp}Perhaps it was only a matter of time.
{np}Catiua, the sword―nothing more than keys.

{np}Lodis can take these isles whenever it likes.{pp}For now, Valeria is best left to her people. It's only a question of who rules, and how.{pp}If nothing else, our sojourn here has taught me that.{pp}―Can you move, Balxephon?
{np}Well enough, I think.
{np}It's time we were leaving Heim.
{np}Well?
{np}The old coot Balxephon had it!
{np}We'd best not tarry.
{np}What are you doing!? They're coming! Make ready to meet them in battle!
{np}Then, to the Hanging Gardens, as discussed.

{np}What do you mean?
...What are you planning!?
{np}We're done taking orders from you!

{np}I'm the regent!
How dare you speak to me like that!
{np}It's over, Brantyn!
{np}Bah, sooner than I expected!
{np}The Dark Knights...fleeing?
{np}We've helped you as we said we would.{pp}This...this is your dungpile to spade.
{np}No! Barbas!
{np}{hero}! As you are my nephew, hear me! It is not too late!{pp}Kneel to me, and together we will rule Valeria!
{np}It is you who should kneel, Brantyn. Throw down your sword and rein in your troops, and your life will be spared.{pp}Resist, and we will show no mercy!

{np}But the Dark Knights have left! You saw them!{pp}It was they who brought this upon us, not I―{pp}Yes, I did their bidding...but I did it to save Valeria.{pp}When we lost King Dorgalua, we could no longer hold Lodis at bay―who could!?{pp}Had we fought to drive them back, they would have killed us all!

{np}If the people are so dear to you, why did you not inform the king that his daughter was alive?{pp}All Valeria would have welcomed the news after the prince's passing...{pp}Look at me and tell me you did not seek to use her―as you used my father!

{np}Yes, I sought to use her...and where is the wrong in that?{pp}I did what any lowborn man would do. When you lack a silver spoon, you fashion one of steel.{pp}You understand. You're like me.{pp}Where you carved out your destiny with a sword, I used my wits. But there's little difference, in the end.{pp}We both walk toward our future treading upon the backs of others.{pp}Deny it, and you only deceive yourself!
{np}Hello, Brantyn.
{np}After all I did for you, Sherri...how could you side against me?{pp}You will die a traitor!

{np}I, a traitor?
You turned on me long before I had the chance.
{np}You still think highly of yourself, I see. A keen eye for fault in anyone but yourself.{pp}You abandoned your faith, abandoned the Bakram―it is a wonder the Resistance will even have you.
{np}They trust me because I choose to trust. In my father, my sisters...myself.{pp}It is only the weak who cling to power.
{np}You deceive yourself to think so. {pal 16}All{palreset} men desire power.{pp}Few ever come to possess it. Those who do have a duty to use it justly.

{np}Such arrogance...
If only I had seen it sooner.{pp}I lost all I had for my error.
I will not repeat it!

{np}Regent, put away your weapons.{pp}Can we not discuss truce?
Surely there is benefit to be had by us both.
{np}A most convincing argument, Your Majesty.{pp}Your royal blood does much to conceal the mark the provinces have left on you.

{np}Three times I sent envoys to treat for peace before moving against Heim. Each time you refused them.{pp}A decision reached with Lodis at your back, I should imagine.{pp}But look about you.
I see no Knights Loslorien.{pp}You cannot win. Is it not a lord's duty to watch the curtain fall with grace?
{np}We need no help from Lodis!{pp}I will not surrender the country I built to some baseborn girl, no matter how thickly Dorgalua's blood runs in her!

{np}So be it.
We fight to the last.

{np}Impossible...
It...it cannot be...

{np}We must not bare our swords against them, even if they resist.{pp}The Dark Knights are our enemy, not the Bakram who follow them.{pp}Dispatch a messenger. Inform them of our intent. If we treat them like rebels, we will only push them away.
{np}It will be done, Your Majesty.
{np}Do likewise with the Resistance. It cannot appear we show favor.{pp}Any who act against my orders will meet punishment swift and fierce.

{np}The war is finally over.{pp}From this day forward we are no longer Walister or Bakram. We are Valerian.{pp}The past must be forgotten. If any hatred still burns within you, shut it away.{pp}We must forge a new kingdom together.
{np}We swear you our undying allegiance, Princess Versalia.
{np}I thank you.

{np}The Dark Knights have sought refuge in the Hanging Gardens. We travel there to rid ourselves of them for good and all.{pp}A great battle awaits us. But beyond it, peace!{pp}We must take up the sword once more. For Valeria!
{np}For Valeria!
{np}It will be done, my lord.
{np}We must do likewise with the Resistance, of course.{pp}If any of our men make protest or show disrespect to the Bakram, they will be punished.
{np}If I may, my lord.
{np}It's...no easy matter.{pp}I'm told there's been a good deal of rapine and plunder in the city.

{np}There is worse.
Elders beaten, women...defiled.
{np}My soldiers do this!?
{np}Crude though it may be, many do battle not for glory or duty but for the spoils.{pp}We cannot rid ourselves of them all.
{np}How will you deal with these, my lord?

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} We must look the other way.
2. They will be punished for their crimes.
{np}They will receive their due, but for now, I see no other course but to look the other way.
{np}We have more pressing concerns.
{np}Today, we begin the long work of peace.{pp}We are no longer Walister or Bakram. We are Valerians.{pp}The war is done.
{np}We hereby swear an oath to serve, your loyal retainers unto death.
{np}They will be punished as they deserve. Good?
{np}Right this way.
{np}Is...something wrong?
{np}No. Nothing.
{np}Ah! M'lord Sir {hero}!
{np}And the p-princess! M'lady!
{np}Lanselot?{pp}What...!?

{np}What's this?
Lanselot's music box?
{np}Ah... Aaahhh... Aaaaaah!
{np}It couldn't... Is it really you?

{np}There, there. It's all right.
In your chair.
{np}The...Holy Knight?{pp}What ill fortune is this?
{np}M'lady...?
{np}Do you know this man?

{np}I'm sorry.
'Twasn't right of me to pry.

{np}No worry.
But I must ask―
{np}Wait, there's something you should see, m'lord.
{np}The sword he carried.
{np}Lombardia!
{np}{FF 9A 03}You received the sword Lombardia.
{np}So these are the Hanging Gardens.
{np}Ah! We've been waiting for you, {hero}!
{np}You've run out of places to hide, Martym!
{np}Who's hiding, I ask?{pp}Lodis barely needs lift a finger to send legions of troops to your pitiful isles.
{np}Is that a threat?
{np}I never make threats.{pp}You, deal with him!
{np}He's getting away!
{np}Well, you certainly took your time.
{np}You Knights of Lodis have a rare gift of flight. A useful skill for cowards.

{np}You'll regret those words!
A knight knows how to pick his battles.
{np}Easy, Martym.{pp}Go to Barbas. Leave this one to me.
{np}Feh!
{np}Fortunate for you, boy!
{np}Not again!
{np}You face me, {hero}! Let us {pal 16}end{palreset} this!
{np}You've done well for yourself. This war's made a hero of you.
{np}I did not take up the sword to become anything.
{np}Maybe so, maybe so!{pp}In fact, perhaps it was the duke's idea. Men such as he have use of heroes.{pp}I'm sure you understand... The title served you well following the duke's passing, after all.
{np}I mislike your reasoning. I do not do this for power!
{np}Yet here you are, a man of power!{pp}As a hero, you led your army, and now you must fulfill their wishes and become the next Dynast-King.
{np}It is not I who shared his blood...
{np}Now, come. Defeat us, and claim Valeria as your own!
{np}Yet here you are, a man of power!{pp}As a hero, you led your army, and now you would fulfill their wishes and place Catiua upon the throne!
{np}This is {pal 16}not{palreset} about power! I do my duty!
{np}As you wish.{pp}Now, do your duty. Defeat us, and claim Valeria for your kin!
{np}Why not leave these isles altogether, Andoras?
{np}You know why I remain.
{np}Dorgalua's legacy.{pp}But why the rift with Sir Lanselot? The promise of riches bring out your true colors?
{np}Riches? You think we're here for coin?
{np}Aren't you?
{np}Your answer lies upon the road ahead. Defeat me if you would find it.
{np}Cease this, Andoras! You are finished.
{np}How can you be so certain?{pp}You know as well as I what lies hidden in these gardens!{pp}A miracle is before me, and I will not pass up my chance to claim it!
{np}Clinging to miracles is ever a sign of weakness―{pp}I have seen what good can come from perseverance and adherence to principle.{pp}Give up your miracle and stand on your own feet, Andoras!
{np}Ha! Green as a spring morn!{pp}I cannot understand how someone of your quality ever made it into the order.
{np}{pal 16}You{palreset} find fault with {pal 16}me{palreset}?{pp}With such fine nobles in House Nildahme, it's no wonder your people suffer.

{np}You have it wrong, Ozma.
It's you who will suffer!
{np}Death comes...too soon.
{np}Where's Barbas? Martym? Where have they gone?

{np}To Dorgalua's...tomb...
Both of them are there...
{np}You've found the tomb? Where? Tell me!

{np}The tomb? Heh...
Beneath the gardens...{pp}This tower...is his tomb-marker... But you're too late...{pp}Barbas is opening the...seal even now.
{np}But he can't open it without Catiua!

{np}No...
He has the Xenobian blade.
{np}Then I haven't much time...

{np}Wait, {hero}...listen.{pp}The Nildahme perished...like these islands, our people...failed to join as one.{pp}It is only...a matter of time before...Lodis invades.{pp}You must make...Valeria...strong. Like a rock...

{np}What's taking so long?
They'll be here any minute now!

{np}Patience, Martym.
The seal is not what I expected...

{np}Look around you, Barbas.
We're all that's left.{pp}I've had my fill of traps and seals!
{np}Be silent, or be silenced!

{np}Barbas! Martym!
There's nowhere left to run!
{np}Andoras must have fallen.

{np}This is it!
The words to break the seal!
{np}Be quick about it!
{np}Berloda en barinda, phaexanra len Philaha.{pp}Seal born of age-old strife, you've served your duty well. In the name of the Great Father Philaha, I release you!
{np}It's done!
{np}Hold them off!
{np}Damn!

{np}Behold the holy blade Brynhildr, deifacted gift of the heavens.{pp}By that name most sacred, hear my plea.{pp}Gate divine, earthly prison of accurst gods. Throw wide your doors! The Great Father commands it!

{np}Is that all?
I had expected something...more.

{np}Martym! Barbas!
No farther!
{np}Persistent, aren't you?
{np}You seem bent on meddling in our plans.
{np}Lay down your weapons and―
{np}Save your breath, {hero}. We both know that will never happen.{pp}You want to kill us. I see it in your eyes. Put down your words, and take up your sword.
{np}The dead of Golyat and Rhime deserve vengeance!
{np}It begins.
{np}What's happening?
{np}Dorgalua's legacy, you simpleton.
{np}You really don't know, do you?{pp}A man came to this place once, long ago...
{np}What man was this?

{np}A valiant warrior who used his strength and skill to possess all he desired.{pp}But there was one foe he could not conquer: death.{pp}Misfortune took his beloved son, and soon after, his wife.{pp}In his despair, he prayed for their return. I need not tell you his prayers went unanswered.{pp}Overcome with wrath, he renounced his faith and sought instead the power of the dark gods.{pp}He descended into the hells where they make their fastness.
{np}...I trust you know the legend of the ogre battle?
{np}The battle between men and ogres in the age of myths.
{np}Yes. The struggle that decided who would rule this earth.{pp}The gods of light sided with men, and the dark gods with the ogres.{pp}For eons the war raged...
{np}What is it to us?
{np}Do you know how the legend ends?
{np}Men were victorious, and the ogres retreated to the darkness.{pp}A tale every child has heard at his mother's skirts.
{np}What do you find so amusing?
{np}It is no nursery tale.
{np}These ruins are the very gate to hell. The Chaos Gate!
{np}The man who journeyed into the abyss is your precious Dynast-King, Dorgalua!
{np}I think we've finally gotten the gate's attention.

{np}The darkness awaits...
And all the power it holds!
{np}I can't let you go.

{np}Of course you can't.
Which is why you must die.{pp}You'll need no gate to enter hell!
{np}You would venture into the abyss to claim this power?{pp}If what you say is true, why is it King Dorgalua never returned?
{np}The gate was made to prevent darkness from entering our world.{pp}It's barred from this side. It cannot be opened from within.
{np}Dorgalua left his most trusted man to prepare for his return, but this gate keeper was easily slain.{pp}With the king missing, it was a simple task to declare him dead and claim the throne.
{np}You use the Xenobian sword, Brynhildr, to break the seal on the gate.

{np}Ah, Princess Versalia.
You grace us with your presence.
{np}If you did not need me to break the seal, why go to such lengths to win me to your side?
{np}The high champion must have known the sword was all we needed.{pp}He meant to use you to rule these pathetic isles.{pp}A waste, when Lodissian steel would serve.
{np}Small wonder Lord Tartaros would not keep counsel with you.{pp}You are too foolish to see his true purpose.
{np}What is this "true purpose" you speak of?

{np}You may rule people with the sword, but you will never win their hearts. Lord Tartaros understood this.{pp}It was not by might alone that you rebelled in Lodis.{pp}You rallied under the banner of overthrowing a corrupt senate and installed the just High Priest Sardian in its place.
{np}What has that to do with these provincial goatherds!?
{np}Brynhildr's mysteries are wasted on the likes of you.{pp}Had it been up to you, no doubt you would have killed me and gone on ruling through brute force.{pp}Lord Tartaros sought a better way!
{np}We're to believe that we were no more than pieces being moved by some unseen hand?

{np}I underestimated you.
I didn't think you'd realized.
{np}I'll dash your head in, you misbegotten filth!
{np}It's time you paid for what you did in Golyat!
{np}And {pal 16}you're{palreset} going to collect? You're welcome to try!

{np}Don't waste your words on this one, Martym. {pp}He's only {hero}'s lapdog.
Hear how he barks for his master?
{np}Maybe I am just a dog. But I'm here, standing before you! Are you man enough to face me?{pp}I'll tear out your throat with my bare teeth!

{np}A rabid cur, at that... All the better.
We fight!

{np}Barbas! Martym!
Heed sense, and flee with your lives!
{np}The traitor speaks, when she would do better to flee!{pp}When we lead you back to Lodis in chains, it will not go easy for you.
{np}It's you who've betrayed the Empire!{pp}I am come to restore Loslorien―to turn it from the treacherous path Balxephon embarked upon.{pp}But you...you have eyes only for wealth and power!
{np}Aren't you forgetting something? It was the high commander who sought to conceal Dorgalua's Legacy.{pp}We seek only to claim the treasure of the Chaos Gate for the glory of Lodis!
{np}The lie falls easily from your lips, but I will not believe it.{pp}The Dark Knights ought never have allowed your filth to sully their ranks!

{np}It is your {pal 16}guilt{palreset} speaks, woman!{pp}The name of House Glacius may curry favor back home, but it means nothing here.{pp}You should have stayed at home and married some rich, old nobleman, if any would have you.
{np}Barbas...how?
{np}Martym, you bloody fool!
{np}Bested by a...a pack of dogs.
{np}The gate―why won't it open!?
{np}I can't die... Not here.
{np}{FF 9A 03}You received the sword Brynhildr.

{np}So close.
So very close...
{np}A...fool I was to trust him.

{np}The flow of the streams has changed since last I was here...but it shouldn't pose a problem.

{np}Well, boy. What'll it be? Press onward? It won't be easy going.{pp}If you think you've seen foul things so far, there's more and worse ahead.{pp}I doubt you'll be finding that pirate's treasure, either.{pp}Time to stop and think about what you're really trying to accomplish here. Think well.
{np}We've come this far―it's not about the treasure.{pp}We'll continue.{pp}Besides...you're still hiding something.
{np}This is as far as I can take you. The way the water flows in here...it becomes a maze.{pp}Sorry, but I can't risk it.
{np}Then, we've gone as far as we can.
{np}Back to the surface.
{np}This as deep as it goes?
{np}Ah. The welcoming party's arrived.
{np}Who defiles our sacred ground...
{np}I feel a draft from up ahead.{pp}There's something beyond here, isn't there.
{np}Might be.

{np}Leave...
Leave here at once.
{np}Leave...or we will take your lives as penalty for your trespass.
{np}Azelstan... It's you!
{np}It's a trick. Not very clever, though.{pp}This is one face that won't come back to haunt me.
{np}Pain... Endless pain to those who defile the sacred ground...
{np}Don't worry. I'll lead you true.
{np}...Azelstan?
{np}Come with me, boy. I'll show you what a ghast thinks is worth protecting.
{np}I don't see anything like a treasure down here.{pp}Perhaps the rumors were...just rumors.
{np}What is this place?

{np}This is their sacred ground.
Well, more of a dead end than anything.
{np}You see the chest of coins there. Take it.{pp}Better than going home empty-handed.

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} {pal 16}This{palreset} is the treasure?
2. I cannot take this.
{np}{pal 16}This{palreset} is the treasure we've been searching for?
{np}Not as much as you were imagining, is it?{pp}Truth be told, this chest is more a grave marker than anything.
{np}Like a gravestone?
{np}Aye. This here's the place where the souls of pirates who die at sea come to rest.{pp}No one mourns them, so they wander until they find their way here.{pp}The Pirate's Graveyard, this.
{np}And the swords stuck into the ground around it?
{np}Left here by pirates...as proof they lived.

{np}A pirate's life is no glorious affair, and neither's his death.{pp}A few manage to come ashore, take a wife, raise a family...but most don't live half so wise.{pp}After your first captain and your last crew are gone, there's no one left to remember you.{pp}That's why they leave their swords. A nameless grave beats just nameless.{pp}If you can't leave your mark any other way, you leave it here.
{np}Thus, a sacred ground...and a treasure worth protecting.
{np}Or a desolate cliff strewn about with junk, depending on how you look at it. Heh.
{np}Is that why you came? To pay your respects?
{np}Ha! You think my heart beats as warm as that?
{np}I have a hard time thinking you came all this way just to reveal the true nature of this treasure.

{np}Aye. There was a time...when I lost sight for what was ahead. When my daughter died.{pp}I couldn't take the battle, so I came here. Maybe I was eager to join the ones who left these swords.{pp}The currents around here are treacherous things. Take your eyes off the sea for a moment, and she'll drag you down.

{np}From the moment I entered the cave, I didn't pause to rest or to think. I just kept walking deeper and deeper.{pp}I knew what this place was as soon as I stepped foot out here.{pp}I stood here a while...then went back the same way I'd come in.
{np}You just turned around?

{np}I did. This here's a place for those who went the full distance.{pp}I left my ship that day.{pp}Why? Because I had nothing more to do with it, that's why.{pp}I wasn't about to sail headlong into death like the ones here...or start a new life, either.{pp}Dread pirate? I was a coward who couldn't put his daughter's death behind him.
{np}But there is something that needs doing.{pp}Thanks for reminding me of that.
{np}Thank you for your help.
{np}Sorry there's not more for you to take home than this pile of coin.{pp}With luck, some of 'em will be old enough to have taken on a bit of value.

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} I can't take this.
2. However little, it will help.
{np}This coin's not for anyone to use. Least of all for war.{pp}I'll let it rest.
{np}Well. I wasn't expecting that from you.
{np}Let's return. We're not meant to be here.{pp}We've things yet to do.
{np}Every little bit helps.{pp}With all apologies to those resting here, I'll take it.
{np}A good choice. That is why you've come, after all.
{np}Let's get back.
{np}{FF 9A 03}You've claimed the Pirate's Treasure.

{np}I can't take this.
This place is no treasure trove.{pp}It serves another purpose, though I cannot say what.{pp}These swords thrust into the ground―someone left these here for something...{pp}As markers? Could this be...a grave?

{np}Aye. This here's the place where the souls of departed pirates come to rest.{pp}No one mourns them, so they wander until they find their way here.{pp}The Pirate's Graveyard, this.{pp}Everything they left here, they left as proof they lived.
{np}Even so.{pp}These things aren't for anyone to use. Least of all for war.{pp}I'll let it rest.
{np}What business've you got with Lobos?{pp}On second thought, it matters not. You see my hideout, you have to die.
{np}The...R-Resistance, were you? Never knew...

{np}What?
Why would this be sacred ground?
{np}Ah... Old friend. Or was it...enemy. You are their defender?{pp}Then I will take your strength, that it may serve a more worthy master...

{np}What? That's Azelstan!
...But why?
{np}I am Rackham...guide to the souls of those who live upon the sea.{pp}Leave this place at once... Leave while you may yet go with your lives.
{np}{hero} of Golyat! I've a score to settle with you on the hierophant's behalf.
{np}My people of Galgastan... Rise...
{np}So the grand leader of the Resistance takes pirate hunting into his own hands?{pp}Boys! They take us here, and we're all headed for the chopping block!{pp}Kill 'em all!
{np}Someone take...me to the sea. A dry grave's no...end for a pirate.
{np}Looking for something?{pp}You'd do well to leave while you still draw breath.{pp}Or you may lose your life before finding what you seek!
{np}I mastered time itself...but I could not stop my own time from coming.

{np}Never thought I'd meet {pal 16}you{palreset} here, {hero} of Golyat!{pp}I thought my hatred ebbed and gone, but the sight of your face brings it boiling back!{pp}I will strike you down...for my fallen brothers, and for the hierophant!

{np}G-Great Father...
Grant ye...rest for the souls of Galgastan.
{np}You call this chaos you bring us "freedom"? The Tigers of Burnham will teach you what it means to rule!
{np}Better to die...than live under you.
{np}Abuna Mreuva, there's something I've been meaning to ask you.
{np}Yes, {hero}?
{np}At the Hagia Banhamuba, Sherri mentioned something called the "Apocrypha."

{np}The Apocrypha?
I can't say I'm familiar.

{np}The Dark Knights are a formidable foe.{pp}We must gird ourselves well if we are to confront them. You know this, Abuna.{pp}With the Apocrypha grimoires in our possession, the odds shift in our favor.{pp}Please, Abuna. Tell me where they can be found.

{np}The Apocrypha are kept hidden for a reason.{pp}They contain a dreadful power. More than any man should wield.{pp}I know of one such man: King Rodrick of Brigantys.{pp}In the final days of the Dorgalua's great war, Rodrick used the Apocrypha in a desperate attempt to change the tide of the battle.{pp}His foes were wiped from the face of the earth...and his own armies with them.{pp}None save the invoker survived.

{np}This did not deter the king. He used the Apocrypha at every turn.{pp}You may not know it, but Brigania Flats was once a lush and fertile highland.{pp}The Apocrypha transformed it into the desolate waste it is today.{pp}Not even the laws of nature can withstand their power.

{np}Yet in the end, it was the Apocrypha that brought down King Rodrick.{pp}Even as he won the war, he lost the love of his people.{pp}After the war's end, King Dorgalua ordered the Apocrypha sealed away.{pp}The danger in the Apocrypha is not the knowledge itself, you see, but rather how it is used.{pp}King Rodrick was not up to the task. Do you think you will fare better?

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} I'm beginning to wonder.
2. I know I will.
{np}After hearing that, I'm not so sure.
{np}Better not to take the reins of a beast you can't control.{pp}There are many who still remember the horrors unleashed by the Apocrypha.
{np}Then let us forget we ever spoke of it.

{np}I am not King Rodrick.
I would never use such power so capriciously.

{np}If that is the way you will lead, I am obliged to follow.{pp}The eight Apocrypha were secreted throughout the isles. I know the location of but six.{pp}These are enshrined in temples, and each commands one of the elements.{pp}Of the remaining two, Light and Dark, I know nothing.
{np}I had heard that the six great fortresses of Valeria were once temples...{pp}But I saw nothing at any of them that would house so great an artifact.
{np}Of course not. I sealed them where unknowing eyes would not find them.{pp}To open the temple doors requires an oracle.
{np}Who are these oracles?
{np}The daughters of the abuna who forged the seal.
{np}{pal 16}Your{palreset} daughters?

{np}Bring one of them with you to each of the fortresses, and the way will open for you.{pp}Touched by the goddesses within the temple, they may be made a True Oracle, though they will serve you well in battle regardless.
{np}Alas, they are not with us, and the temples will remain sealed.{pp}Perhaps you will find the resting place of the other Apocrypha on some distant shore.
{np}O, Great Xoshonell, Goddess of Fire, admit me unto your sacred sanctum!
{np}I am servant to Xoshonell, Goddess of Fire.{pp}You who would become a True Oracle must face a trial. Defeat me, and prove your quality before the goddess.

{np}Magnificent...
A True Oracle you are.{pp}Unto you I grant the revelation and power of the goddess.
{np}{FF 9A 03}You received an Oracle's Mark.
{np}Magnificent...
{np}O, Great Hahnela, Goddess of Air, admit me unto your sacred sanctum!
{np}I am servant to Hahnela, Goddess of Air.{pp}You who would become a True Oracle must face a trial. Defeat me, and prove your quality before the goddess.
{np}O, Vaasa, Goddess of Earth, admit me unto your sacred sanctum!
{np}I am servant to Vaasa, Goddess of Earth.{pp}You who would become a True Oracle must face a trial. Defeat me, and prove your quality before the goddess.
{np}O, Great Greuza, Goddess of Water, admit me unto your sacred sanctum!
{np}I am servant to Greuza, Goddess of Water.{pp}You who would become a True Oracle must face a trial. Defeat me, and prove your quality before the goddess.
{np}O, Great Lyuneram, Goddess of Ice, admit me unto your sacred sanctum!
{np}I am servant to Lyuneram, Goddess of Ice.{pp}You who would become a True Oracle must face a trial. Defeat me, and prove your quality before the goddess.
{np}O, Great Nestharot, Goddess of Lightning, admit me unto your sacred sanctum!
{np}I am servant to Nestharot, Goddess of Lightning.{pp}You who would become a True Oracle must face a trial. Defeat me, and prove your quality before the goddess.
{np}Becalm yourself, Ozma.{pp}I know you're upset, but you cannot allow your feelings to rule you.
{np}I hunt a traitor who has committed unconscionable crimes against his country. What could be more rational?

{np}You do not do this for your country. This is for you and you alone.{pp}With the war faltering, we cannot permit you to wreak havoc as you please.{pp}The situation demands unity. Now more than ever, we must stand as one.{pp}Balxephon realized this, else why admit to his mistake?
{np}You would have us follow our orders without question in the name of {pal 16}unity{palreset}?

{np}It is our duty.
There cannot be order without trust.
{np}Balxephon lost my trust when he deceived me.
{np}What he did, he did for your sake. It was not easy for him.

{np}And I'm to accept this?
I'm to {pal 16}trust{palreset} him?

{np}Listen to reason, Ozma.
I have no wish to lead you back in chains.

{np}Sir Volaq!
The Resistance!
{np}Here?

{np}Ozma!
What are you doing!?

{np}What I must.
I will see whether Hobyrim lives for myself!
{np}I am Ozma of the Knights Loslorien, and I have a question for you.{pp}A blind swordsman fought us at Rhime. Is he with you now?
{np}The man you seek is not among us.{pp}What do the Dark Knights want with him?
{np}It's no concern of yours.{pp}And you're of no more use to me!
{np}I know you can hear me, swordsman!{pp}Are you Hobyrim Von Rahms or no?

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} No, I am not.
2. Yes...I am Hobyrim.
{np}No, my lady. You may shout as loud as you wish, my answer will not change.
{np}So be it.{pp}You have forgotten me...forgotten your homeland.{pp}I will slay you as I would any other Resistance scum!

{np}Yes, Ozma.
It is I.

{np}You're alive.{pp}Balxephon lied to me...
They all lied! Even Oz.{pp}...Why?
{np}They sought to make truth of the lie.
{np}Ozma, listen to me!{pp}We have our orders. What matter the whys and wherefores?{pp}This man is our enemy. It is our oath-bound duty to strike at him!

{np}I don't believe it...
Balxephon killed Stratarchis Vogras!?{pp}When they said you'd murdered your father, I felt something was amiss, but this... I never imagined.{pp}He must have known what it would mean for us―for Lodis.

{np}Loslorien care nothing for means so long as their ends are met. You of all people must know this!{pp}As they shaped Lodis then, they shape Valeria now.{pp}They will rule by brute force and fear, and purge any who dare to speak against them.{pp}But the people of these islands have risen to overthrow their corrupt rulers.{pp}How long before Lodis meets the same fate?
{np}I am a knight of Lodis. I will not betray our homeland!

{np}You name me a traitor, but I have ever been a son of Lodis.{pp}Lanselot and Balxephon are the true betrayers!{pp}It is they who used the High Priest to deceive the people.{pp}It is they who use {pal 16}you{palreset}, Ozma!
{np}{pal 16}He{palreset} is the enemy, Ozma. Don't believe a word of this nonsense!
{np}You wear too many wounds, Ozma. Keep a steady eye on your foe!{pp}This battle is unworthy of your death!
{np}Save your worry, Volaq. I will not die until I've learned the truth!
{np}Do not let vengeance overcome you.{pp}I have already lost Oz. I will not lose you, too.
{np}I am a Loslorien knight commander. Vengeance does {pal 16}my{palreset} bidding!
{np}So, this is Hobyrim. You're really something, you know. Most men would have surrendered their sword along with their sight.

{np}A knight commander, is it?
You have the air of rank about you.

{np}Does nothing escape you? I shall have to take blind swordsmen much more seriously.{pp}To watch you move, it is clear you are no common warrior.{pp}Let our steel sing, then. Your crimes against Lodis demand blood!

{np}Strike me if you can.
I flee from no one.

{np}This is no place to die.
Ozma, we must withdraw!
{np}Hobyrim is dead, and the truth with him.{pp}Back to Heim.
{np}Hobyrim is dead, and the truth with him.{pp}The battle is over. Let's back to Heim.

{np}I yield.
I will fight you no more.

{np}Hobyrim, I must know the truth.
All of it.
{np}Very well.
{np}I will not leave until I have the truth! Away from me, Volaq!
{np}The truth's no good to you dead. Take care, Ozma!
{np}I'll never know...
{np}Ozma, no!
{np}I return empty-handed to the high champion. He will not be pleased...

{np}I'll never know...{pp}Oz...
I rejoin you...at last.
{np}Hobyrim, what past do you share with the Dark Knights?
{np}I was once one of them.
{np}―is my brother.{pp}And Ozma was to be my bride.
{np}Hear me out. I have long since turned my back on Loslorien.{pp}I ventured to these islands with but one purpose: to kill my brother.
{np}And it was Balxephon who made word of this "mischance" known...

{np}And I will have it.{pp}I came to Valeria seeking vengeance, but that is not the only reason I remain.{pp}Yours is a worthy cause, {hero}.
I would join you.

{np}Ozma, I have always loved Lodis.{pp}But the country I knew is gone. High Priest Sardian has twisted it beyond recognition.{pp}I could not save Lodis, but it's not too late for Valeria!{pp}If I can aid them in their revolution, I will do it gladly.
{np}You are a man of honor, Hobyrim.{pp}I should be glad to have you at my side.
{np}What now, Ozma?{pp}Knowing the truth, will you return to Loslorien?
{np}Nothing would please me more than to join you, Hobyrim.{pp}But the Resistance killed my brother, a debt I have yet to repay.

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} As I owe you for my father.
2. I cannot force you to forgive me.

{np}My father would still be alive if not for you.{pp}But he told me to be a stone along the path to our salvation. Begrudging you his death serves nothing.{pp}If it will move Valeria toward peace, then you are welcome among us.{pp}What's done is done.
{np}You would forgive me?
{np}It would be easier to cut you down were you not so obliging.
{np}Let me be your eyes, Hobyrim.{pp}Though it may be you who shows me the way.
{np}Thank you, Ozma. It cheers me to hear you say so.

{np}I'll not beg your forgiveness. It means nothing if not given willingly.{pp}Nor have I forgotten what you did to my father. And there are others who must grudge you as well.{pp}You surrendered to us, so I will not harm you. But when we've finished here, you must leave.
{np}Know I would do whatever I can for you, Hobyrim. But I will not ally myself with the Resistance.
{np}Then you will return to Lanselot.
{np}And devote myself to his cause.{pp}I must trust that the high champion knows what's best for Lodis.
{np}I'll not try to dissuade you.
{np}Be well, Hobyrim.
{np}Speak the truth!{pp}The blind swordsman we encountered at Rhime {pal 16}was{palreset} Hobyrim.{pp}I have it from one of our own whisperers in the Resistance!
{np}You've been busy, then.
{np}You gave the order, Balxephon. I merely received the report.{pp}Had I not chanced to do so, I very much doubt I would ever have learned of it.

{np}Why go on denying it?{pp}Hobyrim lives.
You lied to me!

{np}Ozma's right, Balxephon.
Confess and be done with it.{pp}There should be no secrets among friends.

{np}You have the right of it, Ozma.
Hobyrim lives.

{np}Why, Balxephon?
How could you lie to me?

{np}A grave crime, yes. But I could not bear to see my brother, my own blood, imprisoned and put to death.{pp}Nor could I merely set him free. As adjutant, I bore certain...responsibilities.{pp}I took his eyes to mark him for his crime, made it appear as though he died in the dungeons, and banished him.
{np}The pieces do not fit.{pp}When we were at Phidoch, I suspected nothing. Why lie to me then?

{np}It was for your own good.{pp}Hobyrim was to be your husband. Ordering the man put to his death seemed too cruel by far.{pp}I love you, Ozma.{pp}Hobyrim had brought you enough suffering. I did not wish to see it continue.
{np}Lies upon lies!
{np}As soon preach to a statue once a woman's made up her mind, eh?
{np}You disobeyed orders to save your own brother, as I recall.{pp}Had you kept that from us, I don't expect we would have seen such a commotion.
{np}That's women for you.{pp}Always poking their noses where they don't belong, and turning them up when they mislike what they smell.
{np}Do not mock me!

{np}Calm, Ozma.
Do not take Martym's jibes to heart.
{np}I promise to keep nothing more from you. Forgive me.
{np}The traitor who murdered the stratarchis, his own father, lives in hiding on these isles.{pp}Bringing him to justice is our sacred duty. If you will not see it done, {pal 16}I{palreset} will!

{np}Ozma, wait!
Have you forgotten our purpose here?
{np}A brother who is a traitor, a pig-headed bride. A fine house you keep!{pp}At this rate, we'll be on these bloody isles forever.
{np}See her safely to Lodis, and you'll be well rewarded.
{np}Don't suppose you'd reconsider, m'lord?{pp}Puttin' to sea now, well, it's suicide. The open seas are rife with pirates.{pp}Can't hardly spend no coin if we're dead now, can we?
{np}Which do you fear more? Pirates who may or may not exist...or me?

{np}O-Only a jest, m'lord.
We're only too happy to ferry the lady home.
{np}I'll rejoin you in Lodis as soon as our task here is done. I shall sail with the first ship.

{np}You've some spittle on your cheek...
There, that's better.
{np}Ever the beauty, you.{pp}We'll be married upon my return, as promised.{pp}I will always love you, Ozma. Never doubt it.
{np}Who... Who could have done this!?
{np}Sleep, souls. Embrace the waiting Ever-World!
{np}No...{pp}This does not go well. I cannot deliver them all to rest.
{np}You there! Are you all right!?
{np}The Order of {order}!
{np}Flee while you can!
{np}May the protection of the Father be with you!
{np}No! Blast, if we'd only arrived sooner.
{np}Unh...
{np}She still lives. Quick, aid her!
{np}Too late...
{np}I am...revived. Thank you, good sir. I would...aid you in return.
{np}You need to mend yourself first.{pp}That will be best done elsewhere. Go, quickly!
{np}May the protection of the Father be with you.
{np}Unusual for zombies to attack en masse like this.
{np}Unusual for zombies to attack en masse like this.{pp}Perhaps the woman we saved knows something. We can ask her while we tend to her wounds.
{np}She's in trouble!
{np}Quickly, aid her!
{np}I came here with...my companions, to treat and heal those caught up in this war...{pp}The attack came without warning.
{np}The zombies... They moved like a troop of living men. It was an organized attack.
{np}You believe this was not a chance event but a willful act? Someone sent those zombies on the town?
{np}I fear so. But who would put the dead to...to such... *cough*
{np}Steady!
{np}I fear that...the respite from death you have given me is but temporary...
{np}The zombies move to attack Almorica. Please, you must protect the people there...{pp}Give the dead their deserved rest.
{np}I promise we'll do all we can.
{np}Thank...you.{pp}I go to my maker...in peace.
{np}Our enemy...approaches! Now we will take...what they took from us!
{np}Their leader is as much of a corpse as they.{pp}The dead leading the dead? Something foul is afoot.
{np}To die...again. To be killed...again.{pp}Hatred dark within me...a curse become... Ruin to the Walisters in Almorica!
{np}Looks like she was telling the truth about the dead meaning ill for Almorica.{pp}We must return at once.

{np}How many times must I say this? My goal is nothing short of a perfect restoration of soul and flesh!{pp}Achieve this, and the people of Valeria―nay, of the world entire―will be free from the fetters of mortality!

{np}But if we restore the soul, the body withers. Revive the body, and the soul is lost.{pp}Both lead only to an imperfect death...never to what you desire!{pp}You know this, and yet you continue your foul inquiries. You're taking lives for your playthings!

{np}No more impassioned an argument could I make for the vitality of my research than what you've just said!{pp}My dear Cressida, the knowledge is out there. I {pal 16}know{palreset} it is. All we need do is find it!
{np}If it's knowledge you seek, why unleash your creations on innocents?{pp}Even if they are Walister...this is massacre!
{np}You mistake the manner for the mind. My animates do not blindly follow my will. Their souls {pal 16}want{palreset} this bloodshed.
{np}Souls? Naught but hatred resides in those shells of flesh.{pp}Only the vestiges of the terror they felt at their own deaths remain to drive them. Surely you know this!
{np}You call them vestiges, but these remnants of the former self are the foundation upon which complete soul recovery can be achieved!
{np}Hektor...Sister...Mother!
{np}How could you do this to them... Don't you love them? Don't you love anything!?
{np}I do love them, which is why I keep them close.{pp}Look, Moldova and Hektor remain partners for eternity!{pp}Their love will persist until their bodies decay and dust returns to dust, ash to ash.
{np}You are mad...{pp}Wholly mad!
{np}I fear words will never be enough to convince you.
{np}As arbiter of life and death, I hereby bind you to this place!
{np}My legs... I'm stuck!
{np}Love...never dies.
{np}Sister! Moldova, please!
{np}Necromancer Nybeth! I feared you were behind this.{pp}Who else would send the dead against Almorica?

{np}Ah, if it isn't my old acquaintance...{hero}, was it?{pp}I see you still fail to grasp the significance of my research. A pity.{pp}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you!
Darkness to me!
{np}You were behind them, weren't you? Who else would send the dead against Almorica?

{np}And you must be from the Resistance. A pleasure to make your acquaintance.{pp}Though it seems you fail to grasp the significance of my research.{pp}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you!
Darkness to me!
{np}I'm afraid you mistake me.{pp}I did not direct anyone, living or dead, to attack Almorica Castle.{pp}They wished it for themselves. Particularly...that one.
{np}Unh... Uuuh.
{np}Vyce!?
{np}You...said you'd...help...{pp}Abandoned... You abandoned...me...
{np}No! That was not the way of it!
{np}Why would the Resistance come to my aid?
{np}We couldn't leave you to that fate, whoever you may be.{pp}Now, go while there's still time.
{np}I can't leave! I have to see this finished!
{np}Catiua... Look at...me. I...
{np}No, Vyce. No! You're dead!{pp}You should not be here in this place, in this world. Please, rest!
{np}M-My head...why am I...not me?{pp}This...is {pal 16}your{palreset} doing! You...must pay...
{np}Vyce...I would help you if I could. Believe me!
{np}Pain...my head... H-Help me... {hero}!
{np}Vyce! No!!!
{np}What? Where am I? My...work was complete.
{np}Hektor! Oh, dear Hektor... So noble a man should not be reduced to this.
{np}Why are you sad, Cressida? Do not...grieve for...me.{pp}Go...Cressida. Live. For me...and Moldova.

{np}What...place is this?
Hektor? Where are you?

{np}Cressida... Beloved daughter...
You...must live.

{np}Mother! Sister!
How horrible...how horrible!

{np}Moldova!
May you finally find peace...

{np}Why did this have to be? Why!?
Mother! I'm so sorry...

{np}Mother...Sister...I could have saved you.
I should have...
{np}Well now, this will not do. No, not at all. I've far more important matters to which I must attend.{pp}Enough of these petty squabbles. I'm sure we'll meet again.
{np}You'd leave your dead behind, Nybeth?

{np}Vyce...I...
What else could I have done?
{np}I will never forgive you for this, Nybeth... I will revenge my friends upon you!
{np}Quickly, bind her wounds. She may know something of Nybeth.
{np}Cressida was your name?{pp}The necromancer Nybeth is no stranger to you, is he?
{np}No, he's no stranger. He is my father. And I am his disciple.
{np}You practice necromancy!?
{np}You mean to say that I defile the bodies and souls of the departed.

{np}Until today, I might have said no, what I do is for the benefit of my people...thus I truly believed.{pp}I was wrong.{pp}Where I thought we ushered in happiness, I find only horror...and despair.{pp}My father insists it is because his research is incomplete, but how can any good come from such evil?{pp}He is merely inflicting more pain on those who deserve peace.
{np}Can there be no rest for those he has raised?

{np}Even should they kill every man who ever wronged them, those who return with hatred in place of their soul will never know peace.{pp}There is no past for them, no future. They live forever in the moment of their own death.{pp}I may not believe in the dream of divine salvation...but this is a nightmare.
{np}I am guilty for tying them to this twisted mockery of a life... I have no words to express my remorse.

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} Nor should you expect forgiveness.
2. You will not be judged by me.
{np}Your sins against these people are too deep to be easily forgotten.{pp}But as you have realized your error and seek to make amends, I will spare your life.
{np}Why would I seek forgiveness from you, the murderer of my mother and sister?{pp}If you had not saved my life, I would surely have taken yours.
{np}Then we will leave before you forget your charity.
{np}You do not deserve to be judged here, in this place.{pp}Instead, I would judge Nybeth, who shows none of your repentance.{pp}If you would stop him, perhaps you can help us.
{np}Why would I help you, the murderer of my mother and sister?
{np}I thank you for your aid.{pp}But this matter is between myself and my father. I must resolve it alone.
{np}I see. Then we shall depart. Thank you for shedding some light on this dark matter.
{np}You...murdered my mother and sister.{pp}But no, I will put that aside until my father―until Nybeth is slain. I will help you.{pp}It is he who defiled their memories, and he who should pay!
{np}I will aid you for the sake of those who were given an unlife they did not want.
{np}Thank you, Cressida. Let us put bad blood aside to stop good blood from being shed.
{np}{FF 9A 03}You received a Necroprentice's Mark.

{np}Well, this was unexpected.{pp}The draconic power that rests within this place is not for the hands of the Resistance to hold.{pp}We thought to claim it first, but better to kill you now and be done with it.{pp}What need have we of the Dark Knights? Find your peace in this temple of death, boy!
{np}You'll...never make it to the palace...depths.
{np}I mislike the feel of this place.
{np}Lovely. Only holy magic works on this lot!
{np}...Caught between scales and a dead man.
{np}To his aid!
{np}A fatal...miscalculation!

{np}Thank you, good sirs.{pp}I believe I've hit something of a wall in my search for draconic magic.{pp}Perhaps you might be able to help me a bit?{pp}I'd be happy to make it worth your while. You're with the Resistance, yes?{pp}Escort me into the depths, and I'll help your cause. Fair?

{np}{select 1}{FF 88 02}1{FF 88 02}.{FF 88 01} You have a deal.
2. I must refuse.
{np}Then you are welcome to join us, Rudlum.
{np}A far warmer reception than I'll have from aught else in this foul place.
{np}I'm sorry, but I must refuse.
{np}A shame, that. The going only gets rougher farther down. Take care.
{np}I've had more than enough of these dreary halls already.
{np}Then why are you here?
{np}I might ask the same of you!
{np}...You came here alone?
{np}Not alone...but the others are gone. Turned to cold stone.
{np}Where are they now?
{np}Right beside you.
{np}This was a man?
{np}Yes. Turned to stone as he lived.{pp}The guardian of this temple cursed him.{pp}All the statues here were once living flesh.
{np}...Why stone?
{np}This temple is holy ground... Only the disciples of Ashmedai are permitted within.
{np}Then...who are you?

{np}I am Xadoba...
And you are good as dead.
{np}You're the guardian!
{np}Fool mortal! You will grow cold and stand watch here through the ages!
{np}It is better...this way. Those who seek power are right to tread the dark paths.{pp}Walk on, over my corpse...into the darkness.

{np}Ah! I remember you!
Hmm...{pp}{hero}, was it? A pleasure, to be sure!{pp}So you've come seeking draconic magic as so many heroes of old before you, yes?{pp}Fitting, fitting. All those who wish for victory in battle must ever seek a greater power!{pp}It is necessary, a prerequisite to becoming a leader among men. And quite a leader you've become. Hee!{pp}I will take our meeting here as a sign! Perhaps you'd like to see the fruits of my research?{pp}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you to serve! Darkness to me!
{np}You gave me a bad turn at Ndamsa, but you'll fare far worse this time round! Hee!
{np}Nybeth! Your twisted ambitions die here!
{np}Oelias? Is that you? I did not think to meet {pal 16}you{palreset} here.{pp}It pains me that you still do not grasp the true meaning of your father's research.
{np}My father was not the monster I see before me!{pp}I will cast your soul so deep in the darkness even the gods will not be able to find you!
{np}You've drawn even further away than I imagined.{pp}Is that what you threaten to all those you kill in the name of your revolution?{pp}Does the blood not drip from our hands in equal measure?
{np}That may be, but we do not rejoice in the taking of lives...nor do we play with mortality!
{np}You think I do this, my greatest work, for mere amusement?
{np}You claim otherwise?{pp}What possible reason could you have to rob the lives of innocents, to patch flesh upon flesh, to bind souls to decaying shells?

{np}You ask my reasons?
I do it for the family I love.
{np}For your family!? You engage in these horrors for us!?{pp}When you dragged Dievold back into this world, you left his life behind.

{np}Yes, Dievold was unfortunate.
But it does not change the fact that I did this for you!
{np}I fail to understand.
{np}Then...Dievold told you nothing?{pp}Hrm...that won't do.
{np}Tell me what you meant, Nybeth. How could this be for me!?
{np}Since you ask, I will tell you.{pp}My dear Oelias. You are nothing other than my most precious partner...my wife.
{np}I know you to be mad, but this is beyond the pale!{pp}Me, your wife!? Impossible!

{np}But it is no lie!
You are dead once already.{pp}It was before this warring began...a sudden death.{pp}In Dievold's case, I was mercifully able to save his head, but of you nothing more was left than ribbons of flesh.{pp}It was all I could do to stop the swift flight of your soul and bind it to this body.
{np}This...body? My body!?
{np}Is this true, Dievold? Is it true what he says? I must know!
{np}...You know it yourself, Oelias.{pp}Though he may conceal the truth at times, Nybeth is not the sort to spin such tales.{pp}I am sorry. I could not bring myself to tell you.
{np}But no...I have memories. I am Oelias!{pp}I remember playing with my brother...my mother's many kindnesses...{pp}Those memories are not lies...are they!?

{np}I do not blame Dievold for his inability to disabuse you of your misconceptions.{pp}But the body you inhabit is the body of our daughter Amala!{pp}Amala...survived the tragedy, but her grasp on life was fragile.{pp}I thought...no, before thought, I decided which soul to save!
{np}You chose me...

{np}Yes! Because I love you!
Oelias, as your life now is proof, I love you with all my heart!
{np}I...don't believe it.
{np}You know I tell the truth!{pp}Yes...though at times I might let truth linger in obscurity, I do not lie! Hee!
{np}When I transferred your soul to Amala's body, for reasons I cannot fathom your memories were lost.{pp}In exchange, you absorbed Amala's memories into yourself...in effect, becoming Amala!
{np}Wait. If what you're saying is true, how do you know I'm not really Amala?{pp}You thought you were saving your wife, when in fact you saved me!{pp}Have you any proof that my soul is Oelias's?

{np}Fascinating! If one accepts the hypothesis that the self is a formation of memory―then perhaps you are {pal 16}not{palreset} Oelias after all!{pp}But...ask your soul who you are, and consider the answer you receive.{pp}The soul does not lie!{pp}Yes. Though we tell tales with silvered tongue, we cannot deceive ourselves for long.{pp}One may play the saint, but it is our {pal 16}actions{palreset} which divide good from evil.{pp}We profess our love for another, but is this not merely making excuse for our own irrational behavior?{pp}How can anyone else understand who we are, if they don't even accept our right to exist!?{pp}Yes, only your soul knows you. Face your soul! Embrace it! It's all you have!
{np}I don't know what you're talking about... I don't understand!
{np}Don't let him fluster you, Oelias. Believe in your own strength.
{np}Oh, that won't work, {hero}. She has already seen the truth I speak!{pp}She has communed with her soul and found the answer there, whether she chooses to accept it or not.
{np}Nybeth...Father!{pp}Even if you believe your research is for the good of man, it is anathema, and history will judge you so.

{np}An easy thing to censure me, my son. But can you look upon yourselves and say you are without guilt?{pp}Why have you not thrown down your swords? What you call righteousness is no more than a base struggle for survival.{pp}You close your eyes to the piles of corpses {pal 16}you{palreset} have made, choosing to see only your shining ideals.{pp}Am I any different...perhaps!{pp}For my efforts will bring about true change! You speak of history, but I look to the future!{pp}Yes, many souls may have suffered from my inquiries, but it is a small price to pay.{pp}My sins are for my family, and I will not bow to a senseless oppressor too blind to see the value of my work!

{np}Father, I have no ear for your words or your reasonings. What wisdom can be had from talking to a madman?{pp}I have realized one truth, however. You must be stopped before you can do to another what you have done to me!

{np}You have your father's gift for words, my son! In truth you move my heart!{pp}How unfortunate I cannot restore your body to what it once was...but perhaps that is as it should be, yes?{pp}No more fitting finale to this farce than combat between father and son! Hee! May it entertain you in the afterlife!

{np}You truly believe what you say, Nybeth, don't you. That saddens me.{pp}So many words, grand schemes you build in your mind, when all you build with your hands is corruption.{pp}You would create life, but all you have created is the appearance of life.{pp}You profess love for your family, and yet you have lost them so completely they would rather see you dead.{pp}If your name lingers in history at all, it will be to say that here you faced the Resistance, and here you died.
{np}The young warrior spins a fine tale. But is it truth or fancy?

{np}I can't imagine that it matters whether we defeat you here or not.{pp}It's almost not worth the effort to fight someone so...trivial.{pp}Even to consider its worth is a waste of time, seeing as how you'll likely flee again.
{np}Perhaps you are right. Perhaps these truths I espouse are, in fact, falsehoods―unbeknownst to me, mind you.{pp}But what if I {pal 16}am{palreset} right? Wouldn't you like to know?

{np}Not particularly, no. Words always pale before action, much as dreams fade before achievement.{pp}You have lost your love of family, your thirst for true knowledge, your loyalty to your homeland, and your charity toward your people.{pp}No matter what words we speak here today, you are and will remain a sad, old man who has lost all.
{np}An...unfortunate turn. Though I am not...unprepared.{pp}Demunza, Lord of the Abyss, grant me the destructive fist and merciful heart bound within this ring!{pp}Break your seal!

{np}Ah yes, a much more {pal 16}fitting{palreset} form for one so intimate with death. Hee!{pp}Pure undeath is achievable, you see, provided you use the right tools...{pp}...And you're not too attached to your own humanity!{pp}Something to discuss further next we meet.

{np}I knew you'd flee, Nybeth. And good riddance!{pp}But when you think back on the ideals, the companions, the family you've left behind...{pp}Know that I will have all these things. And you will not.
{np}Hmm... The primordial structures within their bodies fail.{pp}The transformation was...incomplete.
{np}Living Corpse makes undead out of the dead...{pp}While Resurrect merely puts off the true death for a time. Neither is the solution I seek.

{np}I was lucky, perhaps, in the case of the Galgastani knight. Binding soul to flesh is no mean feat!{pp}But true primordial regeneration...that approaches the divine.{pp}I achieve one half of the solution, only to watch the other fall to pieces. As futile as forging swords of glass!
{np}My apologies to you both. You were...failures.{pp}But a necessary sacrifice in the timeless pursuit of eternal, undying youth!
{np}Perhaps I will have to enlist help from another quarter―
{np}Oh? What do we have here?
{np}S-Sir Leonar?
{np}You did me a bad turn at Qadriga―I've been meaning to thank you for that.
{np}I admit I was not expecting company.{pp}{hero} of the Resistance...am I right?{pp}Nice to finally meet you in the flesh, as it were.
{np}I know you. You're Nybeth Obdilord―the corpse-mage from Galgastan.{pp}What have you done to Sir Leonar!?
{np}He and his companion were necessary "materials," shall we say, for my research into immortality. A noble cause, you must agree.
{np}Noble? You profane god's creation and commit sacrilege upon the dead!{pp}Release them, now!

{np}How can I release something that does not exist?{pp}These "men" you see before you are naught more than piles of dirt―or soon would have been, had I left them to decay.{pp}No souls, just animated corpses...{pp}Are you even listening to me? Perhaps this will seize your attention:{pp}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you! Darkness to me!
{np}Now, witness the fruits of my research!

{np}Sir Leonar!
It is I, {hero}!

{np}It's no use, you know. He remembers not one whit of his former life.{pp}How could he, when his soul is gone?{pp}Tell me, do you know why the undead always seem so bent on violence?{pp}It is because death is {pal 16}agony{palreset}...and they despise the living for not suffering as they do.{pp}To the undead mind―such as it is―the only way to ease their pain is to inflict the same upon you!
{np}So Sir Leonar is gone...{pp}Repent swiftly, necromancer, for you join him soon!

{np}What is this place?
What has befallen me?
{np}Sir Leonar!

{np}{hero}...?{pp}Wait...
I remember...death.

{np}What in the hells!?
This body...what demon sorcery is this!?
{np}Xaebos?

{np}Master Nybeth!
What has happened to me? Why am I...
{np}Some of my subjects are...sturdier than others. Hee!
{np}Commander Ronsenbach... You are defiled by my father's sorcery.{pp}Forgive us, Commander. I will not allow this sacrilege to continue!
{np}Sacrilege? My dear child!{pp}Necromancy is a noble art! It is nothing less than the path to salvation of the body and soul.{pp}...The power to overcome death!

{np}Was it salvation you offered my mother and sister in Golyat?{pp}No...you knew it would not be complete.{pp}From the very beginning you knew they would be left in that horrible place betwixt life and death!

{np}I disagree. In this matter, my heart sees {pal 16}truly{palreset} as it has never seen before!{pp}I love Cassandra and Moldova. How could I not try to free them from death's bonds?{pp}No, I must strive to resurrect them, and toward this end, I use my art without hesitation.

{np}So you cling to such dreams, ever lacking the courage to face the truth of your failure.{pp}You talk of freeing your family, but if anyone is captive to death, it is you.{pp}Let me free you from this life, Father, that you may trouble the dead no more!
{np}Nybeth!

{np}Impressive! To come all this way...{pp}I half suspect you are led by the same Dark that shadows my path!{pp}Did you know that I have discovered the purpose for which this temple was constructed?{pp}It was built for people like you! Ah...but I see you are not concerned with such matters.{pp}If you insist on playing the hero come to vanquish me, I shall be happy to act my part.{pp}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you! Darkness to me!
{np}This conflict was foreordained, you know. All is laid out upon the Wheel of Fate, free from the meddling hands of mortals.

{np}Ah...yesss...
So {pal 16}this{palreset} is the Dark!{pp}I am becoming one with you now...
It is... It is ecstasy!{pp}Yes! The Dark has chosen me! The bodies of the unwitting will be my vessels! I am immortal...
{np}Those zombies have that woman surrounded! Wait...what is she doing down here?
{np}There now, go ahead.
{np}Go on, try them!
{np}Thus they are called the "Books of the Dead." I see!{pp}Quite impressive for a mortal accomplishment, even if the books require the temple's raw power to work their magic.
{np}You, down there! ...What are you?
{np}Georges, I leave this to you.
{np}As you wish, madam.
{np}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you! Darkness, be my hand!
{np}Let us see what these mortals have to offer us by way of entertainment.
{np}Bodies are fleshy, weak things... A nuisance. And yet, without, one cannot taste the living air...
{np}There. This is more like it...
{np}The woman from before!
{np}How unusual to see mortals here.{pp}Ah...you are {hero} of Golyat, commander of the forces at Almorica!{pp}That explains how you were able to defeat Georges.
{np}A perfect opportunity to use the dragon lords' Rings of the Dead.{pp}They will resonate with the power of the temple.
{np}That's the same artifact Nybeth used!

{np}The dragon lords were well versed in the Dark. They even fashioned trinkets allowing the most ignorant to wield powerful magic.{pp}Not that any mere surface dweller could comprehend, let alone employ, it.
{np}Denizens of the abyss! From ink of blackest night, I summon you! Darkness to me!
{np}Now, {hero} of Golyat, let us see if you live up to your reputation!
{np}I bow to you, surface dweller. You fight well.{pp}If you plan on venturing further, however, know that ambition and curiosity are not your allies.

{np}Ah, wonderful.
I was hoping we'd meet again.{pp}You and that necromancer have even more insatiable appetites for knowledge than I.

{np}Perhaps you are driven by some unquenchable desire? An ambition that fears not even death.{pp}Do not mistake me. Ambition is vital. Those without cannot prevail in the inevitable contest for survival.{pp}Espouse whatever lofty ideals you wish...we all exist in this world to satisfy our baser desires.{pp}{FF 92}Aaah, I feel it. That dark desire, deep within your heart!{pp}You are a fitting supplicant to this temple. You are closer to the Dark than any I know!

{np}I...tire of this body. Mayhaps I'll take yours.{pp}Don't worry. I'll put your companions' bodies to good use, too.{pp}There are many, many souls in need of bodies. Flesh and blood to anchor them to this world.{pp}You remember Georges? How he pesters me to find him a suitable vessel.{pp}Yes, let us dance your final dance. The time is nigh!

{np}Your kind, too, is but another branch upon the Dark lineage. You're not so different from we demons of the Dark.{pp}No, your souls are born from ours...and as long as this is true, you will never claim the Light!

{np}Ah...weak. Too weak, this corporeal form. But remember.{pp}As long as this palace to the Dark remains, those who dwell upon the surface will venture here to satisfy their desire for power.{pp}And when they come, I will take their bodies as my own, and once again feel warm blood coursing through my veins!{pp}We will meet again.

{np}Master Vepahl!
The army of the false king approaches!
{np}Then we are not alone in our quest for the Great Father's miracle.{pp}Let us not delay further!
{np}Believe in me, my disciples. Believe, and the power of Philaha will work a miracle upon you!
{np}We believe, Master Vepahl.
{np}A miracle! Now, dedicate your new lives as you did your old: for the Tigers of Burnham!
{np}What are those? ...Angels?
{np}March forth, champions of heaven! Wipe all traces of the false king's army from the land!
{np}Is not even the divine power enough to defeat you, Butcher of Golyat!?{pp}...Though it pain me to leave this unsettled, I have duties elsewhere to which I must attend.
{np}Children of god, who march upon the field, bereft of blood and flesh!{pp}By the power of the Great Father Philaha, grant your form once again unto the proud Tigers of Burnham!

{np}These hands, this voice...
Is this {pal 16}my{palreset} body?

{np}Truly a miracle!
God is wise! God is glorious!
{np}Ah, warmth! This...this is what it was to live!
{np}I cannot believe it has happened, though I feel it with every part of my being!{pp}Great Father Philaha! Praise be to you!
{np}You see? With this relic, and the power of {pal 16}his{palreset} miracle, a body once lost can be reclaimed!{pp}As I predicted, this is the promised land! This is god's great revelation!
{np}True resurrection of the dead... Is it possible?
{np}A pity the false king's army had to blemish this miracle by witnessing it.{pp}Attack! End their lives! This miracle belongs not to them, but to the Tigers of Burnham!
{np}This...upon the very day I perceived the mystery of the miracle. Fate is cruel, and you are crueler still, Butcher of Golyat!

{np}Great Father Philaha!
How!? How can you do this to me, your most humble servant?

{np}Lowly beasts that crawl upon the earth, hear my words.{pp}Seek not god's miracle.{pp}These forms you claim by ancient artifice are not life. They are shadow.{pp}Take not god's name for your own.{pp}Whatsoever you may call this miracle, it is but the smallest piece of god.{pp}Test not god's charity.{pp}No matter what tales you tell your soul, you will never understand the mind of god.

{np}Don't be deceived...Butcher of Golyat...{pp}The demon pretends...to be divine...
Don't be de...ceived...
{np}Repent, mortals, for your souls are forfeit to heaven!
{np}Angel or no, those are fighting words!
{np}I did not think to encounter the Resistance in these marches. Ill luck that we must face them alone.{pp}The greater the glory when we present their heads on pikes to Falfaday!

{np}The Butcher of Golyat...
Thought I recognized you.{pp}The Resistance must be desperate to send {hero} himself out relic hunting.
{np}What relics are these?

{np}Do not play coy.
I cannot think you've come all this way simply to see the sights.{pp}Not enough that you have claimed Galgastan for your own. Now you seek to usurp the wisdom of the past besides.{pp}Your appetites are grand, Butcher!

{np}These relics she mentioned―remnants from the age of the dragon lords.{pp}Their knowledge was vast. It was they who discovered how to wield the magic we now find so commonplace.{pp}These soldiers are here seeking the ancient grimoires and magicked swords rumored to have been left after their passing.
{np}Ancient grimoires and magicked swords...
{np}Sherri Phoraena? Is that you? I had heard the Resistance slew you in Banhamuba.{pp}The truth is far worse. You are turned traitor against the Bakram!

{np}Hello, Jilessa.
If you've any sense, you'll withdraw now.{pp}The Bakram cannot hope to win with the Dark Knights as their allies.
{np}You led the search for these relics because you said we could not rely on Lodis forever.{pp}Now that we've come to find them, you tell us to withdraw?{pp}I will not heed the words of a traitor!

{np}I am no traitor. But I want nothing more to do with Brantyn and his failed regency.{pp}Valeria will never know peace while he sits the Bakram throne.{pp}He has no intention of ridding us of the Dark Knights. He is grown far too comfortable.
{np}It may be you're right. But I cannot throw away my homeland as easily as some!{pp}I am a proud Bakram, and will always be so!
{np}Is that pride worth your life?{pp}When you lie dead in an unmarked grave, none will mourn you!

{np}Dame Ozma, is that you?
I can scarce believe my eyes.{pp}Then the rumors are true...
Lodis sides with the Resistance!
{np}I {pal 16}am{palreset} Ozma Glacius, of the Dark Knights Loslorien―no, a knight of Lodis.{pp}But these rumors you speak of, sibyl, are just that: rumors. Not lightly do we forsake our vows.
{np}Then why do you stand among the enemy, poised to strike at us?
{np}It would not do to explain here. Suffice to say, I have my reasons.{pp}My quarrel is not with the Bakram. It is the Dark Knights are my enemy!
{np}As I thought, a common traitor!

{np}I suppose I shall have to grow accustomed to people calling me that.{pp}No matter. It is putting Lodis to rights that concerns me, naught else.{pp}This battle is but one step along the path I must walk.
{np}A convenient tale to tell yourself. Do you find it convinces many?
{np}I do not seek to convince―neither you nor anyone else!{pp}The reasons for my struggle are my own.
{np}Then may your corpse grow cold alongside these Resistance pigspawn!
{np}Falfaday... Reymos...
{np}What now..."my lord"?
{np}We have lost some few soldiers, but I will proceed to Lhazan Fortress as planned.{pp}You will remain here and refortify our position. Make no move until Falfaday and I return.
{np}Refortify with what? The girl and her dragon whelps did for most of my men.
{np}I've arranged for reinforcements. They've met with some unexpected delay, that's all.
