{np}You who would draw swords against the Dark Knights!{pp}You are yet a child.{pp}Throw down your weapon, and you may yet live.
{np}How can you say that, after all the people―all the children―you've just slain!?{pp}If this is guilt, it comes far too late.
{np}Too late? Am I...too late?{pp}How could I let that child be slain...{pp}Has my oath to Loslorien stained me so deeply!?
{np}These children fight better than our footsoldiers! Who are they!?
{np}Didn't expect a ragtag bunch of runts on a backwater island to put up an honest fight, eh?{pp}How could you? You think your night soil smells sweet as flowers.{pp}Well, you're wrong.
{np}I'll take your words as the challenge they are, "runt."{pp}Remorse will not haunt me when you lie bleeding at my feet.
{np}Sister? What's wrong?{pp}You're trembling. Are you ill? We should leave―
{np}No, I suffer no affliction...{pp}Only, when I think back on what happened this day...{pp}Even though I know we are not as we were then, it frightens me.
{np}Courage, Sister. We will not lose this fight.{pp}Think on why we are here.
{np}...You're right.{pp}We're not here to witness a tragedy.{pp}Thank you, {hero}. A word from you was all I needed.

{np}Ozma!? What are you doing here?
I thought you made for the south village.

{np}That's right... I was here, too. Leading my men, together with Oz.{pp}I remember him throwing his dagger after a fleeing girl, like a man playing at darts.{pp}How I trusted in him...in Tartaros and Balxephon.{pp}What a fool I was!
{np}Volaq! Andoras! Enough of this slaughter!{pp}Return to Phidoch!
{np}What are you saying, Ozma? We've received no such orders!
{np}There are no partisans here! This slaughter is senseless!{pp}Tartaros deceives us―his own commanders! I will not play a pawn in his game!
{np}What game? What are you talking about?{pp}Sorcery! Volaq, this is {pal 16}not{palreset} Ozma. A striking resemblance, for certain, but we are deceived! Fire!
{np}Vyce, away from here at once! You are not to die here!
{np}I hate it when you're right.
{np}Andoras, this does not go well! We withdraw!
{np}Hells, why had we not heard such forces were left on this island!?
{np}This changes nothing. They'll simply return with a greater army.{pp}We need to go farther back.
{np}{FF 9C 0101}{FF 8D 0102}{FF 85 0101}Golyat South Village ― Half Past Two{FF 99 01f1}
{np}Stunning. Simply stunning. Your eyes...enchant me!{pp}I would take you back to Lodis, and yet, I already have slaves to spare.{pp}You don't want to be a slave, do you?
{np}In Lodis, we possess the means to preserve a corpse as fresh as the day its soul departed.{pp}{FF 92}...I'll just take your head back with me.

{np}Would you stop, Oz?
I swear, sometimes you make me right ill.

{np}Don't interfere, Sister.
I'm just getting to the good part.
{np}Look, now you've made me waste a perfectly good trophy! The ichor must be injected while the heart still beats.
{np}Oz! There!
{np}Save the villagers first―and focus attacks on the Dark Knight captains!
{np}That's no local garrison...but I've not heard of any Almorican remnants in this town!
{np}Unlike Barbas, I dislike needless conflict.
{np}You fight well for provincial rabble!{pp}Or perhaps this is merely the eagerness of a first battle?{pp}Why risk your lives to save these swine hovels, anyway?

{np}You attack our homes, you attack our families―and you expect us {pal 16}not{palreset} to fight you with every measure of our strength!?{pp}I would ask you in turn: how can you take the lives of these people? They're not even soldiers!
{np}Look at this...{pp}People fleeing for their lives, corpses everywhere! Children, girls...
{np}Never seen a battle before, have you?
{np}Battle? No. This is a simple massacre. A slaughter.{pp}Does Loslorien require a certain degree of bloodthirst before they let you command?
{np}Ha! You expect such taunts to anger me, boy?{pp}...On second thought, why not? You besmirch Loslorien honor at your peril, fool of a wretch! I'll fillet you and cure the strips in the gutter!
{np}Oz! Enough of this mummery.{pp}One day you'll challenge a greater fool than yourself and pay the price.
{np}Your sister has all the wisdom in the family, it seems.{pp}And pretty much everything else worth having.
{np}I daresay the lout {pal 16}wants{palreset} me to kill him! Who am I to deny him?
{np}We are not all-powerful here. Our actions in this place will not alter {pal 16}our{palreset} past.{pp}But we can save lives, and I intend to save as many as I'm able!

{np}Oz...
I did not think I would ever meet you again.
{np}Eh? I've two sisters now? What sorcery is this?

{np}Lower your sword, Oz! There is no need for us to fight.{pp}I say this for your own benefit: leave Golyat at once.{pp}Take the abuna now, and you will lose your life one year hence.{pp}Make a different choice, and you may yet live to a ripe old age.
{np}Such prophecies sound far less dire when it's you saying them, Sister. Me, die in a year?
{np}Don't listen to her, Oz! She is not me!
{np}Begone from my sight, foul thing! Begone!

{np}I cannot say it will be easy cutting a woman, or fiend, or whatever you are, with the aspect of my own sister.{pp}But the thought of seeing that beautiful face twist with pain―ah, now {pal 16}that{palreset} stirs the blood!{pp}I wonder, will you cry with her voice? Oh, this could be more enjoyable than I imagined! And I imagine much...
{np}Oz, back to the van!{pp}We must reform our lines.
{np}Forced to retreat by children!? Bah! Shed a tear for Oz, ladies. He's fallen on hard times.

{np}We need to go further back.
We can't change history from here.
{np}{FF 9C 0101}{FF 8D 0102}{FF 85 0101}Golyat Sailors Way ― Quarter Past One{FF 99 01f1}

{np}Who're you lot!?
Spoiling for a fight, are we!?
{np}This man smells of swill. If you can call it a man!
{np}He's so deep in his cups he can't even see the black of our steel.
{np}I'll take a-a-all of you on! Send ya runnin' with a shiv in yer arse!
{np}V-Vyce?
{np}No, Vyce! They'll kill you!{pp}Run! To the church, run! Go!
{np}Who are they?{pp}Our reports said nothing of Almoricans garrisoned here.
{np}Sellswords, most like. Paid for protection.{pp}I welcome it. These civilians cut far too easily.
{np}I thought you'd say something of the sort, Barbas.
{np}They put up more of a fight than I expected! Now {pal 16}this{palreset} is battle!{pp}Hewing these burghers was about as challenging as chopping firewood.
{np}Talk your bold talk while you can.{pp}If you do not wish to suffer more losses, cease your attack and leave here at once!
{np}Who's bold, now? The child tastes blood once and fancies himself a great warrior!
{np}Let the child fancy what he wants, Barbas. I tire of keeping up with your headstrong lust for battle.
{np}You're lucky if you can hang onto my coattails, you simpering pansy.

{np}I've returned, Father...{pp}It must have been cold on the stone, in the falling snow... Not that you deserved more.{pp}I couldn't have picked a worse father...but my father you were.{pp}Now, you can watch me as I save Golyat.
{np}Vyce, are you all right?
{np}Far better than I imagined I would be.{pp}Though, I could live without those Dark Knights.
{np}I do not want you risking your life unnecessarily!
{np}You're unusually concerned for my health today, Catiua.
{np}I just don't want to see you running off, blood gone to your head―only to get it chopped off.{pp}There is much you must do in the days to come.
{np}I know, I know. I'm not so enthralled with myself as that.{pp}Though it is only me who can avenge my father now.{pp}I {pal 16}will{palreset} give those Dark Knights their due. Sooner or later.
{np}What are you doing here, Ozma? The operation's only just begun.

{np}I'm surprised to see so much pillaging already.{pp}By your orders, no doubt, Martym. I'm sure Barbas is otherwise occupied, fashioning a mountain from the slain.{pp}Simple bloodshed and rapine was ever the ultimate goal for both of you.
{np}We're here to find partisans―I know that much at least.{pp}What I don't know, because you've not answered me, is why you're here, Ozma.
{np}I came to kill two insufferably idiotic men before they could damage the reputation of Lodis even further!
{np}Blast! I'll not let these hedge knights drive me from the field!

{np}No, Barbas!
Our operation's only just begun!{pp}Think on it―there may be other forces lying in ambush. We must first report to Balxephon and the high commander!
{np}I've marked your face well!
{np}Further back... I remember the place!
{np}{FF 9C 0101}{FF 8D 0102}{FF 85 0101}Golyat North Village ― Stroke of Midnight{FF 99 01f1}
{np}Snow?
{np}Odd to see snowfall in these parts.{pp}I had heard the weather here was clement.
{np}With the chill setting in, there will be few on the streets.{pp}An excellent opportunity to ferret out these partisans!
{np}Why ferret, when we can smoke them out? Set fire to the place.
{np}What did you say?

{np}I said set fire to the town! We'll be here till morning if we have to search every house.{pp}The Bakram will be arriving at midday. Best to burn the place to the ground if we're going to be finished by then.
{np}But, that's...
{np}You begin to irritate me, Lord Windsalf. Take your men ahead to the rendezvous point!{pp}Now, go!
{np}Let's move, old man. I'll be behind, making sure you keep the pace.
{np}Yes, sir.
{np}Who are they? They're coming into town!
{np}{hero}, quickly. Find Vyce's father!
{np}I have to tell Father―come to the church as soon as you're able!
{np}You watch yourself, Sister.
{np}Hmm? Who was that?
{np}This is where it all started.{pp}I was here...and all I could do was watch, powerless, as they tore my life apart.{pp}But I'm not so powerless this time!
{np}It's all right. They're tough, but not so tough they won't crack.

{np}Not only do they stand their ground, but we're taking damage.{pp}How could the presence of a force this strong have been overlooked until now?{pp}Perplexing that their commander appears to be a youth―but more perplexing still is their ability...{pp}This could well shift the balance of power between the clans.{pp}Something is exceedingly odd about this...

{np}Looking at it now, it's obvious how unusual this whole thing was.{pp}I mean, seven officers of the Dark Knights, sent to attack a tiny port village?{pp}That's an awful lot of muscle to put toward something like this.{pp}Tartaros understood―he knew that Golyat was key to the Dark Knight's plans.{pp}And now we're here, right in the middle of it.{pp}We have to win.
{np}The Knights Loslorien attacked our town to find my father...no, to find me.{pp}The Wheel of Fortune began to turn for us here.{pp}And now we can change fate... We can save so many from death!

{np}{pal 16}Two{palreset} Ozmas?
What vile sorcery is this?
{np}I am Ozma of House Gladius in truth, but I am not the Ozma you know.{pp}I know everything, Balxephon. I know why you are here―and who you and the high commander truly are.

{np}Go on deceiving your companions, deceiving Lodis if you wish.{pp}But know that all will be revealed in due time.{pp}And when the other me standing there realizes the truth, she will surely turn her blade against you.
{np}A Holy Knight of Xenobia? Could he have followed us here?{pp}No, we would have heard something of this before now, surely!
{np}Dark Knight Lanselot! I did not expect to find you here, but I cannot say I am displeased.{pp}Your folly ends now!
{np}So it {pal 16}is{palreset} you!{pp}Our whisperers and farseers have been asleep at their posts, it seems!

{np}What is this?{pp}The Xenobian knight, a second Ozma... I refuse to believe they are mere conjurings!{pp}Could it be that they have ridden ahead of us upon the Wheel and seen our fated destination?{pp}That {pal 16}would{palreset} account for their knowledge...and strength.
{np}You... Hobyrim! What are you doing here!?
{np}Stopping your schemes, Balxephon!{pp}I will not permit you to claim innocent lives to satisfy base ambition!

{np}What I do, I do for Lodis!{pp}Clearly you fail to understand. Nor do you seem to value the life I gave you!{pp}Very well, I will finish what I started and put you out of your misery. It is the least I can do for my brother!
{np}I struck a devil's bargain with Lodis...

{np}High Commander, forgive me...
Glory to Lodis.
{np}How could I have underestimated them so gravely... I die of shame if not by my wounds!
{np}Feh! Just my luck to die in this backwater!
{np}How is it possible that these {pal 16}nobodies{palreset} have defeated me!?
{np}I underestimated my foe to my sorrow. Forgive me, High Commander, but I must retreat.

{np}I waste my blood on this lot...
Too much remains to be done.
{np}You're...not from this spoke on the Wheel...are you, boy.
{np}Father! Someone comes! They're here! We must flee!
{np}Hmm?
{np}No, I can handle this. You must wait inside.
{np}But, Father!
{np}Trust me, Son. I am in no danger.
{np}Welcome home, {hero}.
{np}You've put on some muscle. You look well. You look like...a man.
{np}All is done as you asked.{pp}My sister is queen of Valeria, and all those who wished Valeria harm have been driven from our shores.
{np}That is good news.
{np}Father, I'm sorry...I...I could not save you.{pp}But I did all you asked, for you. I did all I could.

{np}Then you have done well, {hero}.{pp}But you did not do it for me.
You have your own aspirations now.{pp}Follow them.
They do me proud.
{np}Father, all is done.
{np}You really leaving, {hero}?
{np}If I stay on this island, I'll only be in my sister's way.
{np}In my way? Not at all!
{np}As long as there are people who consider my presence as a count against the queen, I'd best remain absent.
{np}Those blasted nobles sprang up like toadstools after a shower when the war ended.
{np}Besides, I made a promise to Sir Lanselot and Canopus that I would visit them in Xenobia.{pp}But I will return to Valeria and put what I learn abroad to good use.

{np}I understand, {hero}.
I will await your return. As long as it takes, I will wait.
{np}Leave the protection of the queen to me then. I'll guard her with my life.
{np}Well, Vyce. How noble!
{np}Don't jest, Catiua. You know I've always looked out for you.
{np}It's a relief to know you're in good hands. I was never worried.
{np}As well you shouldn't be. I'm more concerned about living up to our parents' expectations.
{np}Go, {hero}. Learn. And bring back lots of stories to tell over our cups.
{np}Aye, that I will. I look forward to telling you much.
{np}So, what's after your coronation, Sister? A wedding, perhaps?
{np}Mmm, yes. Very important for the monarch to have a family. Lends stability to the land.
{np}Stop that, the both of you! I'll keep my own counsel on that matter, thank you very much.

A {if 02}formerly living {/if}knight of the Dark Knights Loslorien, an elite specially trained in the skills of a Beast Tamer.
A {if 02}formerly living {/if}knight of the Dark Knights Loslorien, an elite specially trained in the skills of a Warlock.
A {if 02}formerly living {/if}knight of the Dark Knights Loslorien, an elite specially trained in the skills of a Necromancer.
Summoner
Strega
A magic-user whose command of a wide range of spells dwarfs the knowledge of a common wizard. Able to use their power without worshipping or forging a pact with any gods, demons, or spirits.
Assassin
A killer-of-men for hire, will use any means at their disposal to claim their mark.
False Hierophant
A fallen exarch who chose power over faith, attaining their rank by use of improper means.
Fleeing Villager
A villager of Golyat, fleeing before the sudden attack of the Dark Knights and the Bakram.
Vasque Survivor
One of the people driven from their village during Hierophant Balbatos's blood war. Many lay hidden in Lhazan Fortress following the Bakram invasion.
Hanged Man
This corpse of a man hanged for collaborating with the Bakram was animated by a dark necromancer.
The spirit of a dead sailor lingering in the depths of the Pirate's Graveyard. As long as they still yearn for something of their former lives, they will never be free.
Gladiator
A former swordmaster, skilled with the blade. Now fallen to killing men for a pittance of goth.
Deadeye
A dedicated assassin who revels in the taking of life.
Arcanist
A dark mage that offered their very essence in exchange for limitless knowledge.
Apostate
A fallen priest―an apostate who uses divine magic for personal gain.
Hexblade
A mystic warrior fallen from grace, adept at infusing their blade with dark essence.
Blackguard
A knight who attained immortality through a pact with a demon. No light of reason shines in its eyes, only a lust for bloodshed.
Dreadnought
Ungodly means were used to fetch the soul of this knight from the Abyss who now animates this suit of armor.
Marauder
A savage raider that revels in removing heads from their bodies.
Sellsword
A born killer who thinks of taking lives as nothing more than a game.
Slayer
An insane hunter of man or beast that kills not for honor, glory or gold. They live but for the sheer enjoyment of spilling blood.
Stalker
A dweller in darkness, fed on the blood of the Abyss.
Outlaw
A bandit skilled in inflicting so much pain, death feels like an afterthought.
Sniper
Snipers never hesitate to pull the trigger of their fusil on a man. In fact, they rather enjoy it.
Cannibal
A savage master of dragon and beast who craves human flesh, often joining their pets in their gruesome feast.
Dragonlord
An evil magus, conversant in all forms of spellcraft. Has the peculiar habit of taking men's skins to use as covers for spellbooks.
Occultist
Occultist
A vile master of the dead, inspiring in equal parts fear and respect.
Raven
A dark winged creature, sometimes called the "Angel of Death." A raven rises when the Dark touches the corpse of a man who has passed on, having committed all seven deadly sins.
Overlord
Overlord
A ruler of the underworld, wielding power without limits.
Nephalem
The unearthly beauty of this winged stands in stark contrast to its brutally violent nature.
Nightwing
An ebon winged who fell onto the paths of darkness, the night crow will not cease battle until it has drawn blood.
Raptor
A variety of lizardman with blood-red skin. Its violence is remarkable, even toward its own kind.
Gorgon
A wielder of ancient magic with a gaze that can turn those who draw too near to stone. Of the many tribes of gorgon, the Medusa, Stheno, and Euryale tribes are most famous.
Uruk
Dark magic created this orc-human crossbreed. Superior in both strength and intellect to its forebears.
Draug
A skeletal warrior and wielder of magic, fetched from the Abyss by means of necromancy.
Wraith
A spirit warrior and wielder of powerful magic, fetched from the Abyss by means of necromancy.
Cherub
Cherub
A corrupted servant of the Divine, its once merely mischievous nature twisted into committing acts of horrible cruelty and suffering.
Incubus
Succubus
This nightmare flits nimbly through the air to dodge attacks. Also a wielder of powerful magic.
Scarecrow
Boggart
This horrific creature lurched into life when the Dark settled upon a rotting pumpkin-headed scarecrow.
Bjartskular

This dragon is named for the translucence of its steely scales. The material of its scales is second only to diamond in hardness, and the slight imperfections in its hide catch the light and sparkle like rubies and sapphires, adding to the ancient dragon's breathtaking appearance.
Deathwyrm
Ebon scales cover the sinuous form of this wyrm of darkness. So dark are its scales that they absorb not only light, but the very will of men to fight.
Scylla
A dragon with many heads, spending much of its time in the water. Often takes the form of a beautiful woman to lure travellers to a watery grave.
Naga
Sometimes worshipped as a serpent god, the naga is nothing more than a vile, bloodthirsty monster intent on taking human life.
Damasc Golem
A golem fashioned of damasc steel, the hardest variety of steel known to man. Immune to most melee attacks.
Flesh Golem
Some fiendish mage patched this golem together from a jumble of leftover body parts. Its bulbous form boils with hatred toward the living.
Hippogryph
A horse with the head of an eagle and giant wings. Able to fly with ease over rough terrain and changing elevations.
Phoenix
The fabled immortal bird. Though legend says that any who drink the phoenix's blood will gain its immortality, this is likely just a myth.
Rukh
A giant demon-bird. It's said that the demons rode upon these during the Ogre Battle.
Basilisk
A serpentine desert-dweller with a gaze that can turn men to stone. When facing a basilisk, bring a shield, or don't come at all.
Kraken
A dweller of the deep, the kraken can control water and summon squalls at will.
An aquatic giant, the "Demon of the Sea." Can summon a great tempest to sweep its foes to the depths of the ocean.
Balor
A one-eyed giant, adept in the use of elemental magic, just in case its inhuman strength isn't enough to do the job.
Titan
Member of an ancient race of giants. Sees out of only one eye, the other having been taken as punishment for turning against the gods.
Deva
An avatar of Vija, said to be the most martially adept of the Twelve Heavenly Generals.
Icon
An avatar of the Heavenly General Enja, punisher of men's crimes.
Deva
An avatar of the Heavenly General Maitreya, who extends the hand of salvation to deserving mortals.
Deva
An avatar of the Heavenly General Ijana, who staves off disease and calamity.
Deva
An avatar of the Heavenly General Chandra, who borrows the power of the moon in battle.
An avatar of Vayu, said to be the wisest of the Twelve Heavenly Generals.
An avatar of the Heavenly General Indra, who crushes the desires of mortals.
An avatar of the Heavenly General Rakshas, who brings destruction and devastation to this world.
An avatar of Ahurama, known as an ogre among the Twelve Heavenly Generals.
An avatar of the Heavenly General Asurama, the great revealer, who protects and preserves the teachings of the gods.
An avatar of the Heavenly General Aditi, said to be a scourge upon mankind.
An avatar of the Heavenly General Saranga, said to have shot a great demon with its bow.
Lampada
A guardian of the temple of Ashmedai. A normal person in appearance, her true form is shrouded in mystery.
Ascendant
A guardian of the temple of Ashmedai. It is unclear whether Blackmoor was once a human who reincarnated, or was a lich from the very beginning. His true form is shrouded in mystery.
Erinys

A monster, called the Sea Witch. Many are the men who have lost their lives at the bottom of the sea, lured into calamity by the dulcet tones of her voice. She feeds upon the souls of the men she kills.
Anima
The bird that pulls Hahnela's chariot across the sky. Worshipped as a divinity who calls the strong winds that usher in the spring.
A beastman said to have been created by Vaasa, Goddess of Earth, to serve her in eternity. Called the "Ravager" for his violence, Vaasa uses him for a watchdog.
Anima

The stormbeast, survived from the days of the Ogre Battle. Once a scourge upon mankind, Xolotl was captured by heroes who had received the protection of Nestharot, Goddess of Lightning. Now he serves as her temple guardian.

Said to have been born from the tears Greuza, Goddess of Water, shed for her lost son, Tlaloc has been called a god of rain and of disasters. When the great winds blow, and the floods come, people say it is the work of Tlaloc.
Anima

A creature of fire and a powerful elemental. Ifrit once wreaked havoc among the villages and towns of man, until Xoshonell, Goddess of Fire, caught him and trapped him within an urn. After many centuries, Ifrit repented, and now serves as Xoshonell's temple guardian.
Anima
A chimera with the body of a bird, shell of a turtle, and tail of a snake. It is said that Lyuneram, Goddess of Ice, turned a cruel king into this creature as punishment.
